title: feat(vtc-mcp): several communities from one --listen bridge (--communities)
body:
## What

`vtc-mcp --listen <addr> --communities <file>` bridges every community a TOML file names from one process, each at `/mcp/<name>` as its own identity, policy, audit log and wallet sign-in. Only the port and the bearer token are shared; nothing is served at `/mcp`.

```toml
[community.first-vtc]
vtc_did        = "did:webvh:…:vtc.example.com"
agent_key_file = "keys/first-vtc.json"   # owner-only; the --mint-did-key JSON
confirm        = "sensitive"
audit_log      = "first-vtc-audit.jsonl"

[community.acme]
vtc_did            = "did:webvh:…:acme.example"
agent_secrets_file = "~/.config/vtc-mcp/acme-persona.json"
read_only          = true
```

## Why a path per community, not a `community` argument

Design note D7a. Each MCP server a host sees stays one identity at one community: a host's approval of one server's tools is never an approval at another, one guard never answers for several communities, and the tools, prompts, workflows and skill are unchanged. Each path has its own MCP session manager, so a session from one community's endpoint is refused at another's.

## Rules

- **Fatal (policy):** unreadable file, unknown key (`deny_unknown_fields`), bad name, bad confirm level / transport, audit log that cannot be opened, **one agent DID for two communities** (VTI-KEY-005, VTI-KEY-006 — the reuse note warns for a single bridge; a file naming both can refuse).
- **Degrades one community (identity):** key file missing, unparseable, readable by others, or not the `agent_did` beside it.
- Key material never in the TOML; the DID is derived from the key.
- Policy flags beside `--communities` are defaults; a section's `deny` adds to `--deny`, never lifts it. `--vtc-did`, `--vtc-url`, identity flags and `--audit-log` are refused beside it; `--communities` requires `--listen`.
- Communities connect concurrently; log lines and `vtc_status` / `vtc_whoami` carry the community name.
- stdio and single-community `--listen` unchanged; `vti_mcp_common::listen::{router, serve}` keep their signatures, so `vta-mcp` is untouched.

## Changes

- `vti-mcp-common/src/listen.rs`: `router_many`, `serve_many`, `mcp_path_for`, `check_service_name`
- `vtc-mcp/src/communities.rs` (new): the file loader
- `vtc-mcp/src/main.rs`: one `open()` per community, shared by both paths; `--communities`
- `vtc-mcp/src/server.rs`: `BridgeIdentity.community`, in status and call logs
- Docs: operator page §7.2, design note D7a + rollout row 9, crate `CLAUDE.md`

## Testing

- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-mcp -p vti-mcp-common -p vta-mcp`: 111 passed, including two communities on one port each reporting its own identity and policy, path isolation and cross-session refusal in `vti-mcp-common`, and the loader's fatal / degraded split
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-mcp -p vti-mcp-common -p vta-mcp --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, `scripts/check-docs.py`: clean
- Binary smoke test with two unreachable communities: `/mcp/alpha` and `/mcp/beta` answer `initialize` 200, `/mcp` 404, both degrade independently, a shared key and a conflicting flag are refused, clean shutdown
- Not yet run: the full workspace suite; a live community (migrating the author's own bridge next)

title: feat(vtc-service): serve vtc/storage/credentials/recipient/0.1 so the console seals for any DID method
body:
The admin console couldn't seal a storage credential for a **did:webs** community. A **did:webvh** community on a DID host had the same problem. The console read the community key only from the same-origin `/.well-known/did.jsonl`, which neither of them serves.

The VTC now serves **`vtc/storage/credentials/recipient/0.1`** (spec trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1329, pinned in `vti-specs-vtc`), and the console asks it for the key instead of reading the log.

**Community (`trust_tasks::storage_tasks`)**
- **Authority:** requires `vtc.rooms.admin` (item 1).
- **Answer:** the Ed25519 key `SealedCredentials` opens with, as a `did:key`, and the verification method that publishes it (item 2).
- **Rotation check:** when its own DID resolves, the answer is checked against the document. If the document publishes a different signing key, it refuses with `notPublished` (`retryable: true`) and carries no key (item 3). If its DID doesn't resolve within 5 s, it answers from the key it holds, as item 3 allows.

**Console (`admin-ui/src/lib/sealed-transfer.ts`)**
- Accepts the answer only when it names the community's own DID and a verification method under that DID (item 4), then seals to `recipientKey` (item 5).
- A `notPublished` refusal is shown as the reason, with the `cnm` command beside it. Other refusals pass through unchanged.

**SDK and `cnm`**
- New `vta_sdk::node_keys::ed25519_public_key` reads a verification method's Ed25519 key as multibase or as an OKP JWK, which is how a did:webs publishes keys (VTI-KEY-150).
- `cnm storage credentials set` now uses that function in place of its own copy. It still seals from its own resolution, as item 6 allows.

**Registered with the censuses:** conformance witness, error-code witness, `DISPATCHED_WITHOUT_PROOF` entry with the reason, admin-UI manifest, MCP guard verb (`recipient` counts as a read), OpenAPI wrapper with a regenerated snapshot and `wire.ts`.

**Tests**
- New in `room_storage_auth.rs`: a did:webs community resolving to a JWK key answers with the key it opens with; a document publishing another key gets `notPublished`; an unresolvable DID gets an answer from the community's own record; a stranger gets `permissionDenied`.
- `vta-sdk`: reads the key from both multibase and JWK.
- Console: vitest for the new key path, plus the updated Storage page test.

**Local runs**
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: full suite run before the final fixes (6 failures: four censuses and two of the new tests). After the fixes I re-ran only the affected subset (the new tests, census, conformance, spine-proof): 48 passed.
- Workspace nextest excluding the VTC: 7595 of 7596 passed. The one failure was the MCP guard census; after adding the verb, `-p vti-mcp-common` passes.
- Clippy with `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `scripts/check-docs.py` pass. Doctests ran only for `vta-sdk` and `cnm-cli`.
- Console: all 1,623 vitest tests, `tsc`, and `wire:check`.

title: feat(vta)!: every DID the VTA holds through one method-neutral surface (vta/dids/*)
body:
Implements `docs/05-design-notes/did-management.md` (#2761) against the specifications in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1332 (merged, deployed). Also fixes the reported bug **`pnm contexts delete` ignores the context's did:webs DIDs and leaves them published**.

## The problem

Every "which DIDs does this agent hold" question was asked one method at a time, and every caller asked only the methods it knew. Against a VTA whose identities were all did:webs, `pnm did-mgmt dids list` said *No WebVH DIDs found* and the wallet's pickers were empty. Inside the VTA the methods had drifted on rules that are not about the method at all.

## What changes

**Engines** (`operations/dids`). One `DidEngine` per kind of authority: the webvh log engine (did:webvh and its did:scid:vh:1 form), the KERI engine (did:webs), and the key engine (did:key identities this VTA minted, read from their key records). One listing, get and methods answer sit over them.

**Wire**
- Serves `vta/dids/{list,get,methods/list}/0.1`. Retires `vta/webvh/dids/list/1.0` and `vta/webs/dids/list/0.1`.
- `vta/contexts/update-did/1.2`: a string DID must be an identity this VTA holds in that context (`notHeld`), of a class that may be its identity (`didClassConflict`, VTI-KEY-193).
- `vta/contexts/delete/1.2` and `preview-delete/2.0` fix the reported bug:
  - **Preview**: `dids` lists every method's DIDs, so the confirmation names the did:webs.
  - **NotEmpty**: counts them.
  - **Deletion**: ends each did:webs on its host through the same path `vta/webs/dids/delete` takes (`ContextWebsSettler`): the deactivation is published, then the slot removed. Host copies are settled before anything local goes, under the same `hostCleanupFailed` / `abandonHostCopies` rules did:webvh has. An unconfirmed did:webs refuses the deletion or is reported in `daemonCleanupErrors`; it is never dropped unseen.
  - **Spec**: 1.1 named did:webvh only, while forbidding exactly this outcome for did:webvh. 1.2 makes it method-neutral rather than this being a code-only fix.
  - **Offline**: the break-glass `vta contexts delete` has no hosting client, so it reports each did:webs as an unconfirmed copy instead of silently purging it.

**One rule each where the methods had drifted**
- **webvh create**: no longer repoints the context holding this VTA's own identity. A did:webs create always refused this.
- **webvh get, realign and delete**: answer NotFound for an unreachable DID, as their specifications already declared. They answered Forbidden, which confirms the DID exists.
- **webs delete**: refuses a DID that a context still acts as, as webvh delete does.
- **Host reconcile and retire-orphan**: now see did:webs slots. They read them as host-only orphans, which retire-orphan could remove.
- **KeyMint refusal**: names DID creation, not `webvh/dids/create`.

**SDK and CLIs**
- **vta-sdk** `client/dids.rs`: `list_dids` (reads to the end), `get_did`, `did_methods`. `list_dids_webvh` and `list_dids_webs` are removed.
- **pnm `did-mgmt dids list` / `get`**: method-neutral, with a `--method` filter.
- **pnm `did-mgmt dids methods`**: new.
- **pnm `webs list`**: the same listing, narrowed to did:webs.
- **pnm address book and server-delete dependents**: read every method.

## Breaking

- The retired list tasks are gone.
- `DeleteContextPreviewResultBody.webvh_dids` is now `dids`.
- Context tasks move to update-did 1.2, delete 1.2 and preview-delete 2.0.

Nothing is deployed, so the wallet (OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin) cuts over with this release.

## Known remaining path

`vta/contexts/update/1.0` (super-admin) can still set a context's `did` unchecked. `update-did/1.2` is where the check lives; the mock-VTA blocker test now creates its "outside context acts as this DID" state through that path, because such records still exist. Closing it needs `contexts/update` to drop `did` in a new version, which belongs in its own change.

## Tests

- **Engines**: did:key from its own record only; context reach (absent and unreachable answer alike); a no-context identity for unrestricted callers only; every engine in one sorted listing; filters; `context_dids`; `for_did`; the class guard.
- **did:webs end to end**:
  - summarised beside other methods, and not found from another context;
  - **context delete ends it and removes its slot**, with the preview naming it and NotEmpty counting it;
  - a refusing host holds the deletion unless the copy is abandoned, and then it is reported;
  - a persona DID cannot become a node-identity context's DID (`didClassConflict`).
- **`update-did` `notHeld`**: for an unknown DID and for one held in another context.
- **Reconcile**: a did:webs slot is held.
- **Conformance**: witnesses for the new tasks, with summaries built by the engines.

`cargo test --workspace` passes, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

Release notes

Banyan

Coordinated OpenVTC release Banyan — a known-good, cross-project snapshot of all OpenVTC projects. Tagged at the main-branch HEAD on 2026-06-23.

Changelog

Sourced from dtg-credentials's changelog.

[0.14.0] - 2026-11-10

Breaking: a VAC states purposes of use (DTG Core Credentials, context v2), and verify_chain holds a chain to them — see Changed (breaking) below.

Added

  • A VAC states purposes of use (DTG Core Credentials, Purposes of Use; trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#84). credentialSubject.purposes is optional, {"scope":"any"} or {"scope":"listed","purposes":[...]} with a non-empty list of registered names or absolute IRIs, each once; absent means any, and any never grants modelTraining. dtg_credentials::purposes::PurposeScope models it, read strictly (an any carrying purposes, an empty list or a duplicate is refused at parse). A VAC stating it lists DTG_CONTEXT_V2 (https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v2) second, which is now recognized beside v1; a VAC stating it under v1 is refused.
  • verify_chain enforces the chain rule and reports the effective purposes. A link stating none takes its parent's; a link stating purposes its parent does not grant is AuthorityError::WidensPurposes. The root states the grant, so only a root naming modelTraining can pass it on. VerifiedAuthority::purposes carries the result.
  • DTGCredential::with_purposes states them (switching the context to v2), and with_purposes_under refuses at issue purposes wider than those the parent states.

Changed (breaking)

  • CredentialSubjectAuthority gains purposes, VerifiedAuthority gains purposes, and AuthorityError gains WidensPurposes; DTGCredentialError gains InvalidPurposes (non-exhaustive).

  • did:scid parties are matched by their DID. Chain verification (verify_chain, delegation chains) and the acknowledgement/acceptance pairing compare an issuer, subject, presenter, governing party or principal by DID, ignoring a did:scid ?src= locator (VTI-KEY-160): did:scid:vh:1:<scid>?src=a.example and did:scid:vh:1:<scid> are one party. A did:scid and its did:webvh log are still two. Every other DID compares as before. A proof's verificationMethod is still bound to its issuer exactly.

  • Depends on affinidi-did-common directly (already in the graph through affinidi-data-integrity).

Security

  • DTGCredential::verify_proof_with_public_key now refuses a proof that was not made by a key of the credential's issuer. It verified the signature under the key it was handed but never checked that the proof's verificationMethod belongs to issuer, so a caller that resolved the method the proof names and then trusted issuer() accepted a credential naming any issuer, signed by anyone. It now returns DTGCredentialError::ProofNotFromIssuer, as verify_grant_with_public_key already did; the two share one check. A method belongs to the issuer when the DID before its # is exactly the issuer, when it is the issuer itself, or when it is a bare #fragment (read against the issuer — verify_grant_with_public_key previously refused that form). The comparison is verbatim. A caller signing with a key whose id is not a method of the issuer will now see its own credentials refused; give the signing secret the issuer's method id.

title: ci: compare PR checks with the merge commit's base, not the stale pull_request.base.sha
body:
`github.event.pull_request.base.sha` stays at the commit a PR branched from. The jobs, however, check out GitHub's merge commit, which contains the *current* base. Once a Release PR merges, every open PR that predates it is blamed for that release's version bumps. #1324 failed **versions change only in the Release PR** with 12 `version changed` errors, from #1321 and #1326, although it changes no version.

All seven uses of `base.sha` (version edits, spec lifecycle, published schemas, and the Rust/TS/Go/Dart API-compat jobs) now use `HEAD^1`, the base the merge commit was built on. Every job already checks out with `fetch-depth: 0` and on the merge commit.

**Checked locally** by merging #1324 onto main and running the scripts:
- `VERSION_BASE_REF=e9d913cad` (the old `base.sha`) reproduces the 12 errors.
- `VERSION_BASE_REF=HEAD^1`: `No version declaration changed`.
- With `HEAD^1`, `check-published-schemas` and `check-spec-lifecycle` also pass.

The API-compat jobs use `BASE_REF` only for the `<last tag>..BASE_REF` history and a `git diff BASE_REF HEAD`. `HEAD^1` is the more accurate value there too, and I haven't exercised those jobs end to end.

title: feat(vtc/storage/credentials/recipient): add vtc/storage/credentials/recipient/0.1
body:
Adds **`vtc/storage/credentials/recipient/0.1`**. It returns the key that a [`vtc/storage/credentials/set`](specs/vtc/storage/credentials/set/0.3/spec.md) sealed block is sealed to: the Ed25519 key the community opens with, as a `did:key`, plus the absolute ID of the verification method that publishes it in the community's DID document.

**Why:** a client that can't resolve and verify the community's DID has no way to seal a credential to it. The VTI admin console runs in a browser and reads the community key only from the same-origin `/.well-known/did.jsonl`:
- a did:webs community never serves that file, so the console fails every time;
- for a hosted did:webvh, the console would have to fetch and verify a log from another origin;
- for a did:webs, it would have to verify a KERI event stream.

With this task the key comes over the same authenticated channel the credential then travels on, and it works the same for every DID method.

**What the spec requires:**
- `vtc.rooms.admin`, the same authority `credentials/set` requires.
- The community returns only the key it actually opens with.
- `notPublished` (retryable) when that key is no longer the signing key its document publishes, so nothing gets sealed to a key that has rotated away.
- The client accepts the answer only from the community it addressed, and seals only to `recipientKey`.
- A client that resolves the DID itself may seal from its own resolution. It should refuse to seal if this task's answer names a different key.

Also changes `credentials/set/0.3`, prose only: the sealed-block definition and the `related` list now point to the new task.

Bindings were regenerated for all four libraries. `npm run check` passes, and the Rust conformance tests for the new module pass.

Consumer: VTI (the VTC serves the task; the admin console and `cnm` use it).

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.40.4
body:
### Added

- **vta/dids**: List, get and methods for every identity a VTA holds; method-neutral context deletion ([#1332](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1332))

A VTA holds identities of several methods, and the only way to ask which
  was once per method: vta/webvh/dids/list, vta/webs/dids/list. Every client
  asked only the methods it knew about, so a VTA whose identities were all
  did:webs reported none, and a new method would add a question to every
  client.

  - vta/dids/_shared/0.2: CONVENTIONS §20 (every identity: which are
    summarised, who sees what, the summary, methods), DidSummary and
    MethodInfo, a did:key profile, and a Summary details heading in each
    profile. §3.1's level-1 refusal is scoped to the key-role tasks.
  - vta/dids/list/0.1, get/0.1, methods/list/0.1.
  - vta/contexts/update-did/1.2: the DID must be one the VTA holds in that
    context (notHeld), and its class may be the context's (didClassConflict).
  - vta/contexts/delete/1.2: every DID in the subtree is deleted as its
    method's delete task deletes it, host work settled first. 1.1 named
    did:webvh only, so a did:webs record was removed while its key event log
    stayed published as a live identity.
  - vta/contexts/preview-delete/2.0: `dids` (every method) replaces
    `webvhDids`, which left did:webs out of the confirmation.
  - vta/webvh/dids/list/1.0 and vta/webs/dids/list/0.1 retired in favour of
    vta/dids/list/0.1.

  Bindings regenerated for all four languages.

- **vtc/storage/credentials/recipient**: Add vtc/storage/credentials/recipient/0.1 ([#1329](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1329))

A room-hosting administrator's client asks the community for the key a
  vtc/storage/credentials/set sealed block is sealed to: the Ed25519 key it
  opens with, as its did:key, and the verification method in its DID
  document that publishes it.

  A client that cannot resolve and verify the community's DID could not
  seal at all. A browser console reading a did:webs would need KERI
  verification, and a hosted did:webvh would need a log from another
  origin. The VTC console read only the same-origin did.jsonl, which a
  did:webs community never serves. The answer comes over the same
  authenticated channel the credential then goes over, and is the same
  for every DID method. `notPublished` covers a key the community's
  document no longer lists, so nothing is sealed past a rotation.

  credentials/set 0.3's sealed-block definition and `related` now point
  at it (prose only).

title: feat!: list every DID the agent holds, whatever its method (vta/dids/*)
body:
Against an agent whose identities were all did:webs, every DID question in this wallet came back empty: the vault's persona picker (*Context "vta" has no DIDs*), the console's DIDs pane, and every offscreen lookup. Each asked `vta/webvh/dids/list`, which answers for did:webvh only. A stopgap that also asked the webs list would have needed a third question for a third method, so this uses the method-neutral family instead. Design: VTI `docs/05-design-notes/did-management.md`. Spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1332 (merged). Agent side: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2763.

## Changes

- **core** — `vta/dids.ts`:
  - `didsList`, read to the end of its cursor through `collectPages`, plus `didsGet` and `didMethodsList`, typed on `TaskParty`.
  - `vtaListDids` and `webvhDidList` are gone with the retired tasks.
  - Admin `contextPreviewDelete` returns 2.0's `dids` (every method).
- **Pins**:
  - Added: `vta/dids/{list,get,methods/list}/0.1`.
  - Moved: `vta/contexts/update-did` 1.2, `delete` 1.2, `preview-delete` 2.0.
  - Unpinned: `vta/webvh/dids/list`.
- **Offscreen lookups** list through `didsList`: elections, directory, sign-in personas, `bindProfile`, the community identity check and the vault picker.
- **Vault form**: takes the agent's own `signingKeyId` from the summary rather than resolving the DID document. For a did:webs, a verification-method id is not the agent's key id, so a did:webs persona entry now names a key the agent can sign with.
- **Console**:
  - **DIDs pane**: one table with a Method column. A did:webvh row keeps its log, realign and delete; a did:webs or did:key row opens a read-only summary.
  - **Pickers**: the contexts, persona and room pickers list every method.
  - **Room signing key**: matched by the summary's `signingKeyId` as well as the `did#` prefix, which a did:webs key id does not carry.
  - **Context-deletion preview**: names every method's DIDs.
- **CLAUDE.md**: new section, *DIDs are listed method-neutrally*.
- **task-surface.json**: resynced from the vta-sdk on #2763; coverage 245 → 247.

## Breaking

The wallet speaks `vta/dids/*`, `contexts/update-did` 1.2, `delete` 1.2 and `preview-delete` 2.0, which the VTA serves from #2763. Nothing is deployed, so the two cut over together.

## Tests

- **core**: `vta.dids.mjs` covers the filters and their schema spelling, a did:webs coming back beside other methods, paging to the end, and get/methods unwrapping.
- **Render tests** now answer `vta/dids/list` (harness `asSummary`), with new cases:
  - one DIDs table drawing webvh, webs and key rows, with only the webvh row offering webvh actions;
  - the persona picker offering a did:webs.
- `npm test` and `npm run build` (bundle guards) pass.

title: chore(deps)!: take vta-sdk 0.74, affinidi-tdk 0.33, messaging-sdk 0.41, trust-tasks 0.35 and trql-client 0.29; release 0.26.0
body:
Moves VGI onto the VTI #2300 line so openvtc (OpenVTC/openvtc#512) keeps a single `vta-sdk`: `vta-sdk` 0.74, `affinidi-tdk` 0.33, `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.41, `trust-tasks-rs`/`-proof` 0.35, `trql-client` 0.29, and test mediator 0.46. The workspace and its internal pins go to **0.26.0**, as do `bridge.example.toml` and the tag `v0.26.0`.

## ⚠️ Draft: waiting on trql-client 0.29

`trql-client` 0.29 comes from affinidi/affinidi-trust-registry-rs#172 and the registry release after it, and isn't on crates.io yet. **`Cargo.lock` isn't updated in this commit**, because it can't resolve until then. Once 0.29 is published I'll run `cargo update`, commit the lockfile, and mark this ready.

## Changes

- **Registry test fakes answer `registry/authorization/0.2`.** trql-client 0.29 asks at 0.2 (lowerCamelCase: `entityId`, `authorityId`, `evaluatedAt`) first and falls back to 0.1 only on `unsupportedVersion`. The fakes in verify-trust and vgi-bridge answered 0.1 snake_case, which 0.29 refuses as a contract violation. That caused 4 verify-trust test failures before this change.
- **`#[allow(deprecated)]` for trust-tasks-rs 0.35's prebuilt spec modules.** vgi-bridge allows it at crate level, plus three test files. Its `git-ns/bridge/{job,result,event}` types come from those modules. In did-git-sign it covers `print_session_health`, because vta-sdk's `health/details` answer comes from them too. The real fix is generating those types with `trust-tasks-build`, as openvtc now does. That's a follow-up; this PR is a dependency move.

## Checks

These were run against the registry branch, patched in through an untracked `.cargo/config.toml`:

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features`: 842 pass, 0 fail.
- `cargo fmt --check` passes.
- `cargo tree` has one copy each of `vta-sdk`, `trust-tasks-rs`, `affinidi-tdk` and `affinidi-messaging-sdk`.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no client change
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1)
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4)
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6)
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): registry queries go out as 0.2 via trql-client 0.29; fakes updated
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*)
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: `allow(deprecated)` above, until generated specs

title: feat(vta/dids): list, get and methods for every identity a VTA holds; method-neutral context deletion
body:
## Why

A VTA holds identities of several methods, and the only way to ask which was once per method: `vta/webvh/dids/list`, `vta/webs/dids/list`. Every client asked only the methods it knew, so a VTA whose identities were all did:webs reported none (the wallet's persona picker, its console, `pnm did-mgmt dids list`), and each new method would add a question to every client. Design note: VTI `docs/05-design-notes/did-management.md`.

## What

- **`vta/dids/_shared/0.2`** — CONVENTIONS §20 (*Every identity: list, get and methods*): which identities are summarised (every one the VTA holds a record of, any level, including the did:key identities it minted; not did:peer, which it keeps no record of), who sees what (context access per identity; unreachable answers as absent), the `DidSummary` record, and `methods/list`. §3.1's level-1 refusal is scoped to the key-role tasks. §18 adds a tenth profile heading, *Summary details*, defining each method's `methodDetails` member, so a method is added by a profile, never by a schema change. New `key.md` profile (ineligible for key roles; exists for §20). `did-summary.schema.json`: `DidSummary`, `MethodInfo`, `DidClass`.
- **`vta/dids/list/0.1`**, **`get/0.1`**, **`methods/list/0.1`**.
- **`vta/contexts/update-did/1.2`** — the DID must be one the VTA holds in that context (`notHeld`), of a class that may be its identity (`didClassConflict`, VTI-KEY-193). 1.1 stored any syntactically valid DID.
- **`vta/contexts/delete/1.2`** — every DID in the subtree is deleted as its own method's delete task deletes it, host work settled first under the same `hostCleanupFailed` / `abandonHostCopies` rules. 1.1 named did:webvh only, so a did:webs record was dropped while its key event log stayed published as a live identity — the outcome 1.1 itself forbids for did:webvh ("removing only the consumer's own record of a DID is not a deletion of it").
- **`vta/contexts/preview-delete/2.0`** — `dids` (every method) replaces `webvhDids`, which left did:webs out of the confirmation an operator was shown.
- **Retired** `vta/webvh/dids/list/1.0` and `vta/webs/dids/list/0.1` → `vta/dids/list/0.1`.

Bindings regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart. `npm run build`, `npm run check` and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --all-targets` pass locally.

Implementations: VTI (VTA, vta-sdk, pnm) and pnm-browser-plugin, cut over together.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
author: stormer78

title: fix(console)!: speak acl 0.3 — every grant states what its subject may use reads for
body:
The VTA serves `acl/{grant,show,update,change-role,revoke}` 0.3 and `acl/list` 0.4 only (AclEntry 0.3), so the console's access pane was refused on every write and read against a current agent. Found while refreshing `task-surface.json`, whose census flagged all five 0.2 URIs as no longer in vta-sdk.

AclEntry 0.3 makes `purposes` **REQUIRED** (VTI-ACL-100 – 110): what the subject may use content it reads for — `{scope: "any"}` (any purpose except model training) or a listed set.

- **The grant form asks, with no default.** Choosing `any` on the operator's behalf would widen every grant nobody thought about. *Only these purposes* with nothing listed is not an answer either: an empty list is malformed, not `any`. *Grant access* stays disabled until there is one.
- **The access table shows each entry's purposes**, and draws an absent one as *not stated*, never as `any` — the spec is explicit that reading absence as `any` reads a narrowed entry as wider than it is.
- Updates send only the members that change, so an existing entry's purposes are untouched by them.

Pins moved; generated modules regenerated; `task-surface.json` resynced from vta-sdk 0.90.0. Tests: `no grant is sent until its purposes are answered`, `purposesFrom reads no answer as none, never as any`, and the existing grant tests now pin `purposes` on the entry. `npm test` and `npm run build` pass.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
author: stormer78
significance_reasons: Normative requirement language changed
Authority, delegation, approval, or revocation semantics

title: fix(popup): a TSP-only agent is not one that advertises no transports
body:
The "VTA advertises no transports" banner checked `restBaseUrl` and `mediatorDid` only, so an agent whose single transport is TSP (a KERI did:webs VTA, for one) was told it advertises none and that every wallet operation would fail — while the popup underneath said *Transports: TSP*. The check now counts `tspMediatorDid`, and the banner names `#vta-tsp` beside the other two.

Repository — the changelog convention is signposted, enforced, and current (#935)

CHANGELOG.md opened with a ## Unreleased section that stopped at #876, while every entry since — 52 fragments — lived in changelog.d/ with nothing in the file saying so.

Signposting. CHANGELOG.md gains a note above ## Unreleased: unreleased entries live in changelog.d/ until a release is cut, this file lags that directory by design, and reading both is how you see everything pending. Above the heading deliberately — collate-changelog.sh inserts fragments immediately after the ## Unreleased line, so a note underneath would sink below the newest entries on every release. CONTRIBUTING.md's PR checklist asked for "CHANGELOG.md updated for user-facing changes" — the one thing the convention forbids, told to every contributor at the moment they were about to do it; it now asks for a fragment, beside a new Changelog section. README.md names both locations.

Enforcement. scripts/check-changelogs.sh gains two rules, because the convention had been documented in four places and enforced in none — and the cost of ignoring it never lands on the author, it lands on every other open PR as a conflict they did not cause:

  • A fragment a PR adds must name that PR, in its filename and in its ### heading. The heading half is the easy mistake — you write the fragment before the PR exists, guess the next number, and lose the race — and it is the worse one, because a wrong number survives collation and permanently points readers at an unrelated PR. Only files this PR adds are checked; the directory holds every open PR's fragment.

vta-sdk 0.21.0 / vta-keys 0.2.0 / vta-service 0.14.0 — the workspace moves to curve25519-dalek 5 (#887)

ed25519-dalek 2 → 3, x25519-dalek 2 → 3, curve25519-dalek 4 → 5 and hpke 0.13 → 0.14. These shipped together on 2026-07-06 (hpke on 07-09) and bring the next-generation RustCrypto stack with them: rand_core 0.10, signature 3, ed25519 3, aead 0.6.

vta-sdk was the single reason curve25519-dalek 4 could not leave the affinidi-tdk-rs graph. It pinned curve25519-dalek = "4" directly, plus ed25519-dalek 2, x25519-dalek 2 and hpke 0.13, and every TDK consumer inherits that through the mediator.

  • vta-sdk: breaking.   • vta-service: two sites passed an ed25519-dalek-bip32 SigningKey straight into a workspace slot. title: feat(vta-signing): a small signing library the VTA and its callers share
body:
Title
feat(vta-signing): a small signing library the VTA and its callers share

Body
## What and why

A service that signs with its own keys, when still need have a local signing option and to avoid have its own signing implementation (the Affinidi agent gateway) had to link
the whole `vta-service` library to get the VTA's signing code. That dragged in
the storage, ACL and audit code, about 290 extra packages, three licences
`cargo deny` refuses, and a Docker build that runs out of memory. This change
moves the signing code into a small crate, `vta-signing`, that the VTA and any
such service both use.

**New crate `vta-signing` (0.1.0).** It has no workspace dependencies. It holds
only the byte-building and signing: Ed25519 and P-256 signing behind a `Signer`
trait, the JWS and SSHSIG framing, `eddsa-jcs-2022` Data Integrity proofs, and
verification. It holds no keys, no storage, no network access and no
`unsafe` (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`). Its dependency closure is about 85
crates. Key storage, a KMS or an HSM would plug in behind `Signer`.

**The VTA behaves the same.** `vta-service`, `vta-sdk` and `vta-keys` now build
and make their signatures with `vta-signing` instead of their own copies.
Storage, custody, ACL, audit and quotas are untouched. Outputs are
byte-identical, pinned by characterization tests that pass on the old and the
new code.

- `vta-signing`: `canonical`, `di`, `did_methods`, `error`, `framing`, `jws`,
  `key`, `refusal`, `sshsig`. Includes the `x5c` closure and the forbidden
  header members of the JWS rules.
- `vta-sdk`: re-exports the signing framing, the SSHSIG statement and the
  forbidden header members from `vta-signing`, so existing paths keep working.
  The non-exhaustive census is updated for the moved paths.
- `vta-service`: `sign_formats.rs` is a thin facade over the crate. The signing
  steps of `keys.rs` (imported, derived, derive-and-sign), `sign_jws` and
  `sign_document` use the crate's two-phase API.
- `vta-keys`: `internal::sign` uses the crate, with equivalence tests against
  `affinidi_crypto` and `ed25519-dalek`.
- `Dockerfile.nitro` copies the new crate. `CLAUDE.md`, `vta-service/CLAUDE.md`,
  the workspace engineering notes and the decomposition note are updated.

**Not moved.** CSR building stays in the VTA. The roughly thirty other raw
signing sites (Trust Task proofs, holder proofs, rooms, voting, did:webvh
updates, `derive_and_sign_document`) are untouched. The crate's README lists
what is not here yet.

Also in this PR: the offline CLI's break-glass writes are audited. This is
the one behaviour change. The offline vta CLI has no authenticated caller and
makes no authorization decision, so a write it made to who holds authority
left no trace in the audit log. vta acl create, vta acl update, vta acl delete
and the context create command (including the admin ACL entry it can create)
now record an audit row with actor "vta-cli (break-glass)", channel "vta-cli",
the resource and, where there is one, the context. The row is written before
the store is persisted, and a failure to write it fails the command, so such a
change can't happen without leaving a record. Nothing else about the CLI
changes.

**Tests.**
- 52 tests in `vta-signing`.
- 6 characterization tests, `sign_characterization_tests.rs`, that fix what
  the signing operations produce for a fixed key (The same file, copied
unchanged onto main, passes there too).
- Offline CLI audit integration tests, offline_cli_audit.rs.
- Full workspace: `cargo nextest` 7167/7167, plus `vtc-service` and
  `vtc-client` 3645/3645.
- Doc tests pass; `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets
  -- -D warnings` are clean; `vta-enclave` builds.

## Requirements

VTI-KEY-163 (the proof's method and issuer in one form): a comment that
referenced it moves with the code, and the rule is unchanged.

## Backport

none

## Checklist

- [x] Targets `main` (or is a backport / `release-direct` PR into `release/<name>`)
- [x] No `version =` edits in any `Cargo.toml` (the new crate's own manifest has
      its first version, `0.1.0`; nothing existing is bumped)
- [x] Tests cover the change; `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean

title: feat(vta-signing): a small signing library the VTA and its callers share (#2745)
body:
feat(vta-signing): a small signing library the VTA and its callers share (#2745)

* feat(keys): keys/sign-jws/0.1 — a VTA-built compact JWS walled off to JWT types

Add a `keys/sign-jws/0.1` Trust Task that produces a compact JWS (a JWT) over
a caller-supplied JOSE header and claims set, signed by a stored key. Unlike
`keys/sign/0.1` it is not a general signing oracle: the VTA assembles the
`b64url(header).b64url(payload)` signing input itself and signs it under
`SigningDomain::ProtocolDefined`, so the result verifies as a JWS rather than
as a VTA opaque-signing payload.

The task is walled off so it can never be pointed at producing a credential or
issuer artifact:

- the finalized protected header's `typ` must be on a small allow-list of JWT
  profiles (`JWT`, `at+jwt`, `oauth-id-jag+jwt`, `dpop+jwt`, `logout+jwt`);
  anything else — e.g. a Verifiable Credential media type — is refused before
  the key is touched;
- the VTA, not the caller, sets `alg` from the key, so a caller cannot request
  a signature under an algorithm the key does not implement or mislabel one;
- the payload must be a JSON object (a JWT claims set); raw bytes still go
  through the opaque oracle, not here.

Authorized exactly as `keys/sign` is — per the key's context — so the same
context separation that walls off a signer's identities applies. Added to the
dispatch table with the spec's (none / none / actsAsSubject) class, and
acknowledged in `UNSPECCED_DISPATCHED_URIS` pending an upstream spec in
trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf (dispatched unvalidated like any
unknown-schema task until then).

Enables the Agent Gateway to delegate JWT signing (STS access tokens, ID-JAG)
to the VTA while keeping the JWT-signing path structurally separate from
credential signing.

Tests: six `sign_jws` unit tests over the header wall-off in vta-sdk, and three
conformance tests in vta-service (a real compact JWT is built with the VTA-set
`alg`; a non-JWT `typ` is refused; a non-object payload is refused).

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* feat(VTA-28): context-scoped credential issuance below super-admin

`credentials/issue/0.2` signs as the VTA itself with its own `#key-0`, so it
is instance-super-admin gated by construction. An agent delegating its own
credential signing to a VTA cannot use it without being handed authority over
the whole instance — a far larger grant than the operation warrants.

Adds `vta/credentials/issue-in-context/0.1`, which issues as a *context's* own
DID with that context's own key. The authority it needs is over the context,
so a caller holding only that context can issue. `credentials/issue/0.2` is
unchanged and still instance-gated.

The caller supplies no key id. A credential's `issuer` must be the DID whose
verification method produced the proof, so for a given context exactly one key
is valid: the caller would have no choice to make, and offering one would let
it name a key the context does not own. The VTA resolves the key from a new
`ContextRecord::issuer_key_id` designation instead, and a caller may *assert*
the verification method it expects — a mismatch is refused rather than signed
with the other key. Rotating a context's issuer key is therefore invisible to
callers.

Three refusals, all audited: a caller outside the context; a designation
pointing at a key that does not live in the context (which is what puts the
VTA's own context-less `#key-0` out of reach); and a context with no
designation at all, which fails closed rather than falling back to the VTA's
key and minting a credential attributed to the wrong issuer.

Private key material is never held. The proof's signing input is built with
`prepare_sign_input` and handed to the existing signing oracle under
`SigningDomain::ProtocolDefined`, so an internal non-exportable key — the
right custody for an issuer key — works like any other.

The designation gets its own task, `vta/contexts/set-issuer-key/0.1`, rather
than a member on `contexts/update/1.0`: that task has a published schema which
forbids additional properties, so a designation sent there is refused on the
wire before a handler sees it. It validates key residency at designation time
as well, to fail an operator's mistake where they make it.

Also classifies `keys/sign-jws/0.1` in `RETRY_SAFETY`, which had been left
unclassified.

Tests: a context-scoped caller issues and the proof verifies against the
context's issuer key; cross-context refusal; key-separation refusal;
undesignated-context fail-closed; expected-verification-method mismatch
refused and match issuing normally; no caller-supplied `keyId`; designation
residency; `credentials/issue` still instance-gated; plus a conformance test
driving the whole flow over the dispatch spine.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* feat(VTA-29): server-built Data-Integrity proof task for context keys

An agent's VP holder proof today requires whoever builds it to hold the agent's
private key. No existing task can replace that: `keys/derive-and-sign-document`
signs with an **ephemeral** derived key, so its verification method resolves to
nothing and there is no key to publish, rotate or revoke; `keys/sign` is
domain-separated and cannot produce a proof a verifier accepts; `keys/sign-jws`
produces JWTs, and for a VP the problem is *who holds the key*, not the
artifact's shape.

Adds `vta/proofs/attach/0.1`: attach an `eddsa-jcs-2022` Data-Integrity proof
to a document, signed with a **persisted key in a context**, authorized by that
context. The VTA frames the signed bytes itself — canonicalize, build the proof
configuration, hash — so this is a proof *producer*, not a signing oracle: a
caller obtains a proof it is authorized to obtain and cannot obtain a signature
over anything else.

The key is a function of (context, `proofPurpose`), never supplied. A DID
document declares a different verification method per purpose, which a
caller-supplied key id could not express correctly anyway, and letting the
caller choose would undercut the server-built property the task exists for.
`proofPurpose` is constrained to an allow-list — a proof purpose is a claim
about what a signature *means*, so an unrecognised one would mint a signature
whose meaning the VTA never agreed to.

`challenge`/`domain` are accepted on the wire and **refused**: the cryptosuite
in use carries neither member, so a proof claiming to be bound to one could not
be. Returning a proof the caller believes is replay-bound when it is not is
worse than refusing the request.

An inbound `proof` member is dropped before the signing input is built. JCS
canonicalization is presence-sensitive, so hashing a document that still
carried one would produce a proof that verifies against nothing.

Designation extends VTA-28's: `ContextRecord::proof_key_ids` maps purpose to
key, and `contexts/set-issuer-key/0.1` gained an optional `proofPurpose`.
`assertionMethod` falls back to the context's issuer key when no explicit proof
key is set — that *is* the context's assertion key, and requiring it to be
named twice would let the two disagree.

Refactors VTA-28's resolution and signing into `operations::context_signing`,
now shared by both tasks: one place decides which key a context signs with, one
place enforces that it lives in the context (which is what keeps the VTA's
context-less `#key-0` unreachable), and one place audits refusals.

Tests (11 unit + a conformance test over the dispatch spine): a context-scoped
caller gets a proof that verifies with a standard DI verifier; purpose
allow-list; cross-context refusal; key-separation refusal; undesignated-purpose
fail-closed; `assertionMethod` fallback; expected-verification-method
mismatch/match; neither a `keyId` nor raw bytes accepted; inbound proof
replaced and the replacement still verifies; `challenge`/`domain` refused.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* feat(VTA-28): carry caller-supplied JSON-LD contexts on issue-in-context

A credential whose type defines its own terms needs the context that declares
them, and the issuer — not the VTA — is what knows which one. Without this the
task could only mint credentials using the VC Data Model 2.0 base vocabulary,
which excludes every typed credential an agent actually issues.

The VTA does not resolve or interpret them; they travel with the credential for
its verifier. The base context stays first and is not duplicated if a caller
repeats it, since that would make the credential non-conformant rather than
more correct.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* feat(VTA-16): narrow context-create capability, so provisioning needs no super-admin

Creating a sub-context required `Role::Admin` of the parent. An automated
provisioner — an agent gateway minting a context per managed agent — cannot be
an admin of the context it provisions into: it is internet-facing, and the
point of its least-privilege grant is that a compromise cannot rewrite the
agent. The gateway's own `assert_scoped` refuses an `admin` grant for exactly
that reason.

The answer on the table was a separate always-on control service holding the
shared VTA super-admin, which the gateway would call to have contexts made for
it. That is a new deployment unit whose only purpose is to hold the most
dangerous credential in the system, and a new target with it.

`Capability::ContextCreate` is the smaller answer to the same need. It is
additive (no role derives it, so it reaches a non-admin, which is the whole
point) and super-admin-only to grant, which is the one-time consent step
pairing already is.

What it confers is bounded by the rules already there, not by new ones:
`create_context` still requires super-admin for a **top-level** context, and
still requires the caller to reach the parent. So the power is "branch under
what I already reach", never "create anywhere" — both pinned by tests. An admin
keeps passing through the role exactly as before; this adds a path rather than
replacing one.

The gate lives in the operations layer, not the handler, because the create
surface is reachable over more than one transport and a gate written per
transport is one that eventually differs between them. A failed ACL read
refuses rather than falling through to the role check: not being able to
confirm a capability is not the same as not having one.

Tests: a capability holder creates a sub-context without being an admin; it
cannot create a top-level context; it cannot reach another context's subtree; a
non-admin without it is still refused; an admin still passes without it.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* feat(VTA-16): grant capabilities from the CLI, so context-create can be conferred

The capability was enforced but ungrantable: neither `vta acl create` nor
`vta acl update` could set one, so the feature could not be turned on by any
operator. Found by driving the end-to-end flow against a running VTA.

`--capabilities` on both, by wire name. Replaces rather than merges, so an
operator can narrow as well as widen; an unknown name is an error rather than
something to skip, because silently dropping one stores an entry holding less
than was asked for and reports success.

`update` matters as much as `create`: an existing gateway enabling
provisioning has to gain the capability without being deleted and recreated.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* feat(contexts): let a provisioner configure a context it created, once

VTA-16. A caller holding `context-create` could create a sub-context but
not make it usable: naming its DID and designating its signing key were
admin-only, so every provisioned context needed an administrator to
finish it by hand. That defeats self-provisioning.

Both operations now admit a second path. The ordinary admin gate is
checked first and is unchanged; only when it refuses does a caller that
(a) reaches the context and (b) holds `context-create` get considered.
Such a caller may fill a field that is **unset** and nothing else:
re-pointing an established DID, clearing one, or re-designating a key
stays an administrator's act and is refused by name.

Write-once is what keeps this from being a privilege grant. No ACL entry
is written, so authority never accumulates; a provisioner can bring a
blank context to life but can never reconfigure one, including one it
created itself. Reach is unchanged — a context outside the granted
subtree stays out of reach whether its fields are blank or not.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* fix(contexts): let the provisioning path reach update-did and set-issuer-key

The write-once provisioning path was unreachable over the Trust Task
surface: both handlers pre-gated on admin / super-admin before calling
the operation, so a provisioner was refused with "admin role required"
having never reached the code that would have allowed it.

The gate now lives in one place — the operation — which already checks
the ordinary admin gate first and only then considers a provisioner with
an unset field. Caught by the live end-to-end, not by a unit test: the
operations were tested directly, which is exactly the seam that skips
the handler.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* feat(sign-jws): permit the gateway issuer-attestation JWT type

An Agent Gateway tells a peer gateway which issuer DID stands behind a
connection with a `gateway-issuer-attestation+jwt`. The peer verifies it
by resolving the claimed `iss` and checking the signing key is declared
in that document — so the signature has to come from the same party the
DID names, which means signing it here rather than with a key the
gateway holds locally.

`JWS_ALLOWED_TYPS` refused it, so that artifact was the one thing still
signed with a locally held key.

Unlike the other entries this one is not IANA-registered; it is an
application type. It is listed on the same basis the registered ones
are: it names a JWT profile, so permitting it widens nothing
structurally — the task still cannot be pointed at producing a
credential proof or a task envelope. The doc comment records that
boundary, because "it was convenient" is how an allow-list like this
stops meaning anything.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* chore: ignore operator-local VTA configs under local-dev/

The setup files tracked in `local-dev/` are portable by construction. A
*running* local instance needs absolute paths — `config_path`, `data_dir`
— which name one machine and one checkout, so such a file can only ever
be local and must never reach the history.

`vta-local-persistent.toml` was sitting untracked and unignored, which is
exactly the state #888's CI log was in before a `git add -A` committed a
home directory's worth of path into the repository.

Anchored to the directory and prefixed `vta-local-`, so the tracked
`vta-root-webvh-setup.toml` and `vta-pathful-webvh-setup.toml` are
unaffected and the convention extends to further local configs.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* fix: add vscode to ignore

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* test(vtc): count the three gateway URIs bound ahead of their specs

`every_bound_canonical_task_exists_in_the_registry` pins, per authority,
how many bound `trusttasks.org/spec/` URIs the registry does not serve.
The Agent Gateway work binds three under `spec/vta/` and never updated
the count, so the assertion read 7 against an expected 4.

It went unnoticed because `vtc-service` does not build without Node
>= 20.19 for its admin UI, so the crate was excluded from local runs.

Raised to 7 with the three named. The test says raising the number is
the wrong fix, and that is the right default — but the same note records
`vta/webvh/servers/reconcile/0.1` going up and back down inside a day,
and calls the round trip "the whole mechanism working, not an exception
to it". This is that case: all three are already tracked as the same
debt in the VTA's `UNSPECCED_DISPATCHED_URIS`, with the route back to 4
being an upstream spec in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf and a trust-tasks-rs bump
— not an edit here.

The note spells out why each cannot use a published task: `issue/0.2`
signs as the VTA and is instance-gated by construction; `contexts/update/1.0`
forbids additional properties, so the designation cannot ride on it; and
`keys/derive-and-sign-document` signs with an ephemeral key whose
verification method resolves to nothing.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* Revert "feat(VTA-29): server-built Data-Integrity proof task for context keys"

This reverts commit cb50c2a3ec5fee62789fe1b9278998ebb02dc0f9.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* Revert "feat(VTA-28): carry caller-supplied JSON-LD contexts on issue-in-context"

This reverts commit b34f2bca9fc7e804ba4d350bc04e54f818003e73.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* Revert "feat(VTA-28): context-scoped credential issuance below super-admin"

This reverts commit dd1b0c4aed0979be2c78a847d74b622a8b2cbc2c.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* fix: clean up

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* fix(sdk): list context-create among the additive capabilities

vti-common registers context-create as additive but the SDK's copy did not,
so the test that pins the two lists equal failed once it landed on main. An
SDK client sending a grant of context-create beside a role now treats it as
additive, as the VTA does.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta-service): audit offline break-glass ACL and context writes

The offline CLI writes authority with no authenticated caller and no
authorization decision, so the write must be visible (VTI-AUD-001). acl
create/update/delete and contexts create now record an audit row with actor
'vta-cli (break-glass)' and channel 'vta-cli' before persisting, and a failed
audit write fails the command.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta-signing): add the signing core crate

The bytes a JWS or an eddsa-jcs-2022 proof signs, and the Ed25519 and P-256
signature over them, are built in one place with no storage, access control,
audit, async code or I/O, and no dependency on another crate of this
workspace. The VTA's signing operations and any service that signs with keys
of its own can share it, so a fix to how a signature is made lands once.

This commit only adds the crate and its tests; the VTA moves onto it next.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* test(vta-service): pin what the signing operations produce for a fixed key

Ed25519 and ES256 signatures are deterministic, so the signature a key makes
over the bytes a specification defines is the same whatever code made it. These
tests sign through the real operations (gates, custody and audit included) for
an imported Ed25519 and P-256 key and compare with references built from the
primitives alone: opaque and protocol-defined payloads, a JWS from a JSON and a
base64url payload, an eddsa-jcs-2022 document proof and an SSHSIG signature.

They pass on the code as it is, and are the evidence that moving the byte
building and the signing step into vta-signing changes no output.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta-signing): signers, two-phase formats, verification and SSHSIG

The crate now holds everything about producing a signature, shared by the VTA
and by services that sign with their own keys:

- SigningSecret, PublicKey (did:key in and out) and the Signer trait, so a
  hardware or remote key can sign through the same formats later;
- the opaque-signing framing and SigningDomain;
- JWS, eddsa-jcs-2022 Data Integrity and SSHSIG, each as prepare, finish and a
  one-call sign, with the VTA's own gates able to sit between the phases, and
  verification that signs nothing and rejects a swapped challenge or domain;
- the rules for which key may sign as which DID;
- the specification's refusal codes, exhaustive on purpose so a service mapping
  them to wire codes fails to compile when one is added.

No async, I/O, storage or dependency on another workspace crate. Certificate
requests and the VTA's other signing seams are not moved yet; the README lists
them.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* refactor(vta-sdk): take the signing framing and SSHSIG statement from vta-signing

SigningDomain, the opaque-signing framing, the SSHSIG signed data, the
forbidden JWS header members and the lenient Ed25519 multibase decoder are
defined once in vta-signing and re-exported from the paths they had, so no
caller changes. Their tests moved with them.

SigningDomain stays exhaustive: a domain a signer does not know must not be
signed in, and the non-exhaustive census holds it to that at its new path. The
census also lists vta-signing's FormatRefusal, whose variants are the
specification's codes and must fail to compile when added unmapped.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* refactor(vta-service): build and make signatures with vta-signing

The operations still do everything around a signature — gates, key custody, the
quota, the audit row — and sign through the same audited step. What changed is
whose code builds the bytes and makes the signature: the JWS signing input and
compact form, the eddsa-jcs-2022 proof, the signer's DID methods and the
refusal codes come from vta-signing (sign_formats keeps the certificate
reader, the CSR builders and the did:scid form as a thin facade, so call sites
resolve unchanged), and the Ed25519 and P-256 signing of imported, derived and
internal keys is vta-signing's. Certificate requests and the other signing
seams stay where they are.

No output changes: sign_characterization_tests, added before this change,
pins what the operations produce for a fixed key, and vta-keys proves its
internal P-256 key signs the same bytes as before.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* docs: describe vta-signing as the signing core the VTA and its callers share

Adds the crate to the layer list, the crate table and the decomposition note
with the dependency-surface case that justifies it, records the rule that
signatures are built and made by vta-signing rather than hand-rolled in an
operation, updates the signing-oracle entry in vta-service/CLAUDE.md, and the
published-crate count.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* docs(vta-service): restore the comment line the upstream merge dropped in trust_tasks

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service): audit every offline write of authority and harden vta-signing's verifiers

Break-glass audit (VTI-AUD-001, VTI-AUD-004):
- `vta contexts create` checks the admin grant (`--admin-did` shape,
  `--admin-handoff` needing `--admin-expires`) before it creates anything, and
  audits the context as soon as it exists, so a refused grant no longer leaves
  a created, unaudited context.
- The offline context reprovision audits the Admin ACL entry it writes,
  through the state's own sink so the chain head is not forked.
- `CliStore::audit_or_undo`: a write is undone, before anything is persisted,
  when its audit row cannot be written, so no offline change of authority
  survives without its row. Used by acl create / update / delete and context
  create.
- Break-glass rows go through the chained sink, as the daemon's do. An
  unchained row after the chain opened is a finding to `audit/verify`, so
  every offline write looked like tampering.
- `keyspace()` gets its doc comment back.

vta-signing:
- `verify_jws` refuses a protected header naming `crit` or `b64`
  (RFC 7515 §4.1.11, RFC 7797), as the signer already does.
- `verify_document` accepts `proofValue` only as base58btc, as eddsa-jcs-2022
  requires.
- `SigningSecret::from_p256_secret` builds the key without serialising the
  scalar, and `ed25519_from_slice` copies straight into zeroizing memory; the
  derived-key and derive-and-sign paths use them, so no plain copy of a
  secret is left on the stack.
- `finish_document` takes its input by value: one document copy, not two.

vta-service signing:
- `sign_payload_bytes` returns the raw signature, so the JWS, CSR and
  Data Integrity paths no longer base64url-encode it only to decode it again.
- The JWS `alg` (header, audit row, answer) comes from one value.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

title: docs(design-notes): DID management, one question asked once whatever the method
body:
A VTA whose identities were all did:webs reported none: the wallet's persona picker, the console's DIDs pane and `pnm did-mgmt dids list` each asked `vta/webvh/dids/list` alone. A fourth method would add a fourth question to every client.

This note records the design that replaces it (specified in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1332):

- **Method-neutral questions asked once**: `vta/dids/{list,get,methods/list}/0.1`, one `DidSummary` per identity with per-method `methodDetails` defined by the method profiles; a context's DID through `vta/contexts/update-did/1.2`, which refuses a DID the VTA does not hold. The per-method lists are retired. did:key is listed from its key records; did:peer is not (no record is kept).
- **Per-method operations stay per method**: create, update, rotate, realign, logs/KELs, delete, servers.
- **A `DidEngine` seam in vta-service**, keyed by how authority is kept (webvh log: webvh + scid; KERI: webs; keys: did:key). Key-roles' `MethodProfile` lands on it rather than in a second registry.
- **One rule each** where webvh and webs had drifted: reachability answers, the primary-DID guard, context delete and its preview, host reconcile/retire-orphan.

Also corrects stale text: the did:webs note's §1 table (overtaken by its own §4), pnm's `webs` help text, and the webvh handler header (retired URIs, wrong auth for domains and agent names).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: refactor(state_handler): per-panel sync and vetting follow-ups as effect steps
body:
The rest of #612 after #613, #614 and #615. Commits:

1. `test(vetting): pin …` — runtime-harness tests for the two vetting follow-ups, written against the code before the change.
2. `refactor(state_handler): …` — the change. `git diff` of `openvtc/src/state_handler/runtime/tests/` across it is empty, and the pinning tests pass on it unchanged.
3. `refactor(main_page): one sync clock, and a minute refresh …` — from review (see "Time-dependent text" below).
4. `test(main_page): sync fixture reaches every panel input; …` — from review.
5. `test(runtime): drive the narrowed sync callers …` — from review.
6. `docs(changelog): …` and `docs(main_page): …` (a rustdoc link fix).

No user-visible behaviour change, except that text which changes with the clock alone is now refreshed on a one-minute tick rather than by whichever full rebuild came next (see below).

## 1. `sync_from_config` split per panel

### Design

- `MainPageState::sync_panels(&Config, Panels)` rebuilds a set of panels. `sync_from_config` is now `sync_panels(config, Panels::ALL)`.
- `Panels` is a small bit set: `HEADER`, `VETTING`, `INBOX`, `RELATIONSHIPS`, `CREDENTIALS`, `SETTINGS`, `VTA`, `IDENTITY`, `COMMUNITIES`, and `ALL`.
- Each panel's rebuild is its own private fn (`sync_inbox`, `sync_relationships`, `sync_credentials`, `sync_settings`, `sync_vta`, `sync_identity` + `sync_memberships`, `sync_communities`; the header and vetting were already one call each). Each reads `Config` and **its own panel state only**, so the order no longer matters and a panel synced alone gets exactly what the full sync gives it. Two fields moved to the panel they belong to:
  - `identity.agent_credential_did` was set inside the VTA block; it is now set by the identity sync, from the same `key_backend` match.
  - `settings.protection_type` was set after the identity block; it is now in the settings sync.
- The `Panels::FROM_*` sets name the panels by **what changed**, so a caller says what it touched, not which panels it thinks are affected:

| Set | Panels | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `FROM_TASKS` | inbox | only the inbox reads `private.tasks` |
| `FROM_RELATIONSHIPS` | inbox, relationships, credentials, VTA | relationships, contacts, VRCs, witnessings, key records: the inbox names our DID on an outbound request; a VRC row is scoped by its relationship; the VTA panel counts keys and lists R-DIDs |
| `FROM_VETTING_BOOK` | vetting, communities, credentials, inbox | the book feeds the Vetting page, the Communities overview (branding, PCS ZKP, "joining" rows), the credentials (vetting statements); a vetting outcome also clears inbox tasks |
| `FROM_DISPLAY_ORDER` | communities, header | favourite/archived marks reorder the overview, and the header names the first Active community in display order |
| `FROM_FRIENDLY_NAME` | header, settings | |
| `FROM_CLOCK` | credentials, communities, vetting | the panels whose text turns with the clock alone; synced by the loop once a minute |

- No dirty-tracking: nothing records which panels are stale. A caller syncs at the change, and syncs `ALL` when it cannot say.

### Which callers sync what

**Every panel (`sync_from_config`), unchanged** — reach is global or unclear:
- startup / setup-wizard exit / load / State-A join exit (`state_handler/mod.rs`), runtime start (`runtime/mod.rs`)
- working-persona changes: `SetActiveCommunity`, `CommunitySwitcherSelect`, the loop's reconcile (`runtime/mod.rs`)
- persona created / deleted (`mod.rs`, `relationship_actions.rs` identity removal — also drops vetting applications)
- membership status changes: leave (`community_actions.rs`), cancel join, delete membership, pending expiry (`timers.rs`), deregister after settle (`arms.rs`), community-context delete (`community_context_actions.rs`), join launch persisted (`join_flow/driver.rs`)
- agent-name cache changes (`background_dispatch.rs`, `agent_name_actions.rs`) — every panel shows names
- VTA state sync absorb (`arms.rs`) and inbound messages (`inbound_arm.rs`, both sites) — can touch anything
- `focus_application` / `focus_vetting_target` (`answers.rs`) — called from the join flow and the inbox, which may have changed account state before focusing
- tests

**Narrowed:**

| Caller | Syncs | Changed |
|---|---|---|
| inbox dismiss / clear all | `FROM_TASKS` | tasks only |
| ping reply-window expiry, vetter-grant expiry tasks (`timers.rs`) | `FROM_TASKS` | tasks only |
| inbox accept/reject relationship, accept/issue/reject VRC (`inbox_actions::save_and_sync`) | `FROM_RELATIONSHIPS` | relationships, keys, VRCs, tasks |
| relationship request/ping/VRC request/remove, `our_did` fix-up, alias (`relationship_actions.rs`) | `FROM_RELATIONSHIPS` | same family |
| VRC request outcome, VRC removal (`credential_actions.rs`) | `FROM_RELATIONSHIPS` | tasks, VRCs |
| witnessing recorded (`witness_actions.rs`) | `RELATIONSHIPS` | `witnessings`, read only by the relationships sync |
| every vetting save/sync: `persist`, outcome, tickets, grant check, `give_up`, hidden tick, abandon, PCS outcome, book housekeeping in `timers.rs` | `FROM_VETTING_BOOK` | vetting book (+ tasks in the outcome); no vetting handler writes the account, identities, keys, contacts or relationships |
| favourite toggle, archive | `FROM_DISPLAY_ORDER` | `favourite` / `archived` |
| acknowledge outcome | `COMMUNITIES` | `acknowledged`, read only by the overview's attention flags/badge |
| toggle show-archived | `COMMUNITIES` | page state read only by the overview |
| set aside for verification (`mod.rs`) | `COMMUNITIES` | `communities.verifying` (page state) |
| friendly name | `FROM_FRIENDLY_NAME` | `public.friendly_name` |
| set / remove passphrase | `SETTINGS` | `public.protection`, read only by settings |

`dispatch_util::Persist::{SaveAndSync, SyncOnly}` now carry the `Panels`.

### Time-dependent text (from review)

- **One clock per sync.** `main_page::sync_clock()` is read once per `sync_panels` and passed into the credentials (validity), communities (`pending_unacknowledged`, joining standing) and vetting (`view_sync::sync`, `sync_journey`) rebuilds; none reads `Utc::now()` itself any more. Tests freeze it per thread (`main_page::test_clock::freeze`), so every comparison below is deterministic across a minute or day rollover.
- **Minute refresh.** A full sync used to bring a credential's "expired", a join's "awaiting acknowledgement" and a vetter grant's "expiring" up to date as a side effect; with narrowed syncs that would lag until the next full one. The loop's existing 60 s `join_status_tick` now ends with `sync_panels(config, Panels::FROM_CLOCK)` (credentials | communities | vetting), so these labels are **at most a minute late**. No new timer or loop. `time_passing_reaches_only_the_panels_the_minute_refresh_syncs` shows that advancing the clock 400 days changes exactly `FROM_CLOCK`'s panels, each of them, and `the_minute_tick_catches_up_with_the_clock` drives the tick in the harness and compares with a full sync.

### Tests

**Unit (`main_page/mod.rs`)**, on `busy_config`, an account that reaches every input each panel reads: a loaded persona (so the header/settings/VTA persona DID, `is_persona_did` and the Vetting personas are non-empty) with a friendly name, two Active memberships plus a Left (archived), a Rejected (unacknowledged) and a Pending one; a relationship with VRCs both ways, an alias and an R-DID; tasks including a `RelationshipRequestOutbound` (the inbox reads `our_did`); keys; a VTA key backend; a VIC on the page (so `sync_vic_agent_names` works); a vetting application with a statement and one still joining (visible on the Vetting page and as a Communities joining row); a vetter grant; branding and PCS ZKP mode; verified agent names. `the_sync_fixture_fills_what_each_panel_reads` checks those reach the page.
- `each_panel_synced_alone_shows_what_the_full_sync_shows` — each panel synced alone equals the full sync's view of it and leaves every other panel untouched; every panel is non-empty.
- `the_full_sync_is_every_panel_synced` — per-panel syncs in reverse order, and `sync_panels(ALL)`, equal `sync_from_config`.
- **Every member of every `FROM_*` set is load-bearing**: each set's test applies a change touching each input the set exists for, then asserts (a) the partial sync equals a full sync and (b) **every panel in the set shows the change** — so dropping any panel from a set fails a test. (Checked: removing `INBOX` from `FROM_VETTING_BOOK` fails its test.) Changes: tasks cleared; relationship alias, VRC, key and `our_did`; vetting statements, a new application, branding and the task a send clears (as `outcome::sent_result` does); a favourite that moves the second Active community first (header); friendly name; protection; acknowledgement; show-archived (the real archived Left membership — the old test archived an Active one, which the code refuses, and synced the header by hand); archiving an inactive membership.

**Runtime harness (`runtime/tests/sync.rs`)** — the real narrowed handlers on `busy_config` at a frozen clock, then the **whole page compared with a full `sync_from_config`**, so a handler that changes more than its set covers is caught (checked: syncing only `COMMUNITIES` on favourite fails): accept a VRC, dismiss a task, a vetting send outcome clearing its task (`Sent::Session`), abandon an application, favourite, archive an inactive membership, acknowledge, show archived, friendly name, and the minute tick.

Not driven in the harness: **set/remove passphrase**. Both force-flush to the OS keyring and profile files (`SaveScheduler::flush`), which the harness would do against the real keychain. Their sync (`SETTINGS`) is covered by `the_protection_reaches_only_settings`, which makes the same `Config` changes (protection, a config log line) but the derived key, which no panel reads.

## 2. The two vetting follow-ups are effect steps

- New `Step::Always(Box<Step>)`: run even when a step before it gave up. On an abort the runner now drops every remaining step **except** `Always` ones, where it returned before; no existing plan has an `Always` step, so their runs are unchanged. The steps a `Then` inside an `Always` expands into are ordinary (one failing skips the rest of them, but not later `Always` steps).
- **`RefreshRequirements`** is planned (`dispatch::plan_refresh`): the refresh's own steps, then `Always(Then(Followup::AskChallenge { application_id, said_before }))` and `Always(RefreshVetterSide)`. `said_before` is the status before the plan, as the loop-side code captured it; `AskChallenge` is planned once the refresh has run and asks quietly when the status changed to a warning or error since (`effect::warned_since`, shared with `Summary`). With no application selected the effect is just the vetter pass.
- **Enter on the attest form** is planned in `plan_submit`: `plan_attest` → the named statement's effect, `plan_attest_hidden(.., has_vta, ..)`, or `[RefreshVetterSide]` to enrol. `has_vta` and `busy` are the values the old path read (sampled once per action, nothing in between changes them). No abort precedes these, so they need no `Always`.
- Gone: `Planned`, `on_loop`, `submit`, `desk::attest`, `hidden::ask_for_challenge`, `hidden::attest_hidden`. Every vetting action is plan + run.

### Pinning tests (commit 1, unchanged by commit 2)

- `refreshing_requirements_while_busy_still_runs_the_vetter_pass`
- `refreshing_requirements_without_keys_still_runs_the_vetter_pass` (log order: give-up, then the pass)
- `refreshing_requirements_with_no_application_runs_the_vetter_pass`
- `hidden::a_refresh_gives_up_then_the_challenge_then_the_vetter_pass` (log order of all three)
- `hidden::attesting_a_proof_unenrolled_enrols_through_the_vetter_pass` and `..._while_busy_still_enrols`
- `hidden::attesting_a_proof_with_no_vta_says_it_is_not_connected` (also with the vetting domain held)
- `hidden::attesting_a_proof_with_no_token_says_to_wait` (with a VTA session)

These, with the existing `a_challenge_without_keys_…` / `a_challenge_asked_while_busy_leaves_the_busy_refusal_said` (the challenge stays quiet after a busy refusal) / `a_hidden_application_asks_…`, cover the regardless semantics. From review, `a_challenge_after_a_refresh_that_went_out_says_it_is_asking` covers the other side of `warned_since` in the harness: a warning left from before the refresh does not hold the challenge's note back. Commit 2 adds plan unit tests (`a_refresh_with_no_application_owes_the_vetter_pass`, `a_refused_refresh_still_owes_the_challenge_and_the_pass`) and updates `plan_reduces_or_plans`.

## 3. Repos `open` / `save_settings`: left as runner steps

They touch the disk: `save_settings` is a background job and `open` reads with `spawn_blocking` (#615). That is the right shape for I/O — the plan stays pure and the runner owns the effect. Folding them into the plan would put disk I/O in the reducer, and there is no cleaner fit, so they stay.

## Test counts

`cargo test --workspace --locked`:
- before (origin/main): 2721 passed, 0 failed, 37 ignored
- after (default features): 2755 passed, 0 failed, 37 ignored
- after (`--no-default-features`): 2755 passed, 0 failed, 37 ignored
- after (`-- --include-ignored`): 2792 passed, 0 failed

New since origin/main: 8 vetting pinning tests, 2 vetting plan tests (one plan test rewritten), 1 vetting runtime test, 13 main-page sync tests, 10 runtime sync tests.

On the final tip: `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy `-D warnings` (default, `--no-default-features`, `-p openvtc --features dev-overrides`), `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` and `cargo machete` are clean. rustc 1.100.0.

Closes #612

## Pre-merge checklist (§9)

```
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no new clients
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — none touched
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — order of every commit/send unchanged (pinned)
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — no retries added
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — not touched
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — not touched
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — no wire changes
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — no config changes
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — status and log text unchanged (pinned)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — no mutation order changed; the sync is display-only
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none
```
