title: refactor(state_handler): per-panel sync and vetting follow-ups as effect steps (#616)
body:
refactor(state_handler): per-panel sync and vetting follow-ups as effect steps (#616)

* test(vetting): pin the refresh and attest follow-ups that run whatever came before

RefreshRequirements asks for the hidden-vetting challenge and runs the
vetter pass even after a busy refusal, a give-up, or with no application
selected; Enter on the attestation form attests the hidden way or enrols
through the vetter pass whether or not the vetting domain is held. Pin
both against the current loop-side helpers before they become effect
steps (#612).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(state_handler): per-panel sync and vetting follow-ups as steps

Split MainPageState::sync_from_config into per-panel rebuilds behind
sync_panels(config, Panels). Each caller now syncs the panels that read
what it changed (Panels::FROM_* name them by source); startup, loads,
persona/membership changes, the agent-name cache, VTA state sync and
inbound messages still sync every panel. Persist::SaveAndSync/SyncOnly
carry the panels. New tests show each panel synced alone equals the full
sync for that panel and touches no other, the full sync is every panel
synced, and each FROM_* set after its kind of change equals a full sync.

Make the vetting page's last loop-side follow-ups effect steps. A new
Step::Always runs even after an earlier step gave up; RefreshRequirements
plans the refresh, then Always(Then(AskChallenge)) and
Always(RefreshVetterSide), preserving that both run after a busy refusal
or give-up. Enter on the attest form plans the named statement, the
hidden attestation or the enrolling pass. Planned::Loop, on_loop, submit,
desk::attest, hidden::ask_for_challenge and hidden::attest_hidden go.
The pinning tests in runtime/tests/ are unchanged and pass (#612).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(main_page): one sync clock, and a minute refresh of time-dependent panels

Every sync now formats its time-dependent text against one reading of
sync_clock(), threaded into the credentials, communities and vetting
rebuilds (and the journey view); tests freeze it per thread so two syncs
compare equal across a rollover. Since a change syncs only the panels
that read it, the loop's 60 s join-status tick syncs Panels::FROM_CLOCK
(credentials, communities, vetting), so expiry, acknowledgement and
grant-expiring text lags by at most a minute (#612).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(main_page): sync fixture reaches every panel input; each set's members load-bearing

The sync test account now has a loaded persona and friendly name, an
outbound relationship request, a VIC on the page, a joining application,
a vetter grant, branding and PCS ZKP, and inactive, archived and pending
memberships. Each FROM_* test asserts every panel in its set shows the
change (so none can be dropped) and that the partial sync equals a full
one. The show-archived test toggles the real archived Left membership
instead of archiving an Active one; archiving tests an inactive one.
A clock test shows time passing changes exactly Panels::FROM_CLOCK (#612).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(runtime): drive the narrowed sync callers and compare with a full sync

Runtime-harness tests run the real handlers that sync only some panels
(accept a VRC, dismiss a task, a vetting send outcome clearing its task,
abandon an application, favourite, archive an inactive membership,
acknowledge, show archived, friendly name) over the full sync fixture,
at a frozen clock, and assert the whole page equals a full
sync_from_config; the minute tick is shown catching up after a long gap.
Adds a runtime test that the challenge announces after a refresh that
went out, beside the busy-refusal one (#612).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(changelog): the minute refresh of time-dependent panels (#612)

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(main_page): no intra-doc link to the test-only clock (#612)

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(vtc/storage/credentials/recipient): add vtc/storage/credentials/recipient/0.1 (#1329)
body:
feat(vtc/storage/credentials/recipient): add vtc/storage/credentials/recipient/0.1 (#1329)

A room-hosting administrator's client asks the community for the key a
vtc/storage/credentials/set sealed block is sealed to: the Ed25519 key it
opens with, as its did:key, and the verification method in its DID
document that publishes it.

A client that cannot resolve and verify the community's DID could not
seal at all. A browser console reading a did:webs would need KERI
verification, and a hosted did:webvh would need a log from another
origin. The VTC console read only the same-origin did.jsonl, which a
did:webs community never serves. The answer comes over the same
authenticated channel the credential then goes over, and is the same
for every DID method. `notPublished` covers a key the community's
document no longer lists, so nothing is sealed past a rotation.

credentials/set 0.3's sealed-block definition and `related` now point
at it (prose only).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(bridge): use jemalloc so freed memory returns to the OS
body:
Makes the long-running `vgi-bridge` binary use jemalloc as its global allocator, so freed memory is returned to the OS.

## Why

With the system allocator (glibc malloc on Linux), the process keeps the arenas behind its short-lived buffers (messages, frames, request/response bodies) instead of returning them. RSS ratchets up to its high-water mark and never comes back down, which reads as a leak on a memory graph even though the live heap is flat. jemalloc's decay-based purging returns those pages, so RSS tracks live memory.

## What

Mirrors `affinidi-messaging-mediator`:

- A default-on `jemalloc` feature (`dep:tikv-jemallocator`), with the dependency under `[target.'cfg(not(target_env = "msvc"))'.dependencies]`. MSVC builds and `--no-default-features` builds fall back to the system allocator.
- `#[global_allocator]` is set in `main.rs` only, never in a library crate, so no consumer has an allocator imposed on it.
- jemalloc tuning is exported as `_rjem_malloc_conf`: `background_thread:true,dirty_decay_ms:5000,muzzy_decay_ms:5000`. The prefixed name is required because `tikv-jemalloc-sys` builds jemalloc with `--with-jemalloc-prefix=_rjem_`, so an unprefixed `malloc_conf` export links fine but jemalloc ignores it. The value is typed `&[u8; 63]`, a thin pointer that matches C's `const char *`, rather than a `&[u8]` fat pointer.

Only `vgi-bridge` is changed. The CLIs (`vgi`, `did-git-sign`, `verify-trust`) are short-lived and keep the system allocator. The Dockerfile build stage (`rust:1.98-bookworm`, the full image) already has `make` and `cc` for `tikv-jemalloc-sys`, so it doesn't change. Release targets for vgi-bridge are linux-gnu and macOS, and jemalloc supports both. The `tikv-jemallocator` version comes from the workspace dependencies.

title: fix(vtc-service): setup speaks did:webs, not webvh, once the operator chooses it
body:
After an operator picks did:webs, the VTC setup wizard still asked for a **"WebVH path (blank → server-assigned)"**. It also explained the path as the DID's trailing segment. For a did:webs the path is the slot before the AID, and leaving it blank publishes at the domain's top level (`CreateDidWebsParams::path`).

- **Advice on changing the DID document after mint:** now also gives the did:webs route. This was webvh-only in the registry prompt, the `registry_did` and `[webvh]` field docs, `vtc-setup.example.toml` and `community-lifecycle.md`.

Tests: `the_path_prompt_speaks_the_chosen_method` and `a_did_webs_path_refuses_the_webvh_root_slot`. `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -E 'test(setup)'` passes (85 tests), and clippy for `vtc-service` is clean.

title: feat(vtc-service): store and serve an uploaded community logo
body: ## What and why A community can now upload its logo, and the VTC serves it from its own origin, so it shows in the console, the member portal, both sign-in pages and the default landing page wherever the VTC is hosted. Before this, the logo was only the profile's `logoUrl`. Those pages are served with `img-src 'self' data:`, so a logo at any other address was never drawn, and a deployment with nowhere on the VTC's own origin to put a file (a hosted VTC, say) had no logo at all: a filesystem website must have its own host, and `admin_ui.members_dir` is a snapshot that stops following the daemon on every upgrade. **Depends on trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1324**, which specifies `vtc/community/logo/update/0.1`. This PR pins that version from a bundle built locally from that branch (digest `sha256:344dc73d9c5f…`, the same bytes the registry will publish). It is a draft until that PR has merged and a Trust Tasks release has published the bundle; if the spec changes in review, the pin here must be redone. What it adds: - **The write**: `vtc/community/logo/update/0.1`, pinned in `vti-specs-vtc`. An administrator (`vtc.surface.admin`) sends a PNG, JPEG or WebP, or `image: null` to remove the logo. The community re-encodes it as a PNG of at most 512 px (`directory::images::reencode_logo`, sharing the directory's decoding and its bounds), dropping all metadata and any bytes after the image data, and stores it in the `community` keyspace, which is backed up. 20 changes per administrator per hour, one update at a time, audited as `CommunityLogoUpdated` by digest. - **The read**: `GET /v1/community/logo`, public like `public-profile`. Fixed `Content-Type`, `nosniff`, `default-src 'none'; sandbox`, an `ETag` and `304`. Bytes that do not match their record are never served. - **Pages**: a `logo` member (`url`, `sha256`, `mediaType`, `width`, `height`) on the public profile and on `/v1/member/me`'s `community`. Every page draws it in preference to `logoUrl`, which is unchanged. - **Console**: a Logo card on the Community profile page. It rasterizes an SVG in the browser, from a `data:` URL inside an `` where it runs no script, so no SVG is ever sent or stored. The Logo URL field now says when these pages will not draw the address it holds. - **Repairable store**: an unreadable record is replaced rather than blocking updates, and sending the same image again restores stored bytes that no longer match. Design note with the decisions and where each security property is held: `docs/05-design-notes/vtc-community-logo.md`. Testing: the new unit and integration tests (`vtc-service/tests/it/community_logo.rs`, 11 cases, including a polyglot PNG, a pixel bomb, SVG and HTML sent as PNG, a payload without `image`, a tampered store, the header set and `304`), the census tests, clippy and fmt pass. The admin UI suite passes. The SVG rasterization was also run by hand in a browser under the console's CSP against hostile SVGs (script, `onload`, external image, CSS `@import`, `foreignObject`); none made a network request. Locally, 13 `admin_events` integration tests time out in a full parallel run; they fail the same way on `main` on the same machine and pass when run alone. ## Requirements None in the VTI specification: it has no logo requirement. The task's own conformance items are cited in the code. ## Backport none ## Checklist - [x] Targets `main` (or is a backport / `release-direct` PR into `release/`) - [x] No `version =` edits in any `Cargo.toml` - [x] Tests cover the change; `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean

Before this, the logo was only the profile's `logoUrl`. Those pages are served with `img-src 'self' data:`, so a logo at any other address was never drawn, and a deployment with nowhere on the VTC's own origin to put a file (a hosted VTC, say) had no logo at all: a filesystem website must have its own host, and `admin_ui.members_dir` is a snapshot that stops following the daemon on every upgrade. What it adds: - `vtc/community/logo/update/0.1` (pinned in `vti-specs-vtc`): an administrator (`vtc.surface.admin`) sends a PNG, JPEG or WebP, or `image: null` to remove the logo. The community re-encodes it as a PNG of at most 512 px (`directory::images::reencode_logo`, sharing the directory's decoding and its bounds), dropping all metadata and any bytes after the image data, and stores it in the `community` keyspace, which is backed up. 20 changes per administrator per hour, one re-encoding at a time, audited as `CommunityLogoUpdated` by digest. - `GET /v1/community/logo`: public, like `public-profile`. Served from memory against a small record read, with a fixed `Content-Type`, `nosniff`, `default-src 'none'; sandbox`, an `ETag` and `304`. Bytes that do not match their record are never served. - A `logo` member (`url`, `sha256`, `mediaType`, `width`, `height`) on the public profile and on `/v1/member/me`'s `community`. Every page draws it in preference to `logoUrl`, which is unchanged. - Console: a Logo card on the Community profile page. It rasterizes an SVG in the browser, from a `data:` URL inside an `` where it runs no script, so no SVG is ever sent or stored. The Logo URL field now says when these pages will not draw the address it holds. Design note: docs/05-design-notes/vtc-community-logo.md. Signed-off-by: Geoff Turk * fix(vtc-service): a stored logo an administrator can always repair Review of the community-logo change found three gaps in the update path: - An unreadable `community/logo` record made every later update fail, so nothing but editing the store could replace or remove it. The record is now read leniently and replaced. - "Already stored" was decided from the record alone. Bytes that were lost or no longer matched their record were (rightly) not served, but sending the same image again was a no-op and never restored them. It is now a no-op only when that logo is actually servable; a removal is a no-op only when the record itself says nothing is held. - Only the re-encoding was serialized, so two updates could interleave their check and write. One permit now covers an update from its first read to its write. Also: the route shares the cached bytes with the response instead of copying them per request, and answers 304 to a weak validator (`W/"…"`). New tests: a logo whose document is well over the default 64 KiB bound is accepted through the HTTPS door (the task's own `maxDocumentBytes` applies); a payload without `image` is refused and removes nothing; the repair cases above; weak validators. Signed-off-by: Geoff Turk * build(vti-specs-vtc): re-pin vtc/community/logo/update/0.1 after its schema edit trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1324 moved two member descriptions in the schema so the TypeScript library generates `LogoMediaType` once. The wire shape is unchanged, but the bundle's bytes are not, so its digest moves from sha256:8998873230… to sha256:344dc73d9c5f…. The generated Rust types are the same. Signed-off-by: Geoff Turk * fix(vtc-service): conform the community logo to the published logo/update and logo/show specs Re-pins vtc/community/logo/update/0.1 to the bundle tt-tf #1324 published (it changed in place as a draft) and pins vtc/community/logo/show/0.1. - Removal is `remove: true`, never `image: null` (update item 6); the console sends it. - Every LogoRef names `url`, the absolute https address under `public_url`, the same across updates (item 9); omitted when there is no https public URL. - Serve vtc/community/logo/show/0.1 to any caller, with the bytes on `includeData` (show items 1-4). - Build both responses as the generated types, not a hand-written mirror. - One in-memory snapshot answers the route, the public profile, the portal and logo/show; invalidated by an update and by a backup import. A 304 touches no store, and a logo whose bytes do not match its record is neither served nor advertised, so pages fall back to `logoUrl`. - An update landing between the record and bytes reads is read again instead of answering 404 and logging a mismatch. - The route is `public, no-cache` with the digest ETag: one URL, revalidated. - An audit write failure refuses as `unavailable` (item 7); audit-first order kept and documented, since the converse could leave an unaudited change. - One record read per update; the duplicate byte bound is gone. - The Logo card shares the console's public-profile query. body:
Bumps [aws-lc-rs](https://github.com/aws/aws-lc-rs) from 1.18.2 to 1.19.0.
Release notes

Sourced from aws-lc-rs's releases.

aws-lc-rs v1.19.0

What's Changed

  • Add AES OFB, CFB8, and CFB1 modes by @​lokeswarivejju in aws/aws-lc-rs#1259
    • Adds OperatingMode::OFB, OperatingMode::CFB8, and OperatingMode::CFB1 for AES-128, AES-192, and AES-256 through both the one-shot and streaming cipher APIs.
  • Add an on-demand AWS-LC self-test API by @​Elvrarin in aws/aws-lc-rs#1262
    • Adds aws_lc_rs::try_fips_self_test(), allowing applications to re-run all AWS-LC cryptographic algorithm self-tests without calling the sys crate through unsafe FFI. This does not re-run the module integrity test.
  • Add Keccak-256 digest support behind "unstable" feature flag by @​fabrice102 in aws/aws-lc-rs#1266
    • Adds aws_lc_rs::unstable::digest::KECCAK256 and KECCAK256_OUTPUT_LEN behind the unstable feature for use with the existing digest::digest and digest::Context APIs.
  • Add configurable RSA-PSS salt lengths by @​PaulDance in aws/aws-lc-rs#1267
    • Adds RsaPssSaltLength::{Digest, Max, Custom} and with_pss_salt_length builders on RsaSignatureEncoding and RsaParameters, covering signing and verification for both message and precomputed-digest APIs.
  • Implement Clone for signing key pairs by @​JakeHuneau in aws/aws-lc-rs#1277
    • rsa::KeyPair, EcdsaKeyPair, Ed25519KeyPair, and PqdsaKeyPair can now be cloned directly rather than wrapped in an Arc.
    • Clones share the immutable, reference-counted EVP_PKEY; key material is not duplicated, and a clone remains usable after the original is dropped.

Upstream AWS-LC

  • aws-lc-sys v0.47.0 aligns with AWS-LC v5.12.0 (previously v5.11.0).
  • aws-lc-fips-sys v0.14.4 updates its bundled AWS-LC FIPS 4.2.0 snapshot with recent FIPS 4.x backports.

Build Improvements

  • Lower the minimum system-installed AWS-LC version to 4.2.0 by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1268
    • The default aws-lc-sys system-library path now accepts AWS-LC 4.2.0 or newer, previously 5.7.0, allowing use of a FIPS 4.x system library.
    • Enabling the unstable feature requires AWS-LC 5.7.0 or newer because unstable APIs currently include Keccak-256. Bundled-source builds are unaffected.
  • Share cc compiler detection across builds by @​johncarmack1984 in aws/aws-lc-rs#1273
    • Reuses compiler detection results across the main library build and compiler feature probes, reducing repeated compiler invocations during cold builds.

Updates `korthout/backport-action` from 4.7.0 to 4.7.1
Release notes

Sourced from korthout/backport-action's releases.

Backport-action v4.7.1

What's Changed

Thanks to a contribution by @​jrasm91, backports no longer fail when you combine auto_merge_enabled: true with experimental.conflict_resolution: draft_commit_conflicts. Previously, when a cherry-pick conflicted, the action created the draft backport pull request and then tried to enable auto-merge on it. GitHub doesn't allow auto-merging of drafts, so the backport was reported as an unexpected failure, was_successful was false, and the draft backport pull request didn't receive instructions on how to resolve the conflict.

Now the action doesn't attempt auto-merge on a draft backport pull request and logs it. The backport is reported as drafted with conflicts, and the draft receives the conflict-resolution instructions as usual. With comment_style: summary, that looks like this:

Target Status
stable/8.7 :warning: Drafted with conflicts #612

Auto-merge stays off for the draft. You can enable it once you've resolved the conflicts.

  • Skip auto-merge for draft backport pull requests by @​jrasm91 in korthout/backport-action#793, backported in korthout/backport-action#797

title: chore(deny): ignore the chrono, chrono-tz and humantime unmaintained notices
body:
RustSec published three "unmaintained" advisories on 2026-11-17, and Cargo Deny now fails on every PR (first seen on #616):

| Advisory | Crate | Reached through |
|---|---|---|
| RUSTSEC-2026-0543 | chrono 0.4.45 | direct dependency, and affinidi-*, didwebvh-rs, dtg-credentials, did-git-sign, … |
| RUSTSEC-2026-0555 | chrono-tz 0.10.4 | chrono |
| RUSTSEC-2026-0542 | humantime 2.4.0 | dev graph only: affinidi-messaging-mediator (test mediator) |

None reports a vulnerability; each says the crate is unmaintained and that no safe upgrade exists. Moving off chrono is an ecosystem-wide change (every SDK in the graph uses it), so they are ignored in both `deny.toml` and `.cargo/audit.toml` (kept in step, per #572), with a re-check point: the next SDK bump, or when chronotope/chrono#1768 names a successor.

`cargo deny check advisories`: ok locally.

Applies to `release/0.7` too (same crates), so labelled for backport.

title: chore(deny): accept the chrono unmaintained advisory (RUSTSEC-2026-0543)
body:
RustSec marked chrono unmaintained on 2026-11-17 ([RUSTSEC-2026-0543](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0543)). Since then the `cargo deny` job has failed on `main` and on every open PR, including #1329.

The advisory is status only: every version is affected, there is no fixed release, and no vulnerability is reported. chrono can't be removed from this repo alone:
- it is in the libraries' public API (`issuedAt` and `expiresAt` are `chrono::DateTime<Utc>`), so dropping it means a breaking release of every library;
- it also comes in through `affinidi-data-integrity` and `didwebvh-rs`.

So the advisory is accepted by ID in `deny.toml`, with the reason and the condition for removing it: a migration to `jiff` or `time` here and in affinidi-tdk-rs. `unused-ignored-advisory = "deny"` makes the check fail once chrono has left the graph, which forces the entry to be removed.

This matches OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2759. After this change, a local `cargo deny check` passes (advisories, bans, licenses, sources).

title: perf: use jemalloc in every service binary so freed memory returns to the OS
body:
The service binaries ran on the system allocator. glibc malloc keeps freed
pages in its arenas instead of returning them, so a service's RSS ratchets
up to its high-water mark and stays there; on a memory graph that is
indistinguishable from a leak (the VTC in particular has been climbing).

vtc, vta, vta-enclave, vti-witness, room-host and vti-voting-service now
set tikv-jemallocator as the global allocator behind a default-on
`jemalloc` feature (non-MSVC only), matching the mediator. jemalloc is
tuned through the exported `_rjem_malloc_conf` symbol:
background_thread:true (purge while idle) and 5s dirty/muzzy decay.
The symbol must carry the `_rjem_` prefix tikv-jemalloc-sys builds with;
an unprefixed `malloc_conf` is silently ignored.

Both Dockerfiles build with --no-default-features, so they append
`jemalloc` to FEATURES for every profile. Each crate now carries the
deny-not-forbid unsafe_code lint table for the one exported static, and
is listed in scripts/check-workspace-lints.py.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

Verified locally that jemalloc only reads the prefixed symbol: an invalid option exported as `_rjem_malloc_conf` triggers `<jemalloc>: Invalid conf pair`, while the same option exported as `malloc_conf` is never read. The mediator has the unprefixed name, and a separate PR fixes it.

title: feat(push-gateway): use jemalloc so freed memory returns to the OS
body:
Makes the long-running `vti-push-gateway` binary use jemalloc as its global allocator, so freed memory is returned to the OS.

## Why

With the system allocator (glibc malloc on Linux), the process keeps the arenas behind its short-lived buffers (messages, frames, request/response bodies) instead of returning them. RSS ratchets up to its high-water mark and never comes back down, which reads as a leak on a memory graph even though the live heap is flat. jemalloc's decay-based purging returns those pages, so RSS tracks live memory.

## What

Mirrors `affinidi-messaging-mediator`:

- A default-on `jemalloc` feature (`dep:tikv-jemallocator`), with the dependency under `[target.'cfg(not(target_env = "msvc"))'.dependencies]`. MSVC builds and `--no-default-features` builds fall back to the system allocator.
- `#[global_allocator]` is set in `main.rs` only, never in a library crate, so no consumer has an allocator imposed on it.
- jemalloc tuning is exported as `_rjem_malloc_conf`: `background_thread:true,dirty_decay_ms:5000,muzzy_decay_ms:5000`. The prefixed name is required because `tikv-jemalloc-sys` builds jemalloc with `--with-jemalloc-prefix=_rjem_`, so an unprefixed `malloc_conf` export links fine but jemalloc ignores it. The value is typed `&[u8; 63]`, a thin pointer that matches C's `const char *`, rather than a `&[u8]` fat pointer.

No Dockerfile in this repo. Checked locally with `cargo clippy --bins`; the built binary defines `_rjem_malloc_conf`.

| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.12.0` → `0.12.1` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `verify-go` builds, vets and tests, then `publish-go` pushes the
  tag, which *is* the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `verify-dart` checks each package against the *published* core,
  `tag-dart` pushes the tag, and `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: chore(deny): accept chrono-family unmaintained and nitro_attest zip advisories
body:
RustSec published status-only "unmaintained" advisories on 2026-11-17 for chrono (RUSTSEC-2026-0543) and, as a consequence, humantime (RUSTSEC-2026-0542) and chrono-tz (RUSTSEC-2026-0555). No vulnerability is reported and no fixed release exists; chrono is used across our workspaces and the affinidi-tdk stack, so it cannot leave the graph from any one repo. Each is accepted by ID with a reason and a removal condition (migration to jiff/time). This turns cargo-deny's advisories check green again, which currently fails on main and on every open PR.

Also accepts two zip 2.x vulnerabilities, RUSTSEC-2026-0545 (AES authentication code) and RUSTSEC-2026-0548 (ZipStreamReader header names), on the same sole path as the existing RUSTSEC-2026-0367 ignore: nitro_attest 0.2.0's build script. It builds zip with only the deflate feature, so the aes-crypto code is not compiled, and it reads one SHA-256-pinned entry with ZipArchive::by_name, never ZipStreamReader. nitro_attest requires zip ^2; these are dropped together with RUSTSEC-2026-0367.
author: stormer78
significance_reasons: Security, privacy, threat, or vulnerability relevance

title: ci(deny): record the chrono, chrono-tz, humantime and zip advisories published today
body:
cargo-deny is a required check and fails every PR on five advisories new
to the database:

- RUSTSEC-2026-0543 chrono, RUSTSEC-2026-0555 chrono-tz and
  RUSTSEC-2026-0542 humantime are informational (unmaintained), with no
  patched release. chrono is used by 36 workspace crates and exposed in
  the APIs of the TDK, messaging, data-integrity and didwebvh-rs crates,
  so moving to jiff or time is a cross-repo migration; chrono-tz comes
  only through regorus and humantime only through the embedded test
  mediator.
- RUSTSEC-2026-0545 and RUSTSEC-2026-0548 (zip) are on the same single
  path as the four zip ignores already recorded: nitro_attest's build
  script, which builds zip with only deflate (no AES) and reads one
  SHA-256-pinned archive through ZipArchive, never ZipStreamReader.

Each entry says when to drop it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(vtc/community/logo): add vtc/community/logo/update/0.1 and vtc/community/logo/show/0.1
body:
## What and why

Adds `vtc/community/logo/update/0.1`: an administrator hands the community a new logo, which the community re-encodes, strips of metadata and stores in place of the one it holds. `image: null` removes it. The answer is the stored re-encoding's digest, media type, size and dimensions.

A VTC's console, member portal, sign-in pages and landing page are served with `img-src 'self' data:`, so a logo named by the profile's `logoUrl` at another host is never drawn. A community with nowhere on its own origin to put a file (a hosted deployment, say) had no logo at all. This task lets it store one and serve it itself. It does not change `logoUrl`, which stays an address for readers that fetch from anywhere.

Security choices the conformance list holds:

- **Raster types only** (PNG, JPEG, WebP), in the schema rather than a check a consumer might skip. An SVG served from the community's origin is a document that can run script there, so a client rasterizes an SVG before sending it.
- **Administrator standing is checked before decoding.** Bytes are bounded before decoding, and pixels and decode memory while decoding.
- **Re-encoding.** The image is decoded strictly as its declared type, never sniffed, and stored as the community's own encoding with all metadata and trailing bytes dropped, at most 512 px on the longer side, lossless preferred. The received bytes are never stored or served.
- **Per-signer rate limit, and audit by digest**, refusing an unaudited change.
- **Serving over HTTP**: exactly the stored bytes and type, with `nosniff`, no credential and no cookie, because sign-in pages draw it.

There is no `dryRun` and no `show` task: unlike the theme there is no profile to check against, and the community's HTTP route is the read.

The implementation is OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2751, which pins this version and cannot merge until a release publishes it.

## Checklist

- [x] Every commit is DCO signed (`git commit -s`).
- [x] The title is a conventional commit; any `!` is scoped to the package whose API breaks.
- [x] If `specs/` changed: all four libraries are regenerated (`npm run regen`) and committed.
- [x] No package version and no `CHANGELOG.md` entry is edited — the Release PR does both.
- [x] `npm run check` passes, and the tests for the code touched were run.

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) and [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](../docs/DEVELOPMENT.md).

title: fix(vtc-service): vtc setup finds a TSP-only VTA's mediator
body:
`vtc setup` against a VTA that advertises only `TSPTransport` said the VTA's DID document did not advertise a DIDComm mediator.

**Cause:** `ResolvedVta` already carries `tsp_mediator_did` and `mediator_did` separately, but the wizard passed only `mediator_did` (DIDComm) to the mediator prompt. `connect_setup_client` (the did-hosting picker) had the same gap: without REST it tried only DIDComm.

**Fix** (`vtc-service/src/setup/wizard.rs`):
- `vta_mediator()` suggests the TSP entry's mediator first, then the DIDComm entry's; one mediator for both is reported for both. The prompt names the transports (`Use the VTA's mediator (did:…, TSP)`), and its wording no longer assumes DIDComm.
- `connect_setup_client` tries REST, then TSP (`VtaClient::connect_tsp`, under `feature = "tsp"`), then DIDComm.

**Tests:** four unit tests for the suggestion (TSP-only, DIDComm-only, dual, neither). `setup::wizard` 24/24 pass; `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -D warnings` clean.

Not changed: the "transports to advertise" prompt still pre-selects TSP + DIDComm (deliberate default per its doc comment).

Unrelated, pre-existing on `main`: `vtc-service` does not build without the `tsp` feature (`routes/mod.rs`, `registry/messaging.rs`).
author: stormer78

title: fix(vtc-service): vtc setup finds a TSP-only VTA's mediator (#2755)
body:
fix(vtc-service): vtc setup finds a TSP-only VTA's mediator (#2755)

The setup wizard suggested only the mediator from the VTA's
`DIDCommMessaging` service, so a VTA advertising only `TSPTransport` was
reported as having no mediator. The suggestion now reads the TSP entry
first and the DIDComm entry second (TSP > DIDComm), naming the transports
the VTA uses it for, and the prompt's wording is transport-neutral.

The did-hosting picker's connect had the same gap: without REST it tried
only DIDComm. It now connects over TSP before DIDComm.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: fix: rooms, repos, elections and vetting oddities kept as-is by #614
body:
#614 turned Vetting, Rooms, Elections and Repos into a pure plan plus an effect runner. It kept some odd behaviour as it was, pinned by runtime-harness tests, and listed it for a follow-up. This PR fixes every item on that list except one, which on closer reading is not a bug (item 16). Items 1–9 were the first round; items 10–18 cover the rest of the list. The rule throughout: a failure undoes exactly the book changes made for that attempt, and the status line shows the real reason.

Each commit that changes behaviour also changes the pinning test that locked in the old behaviour. **That test change is the point of the commit**, and each commit message says so. Where no test covered a path, a new one is added.

## 1. Rooms, Accept: the reason was hidden (`85403ed`)
- **Before:** when the key lookup or the build failed, `Refusal::AcceptBusy` was shown over the real reason. The person saw "Rooms already in progress" when the lane was free.
- **After:** the reason is shown. The busy note appears only when the lane is busy (`Sent::Busy`).
- **Test:** `an_accept_whose_key_lookup_fails_shows_the_busy_message` is now `an_accept_whose_key_lookup_fails_shows_the_reason`.

## 2. Rooms, Accept while a request is outstanding (`e1eeb04`)
- **Before:** the flow was set to `Collecting` with nothing sent, and it stayed stuck there.
- **After:** the press is refused, matching Elections, which refuses a press while `pending` is set and changes nothing. Nothing is set, and the status says "A request to this community is still waiting — try again when it answers." The same press works once the earlier request answers.
- **Tests:**
  - `an_accept_while_waiting_is_refused_and_can_be_pressed_again` (runtime; it also checks the retry).
  - `an_accept_while_waiting_is_refused_with_nothing_set` (plan).

## 3. Rooms gave up nothing; now it gives up as Elections does (`d0c0b43`)
- **Before:** a `Next` whose key lookup or build failed returned not-taken. It was retried, and its error rewritten, on every tick.
- **After:** a failure the view shows counts as taken, as in Elections. The reason stays on screen and nothing is retried until the person acts again.
- **Test:** `a_page_step_whose_key_lookup_fails_is_kept` is now `..._is_given_up`. It also checks that a second tick neither retries the step nor rewrites the status.

## 4. Repos: a failing link poll (`f73ad76`, `9b7289d`)
- **Before:**
  - A poll whose key lookup failed repeated its error on every five-second sweep.
  - A poll whose send failed, or that went unanswered, was retried every 5 s and said nothing.
- **After:**
  - `LinkFlow` counts failures in a row. Each one doubles the poll interval: 5 → 10 → 20 → 40 → 60 s, capped at `LINK_POLL_MAX_INTERVAL` (R1.4). The attempt's own `expires_at` still limits how long polling goes on.
  - A failure is said only when it differs from the last one said. An answer resets both the backoff and the "already said" record.
  - Send failures and lost polls now say so once ("couldn't check the link with the community: …" / "no answer to the link check within 30s …"), where they said nothing before (R6.5).
  - The panel shows the current interval.
- **Tests:**
  - Updated: `a_due_link_poll_whose_key_lookup_fails_says_so_once_and_backs_off` and `a_due_link_poll_is_sent_on_the_sweep_beside_a_pending_change`.
  - New: `a_failing_poll_backs_off_to_a_cap_and_an_answer_resets_it`, `a_repeated_poll_failure_is_said_once` and `a_lost_poll_is_said_once_and_backs_off`.

## 5. Vetting `request_vetter`: the prepared request stayed after a build failure (`d5c91ce`)
- **Before:** `prepare_request` recorded the request. A failed document build then gave up without forgetting it.
- **After:** the abort, with `Undo::ForgetUnsent`, is built right after the request is prepared. The build failure applies that same abort, as the signing and send failures already did.
- **Test:** new `a_request_that_fails_before_it_goes_out_leaves_nothing_prepared`. The harness can't reach a build failure, because the builder does not fail on valid input.

## 6. Vetting `ask_for_challenge`: the question stayed filed (`83616ba`)
- **Before:** the `PcsChallenge` question stayed filed when the signing failed, and expired only when its reply window ran out.
- **After:** the abort un-files it, as the send-failure outcome already did.
- **Test:** `a_challenge_without_keys_gives_up_and_leaves_its_question_filed` is now `..._and_unfiles_its_question`. The plan test's abort assertion is updated too.

## 7. Vetting `attest_hidden` with no VTA said "busy" (`5da2a50`)
- **Before:** with no admin VTA session, the PCS job's refusal said that hidden-vetting work was already in progress.
- **After:** the plan checks the session first and says "A hidden attestation is made by your VTA, and it is not connected — attest again once it is. Nothing was sent; the request stays open." This keeps "not connected" apart from "busy" (R6.4).
- **Other vetting paths:** none of them shows the busy message when the VTA is missing. The face plans already check `connected` before `claimable`.
- **Test:** the plan test now also covers the no-VTA case.

## 8. Runs of spaces from a missing `\` (`ea131af`)
#614 named the recovery mismatch message. A search of both crates found six instances of the same mistake, with gaps of 14–26 spaces:
- `vetting_actions/pcs.rs`: the recovery message.
- `identity_panel.rs`: "worlds apart".
- `join_flow.rs`: three wallet messages.
- `join_flow/driver.rs`: the directory-disclosure failure.

All six are fixed.
- **Test:** new `openvtc/tests/string_literals.rs`. It scans both crates for a run of more than 12 spaces inside a string literal, between a word and a lowercase letter. The widest deliberate column alignment, in `health_cmd`, is 12 spaces. The test fails on the old text.

## 9. #614's other vetting items
**Book changes left after a signing or build failure:**
- **`open_session`** (`2f04268`):
  - **Before:** the session the book opened stayed in memory, unsaved, when the key lookup, signing, keeping or build failed. Separately, the community stayed in `requirements_requested` when the requirements question never went out, so the next Enter opened the session without the requirements.
  - **After:** every abort restores the desk entry (`Undo::RestoreDesk`). `Followup::SessionKept` carries the snapshot for the send. A new `Undo::NotRequested` takes back the "asked" mark.
  - **Tests:** `opening_a_session_without_keys_leaves_it_open_and_unsaved` is now `..._puts_the_request_back`. `..._before_the_requirements_without_keys_gives_up_unsent` now asserts the mark is taken back. The plan test applies each abort.
- **`decline` / `withdraw` build failure** (`bb7319d`):
  - **Before:** the request stayed declined, or the statement withdrawn.
  - **After:** the same undo used for signing and send failures is applied.
  - **Test:** the decline plan test applies its abort. The harness can't reach this failure.
- **Hidden-vetting questions:**
  - **Enrolment and draw** (`2907ee0`): `SendOrSay` now carries an undo list. An enrolment forgets its `PcsRoot` question. A draw forgets its `PcsTokens` question and its in-flight record (new `Undo::NotDrawing`). `enrol_asked_at` stays, as on a send failure: the VTA holds the request it built either way, and asking again within the wait would replace it.
    - **Tests:** `an_enrolment_without_keys_is_said_and_left_filed` is now `..._and_unfiled`, and `a_draw_without_keys_is_said_and_left_in_flight` is now `..._and_not_left_in_flight`. `the_answers_are_taken_in_order_and_a_failure_stops_none_after_it` is updated.
  - **Binding question** (`5cc8f33`): `Asked::Binding` now forgets its question on failure. The key check keeps its asked time, so the question is not asked again before `BINDING_REASK`.
    - **Test:** `a_binding_question_without_keys_says_so_and_stays_asked` is now `..._and_is_unfiled`.

**One status line covering another:**
- **`start_application` while busy** (`5816e09`):
  - **Before:** the busy warning replaced "Application started.", although the application was saved.
  - **After:** `Followup::Started` carries the start's message. On a busy domain the status says both: the application started, and its requirements wait until the other send finishes (`m` asks then).
  - **Tests:** `starting_an_application_while_busy_saves_it_and_asks_nothing` is now `..._and_says_its_requirements_wait`. The plan test `the_started_followup_selects_the_row_then_plans_the_refresh` is updated.
- **`RefreshRequirements` while busy** (`e6aa851`):
  - **Before:** the challenge's progress note covered the busy refusal.
  - **After:** `ask_for_challenge(…, announce)` is passed `false` when the refresh just said a warning or an error. The challenge is still asked, without a progress note.
  - **Tests:** `a_challenge_is_asked_even_while_a_persons_send_holds_the_domain` is now `a_challenge_asked_while_busy_leaves_the_busy_refusal_said`. The plan test covers a quiet ask.
- **`DrawNow`** (`d32eb4e`):
  - **Before:** the per-community info summary covered whatever the pass had said, including errors.
  - **After:** a new `Step::Summary` shows its status unless the steps before it in the run left a warning or an error.
  - **Tests:** a unit test of the rule, and a runtime test, `drawing_by_hand_leaves_a_failure_of_the_pass_said`, that fails with the old `Step::Status`.

## 10. Rooms: a refresh on a busy lane said nothing (`c2fd91c`)
- **Before:** opening the panel, or pressing `r`, on a busy Rooms lane read nothing and said nothing. An empty panel stayed on "asking the community…" indefinitely.
- **After:** the memberships read carries `Refusal::Record`, a warning that names the busy lane and says to press `r` once it finishes. The loading screen now shows the status line.
- **Test:** `a_refresh_on_a_busy_lane_sends_nothing_and_says_nothing` is now `..._and_says_the_lane_is_busy`.

## 11. Rooms: `Next::Renew` with no VTA was kept for ever (`a12da39`)
- **Before:** with no VTA session, the renew step planned an `Ask` that could never be dispatched, so it was kept and retried every tick.
- **After:** with no VTA, the step and its renewals are dropped. Every read once a VTA is connected collects them again.
- **Test:** `a_renew_step_without_a_vta_is_kept` is now `..._is_dropped`.

## 12. Elections: a show on a busy lane reset the earlier target (`3708823`)
- **Before:** `plan_show` called `reset_target()` and cleared `shown` before the send. A press refused on a busy lane still lost the target and the presented membership.
- **After:** the new target, and the notification it was opened from, travel in `Commit::Showing { target, opening }` and are applied only once the read is claimed.
- **Tests:**
  - `a_show_on_a_busy_lane_stays_on_the_list` is now `..._and_keeps_its_target`, asserting both stay.
  - New plan test `a_show_keeps_the_earlier_target_until_its_read_is_under_way`.

## 13. Elections: a list refresh on a busy lane (`447e6bd`)
- **Setting `notified_due` is right, and stays.** The held notifications are read from the VTA on a lane of their own, so a busy community lane is no reason to skip them.
- **What was wrong** is the silent refusal of the list read, the same as item 10. It now carries `Refusal::ListBusy`, and the loading screen shows the status line.
- **Test:** `an_open_on_a_busy_lane_sends_nothing_and_says_nothing` is now `..._and_says_the_lane_is_busy`. It also asserts the notifications are still due.

## 14. Repos: disk I/O on the loop (`efc71c7`)
- **Before:** `SettingsSubmit` checked the root directory and wrote the settings file on the event loop. `open` read the file there too.
- **After:**
  - Saving is now `Work::Settings`, a workspace job on the GitWorkspace lane.
    - The plan refuses only what it can tell without the disk: an empty or relative root.
    - The job checks the directory and writes the file on the blocking pool. Its outcome closes the form, or puts the error on it.
    - As a job, a save is refused while another workspace job runs, since that job may be writing the same file.
  - `open` reads the file with `spawn_blocking`. The loop still awaits this one small local read, as it already awaits the persona key lookup beside it.
- **Tests:**
  - New: `settings_are_saved_by_a_job_and_a_clone_needs_a_target` (plan), `the_settings_job_writes_the_file_or_says_why_not` (the job, in a temp directory) and `saving_the_settings_while_a_job_runs_is_refused` (runtime).
  - No runtime test drove the save before: the harness avoided the disk.

## 15. Repos: the settings-read warning on open was cleared at once (`fe78a6c`)
- **Before:** opening noted "couldn't read the workspace settings, using the defaults", then ran `Step::Reading`, which clears the status line. The warning was never seen.
- **After:** the workspace open returns the warning (`fill`), and the runner shows it after the open's steps.
- **Test:** new unit test `opening_returns_a_settings_warning_rather_than_saying_it`. The harness does not touch the profile's settings file.

## 16. Repos: key lookup before the busy check (not changed: not a bug)
I'm leaving this as it is, for three reasons:
- **It is local and cheap.** The key lookup reads the TDK's local secrets, with no network.
- **It is the shared design.** The community-request engine Rooms and Elections use does the same on purpose, and documents it: "a persona whose key cannot be read is told so even on a busy lane".
- **It gives the more useful answer.** A key that cannot be read is a lasting fault that "busy" would hide. Busy is transient and is said once the key is good.

With item 4, a quiet link poll that fails this way is now said once and backs off, so it no longer repeats.

## 17. Vetting: failures not logged (`d247f6e`)
- **Before:** an enrolment or draw that `SendOrSay` could not sign or send, and a binding question that failed (`Asked::Binding`), were said on the status line only. The next status erased them.
- **After:** they also go to the activity log, with a tracing warning (R6.5).
- **Tests:** `an_enrolment_without_keys_is_said_and_unfiled` and `a_binding_question_without_keys_says_so_and_is_unfiled` asserted *not logged*; they now assert logged. The draw test asserts it too.

## 18. Vetting: `application_context` not saved (`e81db95`)
- **Before:** `application_context` derived the application's VTA context and wrote it to the book before the busy check, with no save. A refused press left an unsaved change, and a used one was never written until something else saved.
- **After:**
  - `application_context` is pure. It returns `AppContext { id, join_did, derived }`.
  - The face plans keep a derived context (`keep_context`) only after the busy check, and put a `Step::MarkDirty` in the effect.
  - A card whose key lookup fails takes back a context kept for that card (`Undo::NoContext`).
  - The PCS work plan keeps the context as before; its answers are saved when they settle.
- **Tests:**
  - The busy face tests and `a_card_while_busy_derives_the_context_and_sends_nothing` (now `..._keeps_no_context_...`) assert no context is kept.
  - The started face and card tests now assert a pending save.
  - `sending_a_card_without_keys_gives_up_unsent` asserts the context is taken back.
  - Plan tests updated: `a_face_plan_on_a_busy_domain_is_refused_and_keeps_no_context` and `choosing_a_face_plans_the_list_read`.

`5c3e5e9` is clippy only: Rooms' `Refusal` variants lose their shared `Busy` suffix, plus a `?` and a struct initialiser.

## User-visible changes
Each item has a CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` → Fixed entry. In short:
- **Rooms:**
  - An acceptance that cannot start says why.
  - Accepting while a request is unanswered is refused clearly instead of getting stuck.
  - A failing follow-on step shows its reason once instead of every tick.
- **Repos:** a failing forge-link check is reported once and backs off to 60 s. Send failures and lost polls are now said.
- **Vetting:**
  - No leftover requests, sessions, declines, withdrawals or filed questions after a failure.
  - "Application started." survives a busy refusal.
  - The busy refusal survives the challenge request.
  - "Get tokens" no longer hides a failure.
  - A hidden attestation with no VTA says "not connected".
- **Text:** six messages lose a long run of spaces.
- **Busy lanes:** a refresh on a busy Rooms or Elections lane says the lane is busy, including on the loading screen. Opening an election on a busy lane no longer loses the earlier target.
- **Repos settings:** saving runs as a workspace job, refused while another job runs, and an unreadable settings file is reported when the panel opens.
- **Activity log:** hidden-vetting enrolment, draw and key-binding failures are logged.
- **Faces:** an application's VTA context chosen for a face is saved, and only once the job goes ahead.

## Not changed
- **Repos, key lookup before the busy check:** not a bug; see item 16.
- **Everything else** in #614's "odd behaviour pinned and preserved" list is fixed above.

## Tests (`cargo test --workspace --locked`)
| | passed | ignored |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (c6a2bde), default | 2709 | 37 |
| this branch, default | 2721 | 37 |
| this branch, `--no-default-features` | 2721 | 37 |
| this branch, `-- --include-ignored` | 2758 | 0 |

Also verified on the tip, with stable 1.100:
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- clippy `-D warnings`: default, `--no-default-features`, and `-p openvtc --features dev-overrides`
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`
- `cargo machete`

No `backport release/0.7` label: the reducer and effect code these fixes change exists only on `main`.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)
- [x] No new `reqwest::Client::new()` or bare `fetch()`; all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). No new clients.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3). None added.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). This PR removes cases of it: every in-memory book change made for an attempt is undone when the attempt fails before it goes out. Where a pre-send save had already run (decline, withdraw, session send), the undo lands before that coalesced save writes, so disk matches.
- [x] Every retry is bounded and backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4):
  - The Repos link poll now backs off exponentially, capped at 60 s, and the attempt's expiry limits it.
  - Rooms no longer retries a failed step every tick.
  - Rooms no longer retries a renew step every tick with no VTA.
  - **Deviation:** the link poll backoff has no jitter. It is one client polling its own link attempt, so there is no herd to spread.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). The link poll keeps polling through failures, with backoff.
- [x] Acks and deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). N/A.
- [x] New or changed wire types: camelCase, `deny_unknown_fields` where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers updated (R3.*). No wire changes.
- [x] Config absence means the most restrictive interpretation; fail closed (R5.*). Unchanged.
- [x] Logs and status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*):
  - R6.4: hidden attestation "not connected" vs "busy", and Rooms Accept's reason vs "busy".
  - R6.5: link-poll send failures and lost polls are now said, and hidden-vetting send failures are logged.
  - R6.4: a busy Rooms or Elections refresh says the lane is busy, instead of saying nothing.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1):
  - Every undo is in memory and runs in the same loop turn as the failure.
  - The face context is now kept only after the busy check, with a save scheduled.
  - The settings save is atomic in `save_to` and happens in the job.
  - Nothing persisted moves earlier.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: R1.4, no jitter on the link poll backoff (above).

title: fix: rooms, repos, elections and vetting oddities kept as-is by #614 (#615)
body:
fix: rooms, repos, elections and vetting oddities kept as-is by #614 (#615)

* fix(rooms): an acceptance that cannot start shows the real reason

On a key-lookup or build failure, Accept showed the busy note over the
reason. The busy refusal is now shown only for a busy lane.

The pinning test an_accept_whose_key_lookup_fails_shows_the_busy_message
locked in the old behaviour from #614; it is renamed and now asserts the
reason is shown. Changing that test is the point of this commit.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(rooms): refuse an acceptance while a request is unanswered

Accept pressed while the view still waited on an earlier request set the
flow to Collecting with nothing sent, leaving it stuck. It is now refused,
as Elections refuses the same case: nothing is set and the status says to
try again when the request answers.

The pinning tests an_accept_while_waiting_leaves_the_acceptance_set and
an_accept_while_waiting_is_planned_with_nothing_to_send locked in the old
behaviour from #614; they now assert the refusal, and the runtime test
also checks that the same press starts the acceptance once the earlier
request is answered. Changing them is the point of this commit.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(rooms): give up a step whose key lookup fails, as Elections does

A Next whose key lookup or build failed returned not-taken, so the loop
kept it and retried it, rewriting the error, on every tick. A failure the
view shows now counts as taken: the reason stays and nothing is retried
until the person acts again.

The pinning test a_page_step_whose_key_lookup_fails_is_kept locked in the
old behaviour from #614; it is renamed ..._is_given_up and now asserts the
step is dropped and a second tick neither retries it nor rewrites the
status. Changing it is the point of this commit.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(repos): report a failing link poll once and back it off

A link-status poll whose key lookup failed rewrote its error on every
five-second sweep, and one whose send failed or went unanswered was
retried on the floor interval silently. Each failure in a row now doubles
the poll interval up to 60 s (R1.4; the attempt's own expiry bounds the
polling), and a failure is said on the status line only when it differs
from the last one said; an answer resets both. The panel shows the
current interval.

The pinning tests a_due_link_poll_whose_key_lookup_fails_says_so and
a_due_link_poll_is_sent_on_the_sweep_beside_a_pending_change locked in
the old behaviour from #614; they now assert the failure is said once and
the poll backs off. Changing them is the point of this commit. New unit
tests cover the backoff cap, the once-only reporting and a lost poll.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vetting): forget a prepared request whose document fails to build

request_vetter prepared the request in the book, then gave up without
undoing it when the document build failed; only a signing or send failure
forgot it. The plan now builds the abort once, right after the request is
prepared, and applies the same abort on a build failure. Abort::apply is
callable from a plan for this, and takes any Display error.

No pinning test covered the build failure (the builder does not fail on
valid input, so the harness cannot reach it). A new unit test applies the
abort the plan returns and checks the prepared request is gone.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vetting): un-file a challenge question whose signing fails

ask_for_challenge filed its PcsChallenge question before signing and left
it filed when the key lookup or signing failed, so the book waited on a
question that never went out until the reply window expired. Its abort now
forgets the question, as the send-failure outcome already did.

The pinning test a_challenge_without_keys_gives_up_and_leaves_its_question_filed
and the plan test's abort assertion locked in the old behaviour from #614;
they now assert the question is un-filed. Changing them is the point of
this commit.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vetting): say the VTA is not connected when attesting hidden without one

attest_hidden with no admin VTA session fell through to the PCS job's
refusal, which says the hidden-vetting domain is busy. R6.4: an operator
must be able to tell unreachable from busy. The plan now checks the
session first and says the VTA is not connected; the busy message stays
for a busy domain. No other vetting path shows the busy message when the
VTA is missing (the face plans already check the session first).

No pinning test covered this path; the plan test now also asserts the
no-VTA refusal.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix: drop the runs of spaces a missing line continuation left in six messages

A string literal wrapped across lines without its trailing backslash keeps
the next line's indentation inside the message (rustfmt later joined each
onto one line, leaving a 14-26 space gap mid-sentence). #614 named the
hidden-vetting recovery mismatch; a search of both crates found five more:
the identity panel's shared-value warning, three wallet join messages and
the unreadable directory-disclosure failure.

New integration test openvtc/tests/string_literals.rs scans both crates'
sources for a run of spaces longer than any deliberate column alignment
inside a literal, between a word and a lowercase letter, so the mistake
cannot come back unnoticed.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vetting): undo an unsent session and an unsent requirements question

open_session opened the session in the book before signing and kept it
when the key lookup, signing, keeping or send failed, leaving the request
in an unsaved session nobody received. Each of those aborts, and a build
failure, now restores the desk entry to where it stood
(Undo::RestoreDesk; SessionKept carries the snapshot for the send).

When the session first asks the community what it requires, the page
marked the community as asked before signing and kept the mark when the
question never went, so the next Enter opened the session without the
requirements. A new Undo::NotRequested takes the mark back on failure.

The pinning tests opening_a_session_without_keys_leaves_it_open_and_unsaved
and opening_a_session_before_the_requirements_without_keys_gives_up_unsent
locked in the old behaviour from #614; they now assert the request and the
mark are put back. Changing them is the point of this commit. The plan
test also checks each abort and applies it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vetting): undo a decline or withdrawal whose document fails to build

plan_decline and plan_withdraw changed the book (request declined,
withdrawal recorded) and, if the document build then failed, gave up
without undoing it. Each now builds its undo once, after the book change,
and applies it on a build failure as on a signing or send failure.

No pinning test covered the build failure (the builder does not fail on
valid input); the decline plan test now applies its abort and checks the
request stands where it stood.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vetting): un-file a hidden enrolment or draw whose signing fails

plan_enrolment and plan_draw filed their question (and, for a draw, the
in-flight record) before the signing, and SendOrSay only said the
failure, leaving the book waiting on questions that never went out until
their windows ran out. SendOrSay now carries the undo for its attempt: an
enrolment forgets its PcsRoot question and a draw forgets its PcsTokens
question and in-flight record (new Undo::NotDrawing). An enrolment keeps
enrol_asked_at, as the send-failure path does: the VTA holds the request
it built either way, and asking again inside the wait would replace it.

The pinning tests an_enrolment_without_keys_is_said_and_left_filed,
a_draw_without_keys_is_said_and_left_in_flight and
the_answers_are_taken_in_order_and_a_failure_stops_none_after_it locked in
the old behaviour from #614; they now assert the questions are taken
back. Changing them is the point of this commit.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vetting): keep "Application started." when its requirements wait

start_application saved the application, then the Started followup's
requirements question was refused on the busy vetting domain and the busy
warning replaced "Application started.", reading as though nothing
happened. Followup::Started now carries the start's message, and on a busy
domain the status says both: the application started, and its
requirements wait (m asks once the other send finishes).

The pinning test starting_an_application_while_busy_saves_it_and_asks_nothing
and the plan test the_started_followup_selects_the_row_then_plans_the_refresh
locked in the old behaviour from #614; they now assert the combined
status. Changing them is the point of this commit.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vetting): a challenge request no longer covers a refused refresh

RefreshRequirements runs the requirements question, then the hidden
application's challenge request (unheld, so never refused). When the
requirements were refused as busy, or gave up, the challenge's progress
note replaced that reason. ask_for_challenge now takes announce: the loop
passes false when the refresh just said a warning or error, and the
challenge is asked without a progress note.

The pinning test a_challenge_is_asked_even_while_a_persons_send_holds_the_domain
locked in the old behaviour from #614; renamed
a_challenge_asked_while_busy_leaves_the_busy_refusal_said, it now asserts
the busy refusal stays. Changing it is the point of this commit. The plan
test covers a quiet ask.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vetting): "get tokens" keeps a failure the pass said

plan_draw_now runs the vetter pass, then shows what each community does.
That info status replaced whatever the pass had said, including a warning
or an error (a binding question that could not be signed). A new
Step::Summary shows its status only when the steps before it in the run
did not leave a warning or an error; DrawNow's summary uses it.

The plan test now expects Step::Summary. New tests: a unit test of the
summary rule and a runtime test where the pass's failure stays said (it
fails with the old Step::Status).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vetting): un-file a binding question whose signing fails

plan_ask_binding filed the PcsBinding question before the Ask step's
signing, and Asked::Binding's failure only said so, leaving the book
waiting on a question that never went. The failure now forgets the
question (Asked::Binding carries its document id), as the send-failure
outcome does. The key check keeps its asked time, so the question is
asked again only after BINDING_REASK.

The pinning test a_binding_question_without_keys_says_so_and_stays_asked
locked in the old behaviour from #614; renamed ..._and_is_unfiled, it now
asserts the question is gone and not re-asked early. Changing it is the
point of this commit.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* style(repos): collapse the link sweep's nested if (clippy)

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(rooms): a refresh on a busy lane says so

The memberships read a refresh (or opening the panel) sends had no
refusal, so on a busy Rooms lane nothing was read and nothing said; an
empty panel stayed on its loading line indefinitely. It now carries
Refusal::RecordBusy, a warning naming the busy lane and saying to press r
once it finishes, and the loading screen shows the status line.

The pinning test a_refresh_on_a_busy_lane_sends_nothing_and_says_nothing
locked in the old behaviour from #614; renamed
..._and_says_the_lane_is_busy, it now asserts the warning. Changing it is
the point of this commit.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(rooms): drop a renew step when no VTA is connected

Next::Renew with no VTA session planned an Ask that could never be
dispatched, so the step was kept and retried every tick for as long as
the panel stayed open. With no VTA it is now dropped with its renewals;
every read once a VTA is connected collects them again
(community_rooms::collect_renewals).

The pinning test a_renew_step_without_a_vta_is_kept locked in the old
behaviour from #614; renamed ..._is_dropped, it now asserts the step and
renewals are gone. Changing it is the point of this commit.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(elections): a show refused on a busy lane keeps the earlier target

plan_show reset the view's target (and presenting, opening, disclose)
and cleared what was shown before the send, so a press refused on a busy
lane still lost them. The new target and the notification opened from now
travel in Commit::Showing and are applied only once the read is claimed;
the send goes to the target directly.

The pinning test a_show_on_a_busy_lane_stays_on_the_list did not check
the target; renamed ..._and_keeps_its_target, it now asserts the earlier
target and presented membership stay. A new plan test checks the plan
changes no target and the commit sets it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(elections): a list refresh on a busy lane says so

#614 pinned that a list refresh on a busy community lane still set
notified_due. That part is right and stays: the held notifications are
read from the VTA on its own lane, so a busy community lane is no reason
to skip them. What was wrong is that the list read itself was refused
silently, leaving an empty panel on its loading line. It now carries
Refusal::ListBusy, a warning naming the busy lane, and the loading screen
shows the status line.

The pinning test an_open_on_a_busy_lane_sends_nothing_and_says_nothing
locked in the silence; renamed ..._and_says_the_lane_is_busy, it asserts
the warning and that the notifications are still due. Changing it is the
point of this commit.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(repos): save the workspace settings in a job, read them off the loop

SettingsSubmit stat-ed the chosen root and wrote the settings file on the
event loop (WorkspaceEffect::SaveSettings), and opening the panel read the
file there. Saving is now Work::Settings, a workspace job on the
GitWorkspace lane: the plan refuses a root it can tell is wrong without
the disk (empty, relative), and the job checks the directory and writes
the file with the blocking pool, its outcome closing the form or putting
the error on it. As a job it is refused while another workspace job runs,
which may be writing the same file. Opening reads the file with
spawn_blocking.

No pinning test drove the save (the harness avoided the disk). The plan
test settings_are_saved_by_a_job_and_a_clone_needs_a_target replaces the
one that pinned SaveSettings; new tests cover the job's write and refusal
and a save refused while a job runs.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(repos): keep the settings-read warning that opening showed

Opening the panel noted "couldn't read the workspace settings, using the
defaults" while filling the workspace, then ran the read's Step::Reading,
which clears the status line, so the warning was never seen. The
workspace open now returns the warning (fill), and the runner says it
after the open's steps.

No pinning test covered this (the harness does not touch the profile's
settings file); a new unit test checks the fill returns the warning
instead of saying it, and takes readable settings.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vetting): log hidden-vetting send failures as well as saying them

SendOrSay (an enrolment or a draw the VTA built) and Asked::Binding said
a signing or send failure on the status line only, so the next status
erased it and no record stayed (R6.5). Both now also write the activity
log and a tracing warning.

The pinning tests an_enrolment_without_keys_is_said_and_unfiled and
a_binding_question_without_keys_says_so_and_is_unfiled asserted the
failure was not logged (from #614); they now assert it is. Changing them
is the point of this commit. The draw test asserts it too.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vetting): keep an application's derived context only when used, and save it

application_context derived the application's VTA context and wrote it
to the book before the busy check, without a save, so a refused press
left an unsaved change and a used one was never written until something
else saved. It is now pure (AppContext with a derived flag); the face
plans keep it with keep_context only after the busy check and put a
Step::MarkDirty in the effect. A card's key lookup that fails takes back a
context kept for that card (Undo::NoContext). The PCS work plan keeps it
as before; its answers are saved when settled.

The pinning tests choosing_a_face_while_busy_derives_the_context_and_reads_nothing,
a_card_while_busy_derives_the_context_and_sends_nothing, the other busy
face tests, sending_a_card_without_keys_gives_up_unsent, the started face
tests (no save pending) and the plan tests
a_face_plan_on_a_busy_domain_is_refused_after_deriving_the_context and
choosing_a_face_plans_the_list_read locked in the old behaviour from
#614; they now assert no context on a refusal and a pending save when a
job starts. Changing them is the point of this commit.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* style: clippy on the follow-up fixes (Refusal names, ? operator, struct init)

Rooms' Refusal variants lose their shared Busy suffix (the enum is the
busy-lane refusals), repos_workspace::open uses ?, and a test builds its
settings with struct update syntax.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(repos): use a root that is absolute on Windows too

/srv/code is not an absolute path on Windows, so the settings-save plan
refused it there and the test failed.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: fix(vtc-service): setup never mints a did:webvh for an operator who chose did:webs
body:
When the interactive wizard could not read the VTA's did-hosting catalogue
(for example against a TSP-only VTA, which the catalogue client could not
reach), it returned `IdentityMethod::Webvh` before asking for the method, so
an operator who wanted a did:webs got a did:webvh with only a printed line to
say so.

The method is now asked in every case. Without the catalogue, a did:webvh is
still left to the VTA's own server pick; a did:webs, which needs a named
server and has no serverless mode, is refused with the fix:
`vtc setup --from` with `identity_method = "webs"` and `[webvh] server_id`.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

Tests: `without_the_catalogue_a_did_webvh_leaves_the_server_to_the_vta`, `without_the_catalogue_a_did_webs_is_refused_with_the_fix_not_minted_as_webvh`. The TSP catalogue connection itself is being fixed separately on `fix/vtc-setup-tsp-only-vta`; this touches only the fallback.
author: stormer78

title: fix(vtc-service): setup never mints a did:webvh for an operator who chose did:webs (#2756)
body:
fix(vtc-service): setup never mints a did:webvh for an operator who chose did:webs (#2756)

When the interactive wizard could not read the VTA's did-hosting catalogue
(for example against a TSP-only VTA, which the catalogue client could not
reach), it returned `IdentityMethod::Webvh` before asking for the method, so
an operator who wanted a did:webs got a did:webvh with only a printed line to
say so.

The method is now asked in every case. Without the catalogue, a did:webvh is
still left to the VTA's own server pick; a did:webs, which needs a named
server and has no serverless mode, is refused with the fix:
`vtc setup --from` with `identity_method = "webs"` and `[webvh] server_id`.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
author: stormer78

title: fix(setup): show and use a TSP-only agent's relay
body:
Follow-up to #438. With a did:webs VTA that advertises only `TSPTransport` now onboarded, three places still read the DIDComm mediator alone:

- **Setup → How to reach it** read `connection.mediatorDid` only, so it said *Reached over REST — this agent publishes no mediator* for an agent reached over TSP. It now uses DIDComm's mediator, else TSP's, and shows the transport line (TSP). The REST text appears only when REST is advertised.
- **`readActiveConnection`** (background) refused vault, context and DID tasks with *advertises no usable transport* unless REST or DIDComm was present. It now accepts TSP, and `readActiveConnectionRaw` carries `tspMediatorDid`.
- **`device/set-wake`** now suggests the TSP mediator as the trigger when there's no DIDComm one.

The same rule as `agentRelayMediator` (#438) applies throughout: an agent's relay is DIDComm's mediator, else TSP's.
author: stormer78

title: fix(setup): show and use a TSP-only agent's relay (#439)
body:
fix(setup): show and use a TSP-only agent's relay (#439)

After #438 a did:webs VTA advertising TSP alone onboards, but the wallet
still read only the DIDComm mediator in three places:

- Setup's "How to reach it" said "Reached over REST — this agent publishes
  no mediator" for an agent reached over TSP.
- readActiveConnection refused every vault, context and DID task with "no
  usable transport" unless REST or DIDComm was advertised.
- device/set-wake suggested no trigger mediator.

Each now reads the agent's relay as DIDComm's, else TSP's, as
agentRelayMediator does; the REST copy is shown only when REST is advertised.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
author: stormer78

title: fix(onboarding): onboard a VTA that advertises TSP alone
body:
## Problem

After #437 the did:webs VTA `did:webs:webvh.storm.ws:nodes:EJdeTq8v1SPknlbBkCXjSphLhP_N2D_9-IvFzBCYPxh5` resolves, but onboarding stops at:

> … advertises no #vta-didcomm or #vta-rest service

That VTA advertises only `#tsp` (`TSPTransport`), which is valid: VTI prefers TSP > DIDComm > REST and matches on `type`. `doOnboardConnect` already provisions over TSP, but `doOnboardPrepare` refused a TSP-only agent before connect could run.

Fixing only that would onboard the wallet with **no inbox**, because the inbox was taken only from the DIDComm service. The VTA's consent requests would then never arrive (R7.2).

## Change

- **prepare** accepts TSP, DIDComm or REST, and returns `tspMediatorDid`; the onboard view stores it on the connection and labels the transport TSP.
- **`agentRelayMediator`** (core): an agent's relay is its DIDComm mediator, else its TSP mediator. The inbox session multiplexes TSP and DIDComm frames on one socket, so a TSP-only agent has an inbox just as a DIDComm one does. It's used at onboarding (inbox recording), in `followAgentInbox` (boot re-follow), in `parseAgentMediatorDids` (stored-connection adopt), in the self-test's `inbox.mismatch` check, and in the Mediator Lens `locate` (which already did this inline).
- **`resolveVtaServices`** matches a service `type` written as a string or a set (DID Core §5.4), the same bug class as vti-didcomm-js #42.

## Not changed

An operator-supplied mediator still stands in for DIDComm only. A TSP mediator is never turned into a DIDComm service: per VTI, the protocol must not be inferred from the endpoint's shape.

## Tests

- `packages/core/tests/didcomm.agent-relay.mjs`: TSP-only, both, REST-only.
- `wallet-inbox.test.mts`: a TSP-only stored connection adopts its TSP relay; DIDComm wins beside it.
- Live: `resolveVtaServices` on the did:webs VTA returns `tsp` and relay `did:webvh:QmR5x…:webvh.storm.ws:mediator`.

The comment in `doOnboardConnect` notes that TSP delivery to a just-granted ephemeral had never been exercised. This VTA is the first live test of that path.
author: stormer78

Interoperability, canonicalisation, conformance, or protocol behaviour

A did:webs VTA may advertise only a TSPTransport service. Onboarding's
prepare step refused it ("advertises no #vta-didcomm or #vta-rest service")
although connect already provisions over TSP, so that path was unreachable.

  re-follow (followAgentInbox), the stored-connection adopt and the
  self-test's inbox check all read it, so a TSP-only agent's consent
  requests reach the wallet.

title: chore(deps): @openvtc/vti-didcomm-js 0.16.1 — did:webs service type as a set
body:
Raises `@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js` to **^0.16.1** (OpenVTC/vti-didcomm-js#42, #43).

Adding a did:webs-based VTA in the wallet failed with:

> did:webs: did.json does not match the verified key state: did.json's services differ from those the stream authorises

The VTA's `did.json` publishes `"type": ["TSPTransport"]` while the KERI stream derives `"TSPTransport"`; 0.16.0 compared the JSON as written. 0.16.1 compares a service's type as a set (DID Core §5.4), matching affinidi-did-webs 0.13.9 (affinidi-tdk-rs #1173). The floor is a correctness constraint: below it a did:webs VTA with a designated service cannot be onboarded.

Verified against the live `did:webs:webvh.storm.ws:nodes:EJdeTq8v1SPknlbBkCXjSphLhP_N2D_9-IvFzBCYPxh5` artifacts with the installed 0.16.1: resolves.
