title: feat(go-specs): release the generated specification packages as their own module
body:
Step 3 of #1112. Go core **v0.13.0** is on proxy.golang.org, and it is the first core without `specs/`. So `trust-tasks-go/specs` can require it and build. This PR wires that module's release. Import paths do not change. Anyone who imports a prebuilt package adds the module next to the core with `go get github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go/specs`.

## What changes

- **`trust-tasks-go/specs/go.mod`** requires core `v0.13.0`, and the TODO is gone. `go mod tidy` created `go.sum`, which lists only the core. There is no `replace`. `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass in the module (1577 packages), on stable and on go1.22.12.
- **Release wiring.** It matches how #886 wired `capabilityclient`, and `npm run check-release-lists` agrees:
  - `specs/version.go`: `package specs`, next to the generated `extends.go`, with `const Version = "0.1.0"`. This is the seeded initial version, and `CHANGELOG.md` is an empty preamble, as `capabilityclient` and `proof` had.
  - A `verify-go`/`publish-go` matrix leg in `publish.yml` with tag prefix `trust-tasks-go/specs/v`.
  - A `GO_MODULES` entry in `release-pr.sh`.
  - A `release-bump-go.sh` arm. It watches `trust-tasks-go/specs`, `specs/` and `scripts/build-go-bindings.mjs`, with scopes `go-specs` and `go-bindings`. `go-specs` is added to commit-lint's `!` scope list.
  - The core's watch still excludes `trust-tasks-go/specs`. It still watches `specs/` and the generator, because they write `trusttasks/extends_index.go`. So a spec change can release both modules.
- **`go.yml`** has a new `specs` job. It runs build, vet, gofmt and `test -race` on 1.22 and stable, and exits early through changed-paths like the other nested modules. `specs` comes off `NOT_BUILT_YET`, and that map is now empty.
- **Smoke test.** It moved from `smoke/testdata/smoke/` to `specs/smoke/smoke_test.go` and is now an ordinary test in the module. It runs against the published core it requires, which is what an importer gets. The core's `smoke/smoke_test.go` driver stays. It now copies the test from `specs/smoke` and still runs it against the checkout's runtime, so the core's `go test ./...` keeps driving generated code through unreleased runtime changes.
- **`build-go-bindings`.** `OUT_DIR_SOURCE_FILES` now also keeps `version.go`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `smoke/`. The generator refuses to write a package onto any of them. `npm run regen` leaves no drift.
- **Other:** Dependabot now watches `/trust-tasks-go/specs`. The docs are updated:
  - `trust-tasks-go/README.md`: the warning is replaced with `go get` instructions, and the nested-module table row now says the module is released.
  - `docs/packages/go.md`: the interim section is replaced.
  - `RELEASING.md`: the module's row and the watch paragraph are updated.
  - The website's Go library summary is updated.

  `docs/runtime-parity.md` does not mention the module.

The `specs` module has no API-compatibility job, just as the other nested modules have none. Changes to its generated packages are already gated by `published schemas change only additively`.

## What happens at merge

No Release PR is needed first. The initial version is seeded in `version.go`, and `publish-go` seeds the first tag itself (RELEASING.md, "The Go module seeds itself").

1. `verify-go` (leg `trust-tasks-go/specs`) sees that `trust-tasks-go/specs/v0.1.0` does not exist. It runs `go build/vet/test ./...` in the module against the published core v0.13.0.
2. `publish-go` pushes the tag **`trust-tasks-go/specs/v0.1.0`** and warms proxy.golang.org. **This tag is permanent and cannot be retracted.**
3. `release-pr` runs after `publish-go`. For `trust-tasks-go/specs` it finds `v0.1.0` at HEAD and has nothing to release. The other legs (core `v0.13.0`, proof, didcomm, capabilityclient) are already tagged, so they skip.
4. This PR changes `scripts/build-go-bindings.mjs` and `trust-tasks-go/smoke/`, which are in the core's watch. So the next Release PR also proposes a **patch** for the core (`v0.13.1`). The title has no `!`.

## Checks run locally

- In `trust-tasks-go`: `gofmt -l .` reports nothing, and `go vet ./...` and `go test -race ./...` pass. The smoke driver runs; it does not skip.
- In `trust-tasks-go/specs`: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `go test -race ./...` pass on stable, and build, vet and test pass on go1.22.12.
- `npm run regen` leaves no drift.

- `scripts/release-bump-go.sh trust-tasks-go/specs` parses the new arm. It stops with the expected "No trust-tasks-go/specs/v* tag exists" error, because `publish-go` writes that tag.

Since #1312, the `Release PR` job in `publish.yml` has failed with `Process completed with exit code 141` (SIGPIPE) on every push to main, so no Release PR has been opened. `release-pr.sh` and the three `release-bump-*.sh` scripts now run under `set -E` with an `ERR` trap. When a step fails, the trap prints `::error file=…,line=…::exit N from: <command>`. title: feat(tsp): carry the binding 0.2 deliveryId on Envelope; refuse duplicated envelope members again
body:
## What and why

This follows up #1322, which added `trust_tasks_tsp::Envelope`. It acts on review points that came in after #1322 merged.

### 1. Binding 0.2 `deliveryId` (§2.1)

`bindings/tsp/0.2/spec.md` §2 adds an optional `deliveryId` envelope member, a string of 1 to 256 characters. It asks the consumer to send an end-to-end delivery receipt (`messaging/receipt`). The envelope `type` is unchanged from 0.1. The Affinidi messaging SDK (0.49, `delivery.rs` `tsp_envelope` / `tsp_delivery_id`) already sets and reads it. Without this change, an application that moved from hand-written envelope code to `Envelope` would lose its receipts.

```rust
pub const MAX_DELIVERY_ID_LEN: usize = 256;
pub struct InvalidDeliveryId { /* private */ }        // Error; length() -> usize
impl Envelope {
    pub fn with_delivery_id(self, delivery_id: impl Into<String>) -> Result<Self, InvalidDeliveryId>;
    pub fn delivery_id(&self) -> Option<&str>;
}
```

- **Writing:** `to_bytes` writes `deliveryId` only when one is set.
  - **Golden test without one:** the bytes are unchanged, still the 0.1 envelope.
  - **Golden test with one:** `{"deliveryId":…,"document":…,"type":…}`. This is the object the SDK builds, in the same member order, because it is built the same way.
- **Reading:** `from_bytes` keeps a valid `deliveryId`. It drops an invalid one (empty, more than 256 characters, or not a string) and still reads the envelope. §2.1 says the id must not affect the framework pipeline, so a bad id costs the producer its receipt, not its document. The SDK's reader filters the same way.
- **Unchanged:** `unpack_trust_task` / `TspConsumer` behave as before. They open a 0.2 envelope (there is a test for this) and do not expose the id. Sending receipts belongs to the delivery layer.
- **Why a new error type:** `TspError` is not `#[non_exhaustive]`, so a new variant would break its API. `InvalidDeliveryId` is a new type, which is additive.

### 2. Duplicated envelope members

Since #1322, `from_bytes` parsed the payload through a `serde_json::Value` to require an object. A `Value` keeps the last of two duplicated members silently, so `{"type":"x","type":"…/envelope",…}` was accepted. The binding's private envelope used to refuse that.

This PR goes back to deserialising straight into the derived struct, which refuses a duplicated `type` or `document`. A check on the first non-whitespace byte (`{`) keeps the object-only rule. Reasons for refusing rather than matching the TS/Go/Dart last-wins parse:
- Under RFC 8259 a JSON object with duplicate names has unpredictable meaning.
- An envelope whose `type` or `document` is ambiguous is not one a conforming producer writes.
- The Rust crate refused it until #1322.

The TS, Go and Dart bindings still take the last occurrence. That is a parse-level difference on non-conforming input only. A unit test covers both duplicated members.

### 3. Comments

- `to_bytes` explains why it builds a `json!` map rather than serialising a struct. The map keeps the member order, and so the bytes, the same as before, whether or not serde_json's `preserve_order` is on. A struct would fix one order and change the bytes in one of those builds.
- The golden comment now says the keys are sorted, because serde_json is built without `preserve_order`.

### 4. Error for a non-object payload

`InvalidBody` now names the kind of value received, for example `invalid type: sequence, expected the binding envelope object` or `invalid type: integer `7``. If the payload is not JSON at all, the error is the parser's own.

### 5. Consumer-observable tightening, for the maintainer to judge

#1322 made `unpack_trust_task` / `TspConsumer` refuse an envelope sent as a JSON array. This PR restores the refusal of duplicated members, which #1322 had briefly loosened. Both changes are visible to consumers, but only on input that does not conform to binding §2: no conforming producer, in any of the four languages, writes either form. I have therefore titled this `feat(tsp):` with no `!`. If you see refusing non-conforming input as a behavioural break under [DEVELOPMENT.md's semver rule](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/blob/main/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#library-versions-are-semver-over-the-librarys-api-not-the-frameworks), retitle it `feat(tsp)!:`. That would make the next release of the core group 0.41.0 instead of 0.40.1.

## Checklist

- [x] Every commit is DCO signed (`git commit -s`).
- [x] The title is a conventional commit; any `!` is scoped to the package whose API breaks.
- [x] If `specs/` changed: all four libraries are regenerated (`npm run regen`) and committed. (n/a)
- [x] No package version and no `CHANGELOG.md` entry is edited — the Release PR does both.
- [x] `npm run check` passes, and these ran clean:
  - `cargo test -p trust-tasks-tsp`
  - `cargo clippy -p trust-tasks-tsp --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc -p trust-tasks-tsp --no-deps`
  - `cargo fmt --all --check`
  - MSRV 1.95 `cargo check --all-targets`
  - `cargo semver-checks check-release -p trust-tasks-tsp --baseline-rev trust-tasks-tsp-v0.40.0 --release-type minor`: 202 checks pass, no semver update required.

title: feat(tsp): expose the binding envelope for applications that seal through their own TSP stack
body:
## What and why `trust-tasks-tsp` now exposes the binding's envelope object without the TSP seal, as `trust_tasks_tsp::Envelope`. `pack_trust_task` / `unpack_trust_task` take raw VID keys and do the seal themselves. An application whose own TSP stack seals and opens messages cannot use them. The Affinidi messaging SDK's TSP path is one such stack: it holds the keys and the relationship state. Such an application has been hand-writing the `{type, document}` object and its `type` check: the Affinidi trust registry does it in its server and again in its client. `Envelope` gives it the same code `pack_trust_task` and `unpack_trust_task` use, so the bytes cannot drift. ```rust impl Envelope { pub fn new(doc: &TrustTask

) -> Result; // SerialiseBody pub fn from_document(document: serde_json::Value) -> Self; pub fn from_bytes(payload: &[u8]) -> Result; // InvalidBody | WrongEnvelopeType pub fn to_bytes(&self) -> Vec; pub fn document(&self) -> &serde_json::Value; pub fn into_document(self) -> serde_json::Value; pub fn into_trust_task(self) -> Result, TspError>; // InvalidBody } ``` `ENVELOPE_TYPE` was already public. It moves to the new module and is re-exported at the same path. The new API is additive (`feat(tsp):`, no `!`). Fields are private, so the type can grow without a break. `from_bytes` keeps the `document` as received, because a proof is verified over the received object, never over a typed copy (binding §2, SPEC §4.7). `Envelope` does not repeat the checks `unpack_trust_task` makes on the TSP message itself (Direct carriage, cleartext sender and receiver VIDs), and it does not run the SPEC §7.2 consumer checks. The rustdoc and README say this, and they point to `GuardedConsumer::consume_body` with a `TspHandler`. **Wire:** the bytes do not change. `pack_inner_direct` and `open` now use `Envelope`. `tests/envelope.rs` pins the plaintext to a golden string and checks four things: - `pack_trust_task` seals exactly `Envelope::to_bytes`. - A payload sealed from `Envelope::to_bytes` opens with `unpack_trust_task`. - `pack_trust_task`'s plaintext parses with `Envelope::from_bytes`. - Member order and whitespace in a received envelope do not matter. A unit test checks the bytes against the `json!` construction the binding used before. **One behaviour tightening:** the envelope payload must now be a JSON *object*, as binding §2 requires. A derived struct deserialiser also accepted the two members as a JSON array, so `unpack_trust_task` and `TspConsumer` used to take `["…/envelope", {…}]`. No conforming producer sends that, and the TS, Go and Dart bindings never sealed it. **Other bindings:** none of `trust-tasks-ts-tsp`, `trust-tasks-go/tsp` or `trust_tasks_tsp` (Dart) exposes the envelope apart from its pack/unpack. No repository rule requires public-API parity for the hand-written binding siblings, so this PR records the gap as a `todo` row in `docs/runtime-parity.md` and does not add three more APIs nobody has asked for yet. The wire object is the binding's, so nothing differs on the wire. ## Checklist - [x] Every commit is DCO signed (`git commit -s`). - [x] The title is a conventional commit; any `!` is scoped to the package whose API breaks. - [x] If `specs/` changed: all four libraries are regenerated (`npm run regen`) and committed. (n/a, no `specs/` change) - [x] No package version and no `CHANGELOG.md` entry is edited — the Release PR does both. - [x] `npm run check` passes, and the tests for the code touched were run: `cargo test -p trust-tasks-tsp` (unit, integration, doctest), `cargo clippy -p trust-tasks-tsp --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc -p trust-tasks-tsp --no-deps`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, and `cargo check -p trust-tasks-tsp --all-targets` on the 1.95 MSRV.

title: feat(runner): complete configured RAHP Evaluation Runner, pinned DTG examples and scheduled reports
body:
## What changed

Implements [#63](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/issues/63) in three bounded increments as an **optional RAHP Evaluation Runner**, not a telemetry monitoring plane, an automated governance controller, or an independent assurance authority. The deliverable is a deployable, source-pinned, configuration-driven evaluation entry point with independently reproducible historical demonstrations, portable documentation, failure and uncertainty semantics, and multi-target reporting.

The main architectural distinction is **evaluation** versus **monitoring**. RAHP executes bounded analytical examinations and validates assessor-authored findings. The independent DTG Portfolio Monitor observes repository activity and can provide advisory selection metadata, but it does not own RAHP evaluations and its downstream executor definitions are not transplanted upstream.

## Why this is warranted

Upstream already has a portable method (`method/`), a DTG worked instance (`data/`), a canonical review record (`rahp-spec-review/v1`), corpus/review validators, and retained-source TRQP/VRC/TEA examinations. An unfamiliar adopter lacked a single, configurable execution/repetition/reporting path that could be scheduled without editing upstream scripts. Reimplementing the downstream RAHP controller or treating source-activity metrics as assurance would erode the method's governance/authority boundaries. The increments here instead compose existing upstream validator contracts and deliberately separate documentary review validation from target-specific examination.

## Increment 1: bounded offline examiner

**Files:** `runner/__main__.py`, `runner/examples/retained-trqp.yaml`, `tests/test_evaluation_runner.py`, `runner/README.md`, `README.md`.

- Versioned `rahp-evaluation-runner/v1alpha1` YAML configuration, strict fields, stable unique target IDs, exact allowed evaluator and immutable source revision agreement with retained `review.yaml`.
- `python3 -m runner validate` and `run`, bounded subprocess execution of **installed upstream** `review/examine.py`, never target-supplied code or shell.
- Per-run `evaluation.json` / `evaluation.md`, configuration SHA-256, provenance, machine-validation status, explicit `assurance: review-required` when validation succeeds and `not-assessed` when it fails.
- Tests for unknown fields, duplicate IDs, mutable refs, unknown evaluator/repository, missing mandatory fields, false-success output, timeouts, failed examiner, revision mismatch and the actual upstream examiner consumer path.

This increment runs offline with the retained TRQP source and original upstream example-local evidence. It does not claim arbitrary specification examination.

## Increment 2: independently executable documentary evaluation service

**Files:** `runner/service.py`, `runner/examples/service.yaml`, `runner/Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore`, `runner/deployments/systemd/*`, `runner/docs/operations.md`.

- Separate versioned `rahp-evaluation-runner/v1alpha2` contract, preserving the v1alpha1 offline interface and its stronger retained TRQP-specific evidence semantics.
- Explicit repository, ref/revision, reviewer-authored `review`, selected `risks`, `artifact` path and optional artifact hash; no generic arbitrary-code evaluator.
- Public GitHub HTTPS Git acquisition with restricted transport, Git hooks disabled, immutable revision resolution and exact comparison with the review's `target.revision`. The fetched source artifact is hashed and optional expected digest is enforced.
- Existing installed `review/validate_spec_review.py` validates the documentary review against the explicitly supplied corpus; this **does not automatically extract risks, inspect runtime behavior or prove the reviewer's inference**.
- Per-run reports preserve config/review/risk/method digests, source SHA, artifact SHA-256, outcome, UTC timestamp and claim boundary. Missing evidence/source, invalid review, checksum mismatch and unexpected failures remain failed/not-assessed.
- An OCI image recipe for one-shot execution, with nonroot user, no supplied credentials and supported Git/Python dependencies; a root `.dockerignore` excludes Git metadata, local evidence and private environment files from build context.
- systemd service/timer and independent operator instructions to schedule the **same** CLI on VM/container/host; no permanent daemon, public HTTP endpoint, database, alerting product or Kubernetes operator introduced.

## Increment 3: curated portfolio selection, history and isolation

**Files:** `runner/examples/dtg-curated.yaml`, `runner/examples/dtg-service.yaml`, `tests/test_evaluation_service.py`, `.github/workflows/evaluation-smoke.yml`.

- An **advisory**, pinned `dtg-portfolio-monitor-curated-v1` inventory adapter. The example is adapted from [the independently maintained portfolio monitor curated registry](https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/dtg-portfolio-monitor/blob/1a1982212bce36d79a5fb9dc6d58bec7b7d9e01a/config/repositories.yaml), with its original Apache-2.0 provenance and immutable source commit declared. A local SHA-256 digest must match; configured projects not present in the allowlist are rejected. The monitor's materiality/discovery/weight classifications do **not** constitute RAHP policy or methodology authority.
- A realistic historical VRC sequence using existing upstream `review/examples/vrc-v03/baseline-review.yaml` and `reassessed-review.yaml` at two immutable `trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-tf` source revisions. The runner actually fetches both revisions in CI and validates their assessor-authored statuses.
- Multi-target `run-all` executes each configured evaluation, records failures independently, and returns nonzero when any target fails. One unavailable target does not erase the results of its peers.
- `series` explicitly groups comparable review iterations. Historical comparison is permitted only under the same repository, evaluation type, review schema, selected risk corpus digest and installed method validator digest. Comparison reports **differences in reviewer-authored status**, not automated remediation proof. A missing finding is `absent`, never silently `resolved`.
- An exclusive same-volume output lock prevents concurrent invocations racing when selecting comparison baselines.
- Offline boundary/negative tests cover malicious/unsafe paths, inventory checksum mismatch, invalid refs, repository admission, review identity, simulated acquisition failure, partial multi-target execution, incompatible comparisons and absent-finding semantics.
- An independent GitHub Actions smoke workflow exercises **real Git source acquisition**, two historical review-record validations, comparison output, and a Docker build/CLI configuration test. The workflow uploads evidence with bounded retention.

## Reproduction and expected results

From the upstream checkout after installing requirements:

```sh
python3 -m runner validate --config runner/examples/retained-trqp.yaml
python3 -m runner run --config runner/examples/retained-trqp.yaml --target retained-trqp --output /tmp/rahp-offline

python3 -m runner.service validate --config runner/examples/dtg-service.yaml
python3 -m runner.service run-all --config runner/examples/dtg-service.yaml --output /tmp/rahp-service

python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python3 tools/validate.py --summary
```

The service's completed evaluations report `validation: review-record-valid` and `assurance: review-required`. A source acquisition failure, stale source revision, unsupported evaluator, invalid corpus/review or incomplete result is **not** a PASS. A two-revision historical comparison may report `F-001: open → resolved` **as asserted in the two upstream VRC review records**; it does not independently establish that the risk is eliminated.

Build/validate the container using the commands in [operations documentation](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/blob/feat/rahp-evaluation-runner/runner/docs/operations.md). These are independently testable acceptance paths, not instructions to copy downstream assessment schemas into upstream.

## Observed validation and assurance evidence

- [RAHP validation on expanded implementation](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/actions/runs/43355671936): **passed**, including the new service tests and existing repository regressions.
- [Real Git acquisition, historical VRC comparison, container build and config smoke](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/actions/runs/43355671947): **passed**.
- [Upstream Pages build and link/route checks](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/actions/runs/43355671891): **passed**, PR deployment intentionally skipped.
- The final sign-off-consolidated commit will rerun these checks; final-head status must be examined before merge.
- DCO sign-off is supplied under the responsible user's GitHub-associated no-reply identity; verify the final head's DCO and EasyCLA checks. This is contributor certification of the contribution, **not** Task Force approval of RAHP methodology.

### Adversarial and false-success boundary

The tests deliberately attempt to make an invalid configuration appear executable, equate an unknown evaluator with a supported one, accept a mutable/mismatched source as immutable, conflate a validation result with assurance success, hide a failed target within a larger batch, carry a historical conclusion across incompatible method/corpus baselines, and treat disappearing findings as resolved. The implementation is designed to reject or explicitly preserve those states.

The canonical consumer path is checked both offline and using two actual publicly fetched historical Git commits. The code path fetches immutable source bytes and validates review schema/provenance; independent source publisher authentication, actual harm inference and real-world operational control effectiveness remain outside the claim.

## Authority, compatibility, privacy and governance

- **No changes** to `method/`, canonical `data/`, upstream review schema/vocabulary, risk scoring, authorized risk acceptance or actual normative requirements.
- The monitor remains an **independent derived observatory**, not official ToIP or upstream RAHP authority. Its current downstream pressure-test file paths remain non-executable upstream.
- The two configuration contracts are separately versioned and documented. Previous core `review/` CLI and review-record consumers remain supported. Configuration changes should be treated as compatibility events if published for adoption.
- The runner currently supports public GitHub HTTPS; unsupported private or external hosts, auth credentials, webhooks and arbitrary plugins require independent review.
- Reports may contain source-context identifiers. Operators own access controls, backup, retention, deletion and incident handling. Git revision/digest verification is not an independently trusted publisher signature.
- Source-collection materiality and freshness signals are advisory, not automatic evaluation applicability or proof of assurance.
- Historical status differences reflect documented reviewer conclusions and their limitations; they are not new governance determinations.
- The code introduces optional operational maintenance responsibilities, which the competent Task Force should explicitly accept or decline before positioning this as a stable supported product.

## Related issues and disposition

Tracks [#63](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/issues/63). Complements [#9](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/issues/9) adoption, [#49](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/issues/49) first-use, and [#17](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/issues/17) convergence without subsuming their contracts. [#34](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/issues/34) covers runtime-governance *semantics*, not this orchestration service. [#62](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/issues/62) remains proposed V3 coordination, not evidence of prior Task Force authorization.

**Review recommendation:** examine configuration semantics, false-success boundaries, source acquisition trust, evidence claims and whether upstream will accept the maintenance burden. Keep this PR draft until final checks, independent review and competent upstream disposition are complete. Merge alone would not resolve GAP-3.1/GAP-5.1 or confer governance approval.

## AI-assisted contribution disclosure

AI assistance drafted and executed the runner, documentation, fixtures, CI and test changes using the linked user's repository permissions. The responsible human requested the implementation and explicitly authorized DCO sign-off under the existing GitHub-associated identity. CI results and retained test evidence are identified above. Independent contributor/Task Force review is not claimed and remains required.

title: refactor(runtime): Runtime struct, join on the main loop, unified community replies, cheaper state sync
body:
PR 9 of the remediation plan on #589: the runtime restructure.

Closes #528, closes #529, closes #534, closes #555, closes #556, closes #565, closes #557. Part of #535, part of #537.

## Changes

**#528** `StateHandler::main_loop` becomes `state_handler/runtime/`: a `Runtime` struct holding the loop-local state, one method per `select!` arm (`arms.rs`, `inbound_arm.rs`, `timers.rs`), and a short router in `Runtime::run`. The arm bodies moved unchanged. There is a harness that drives single arms and the whole loop.

**#529** The join is driven from the loop that owns it, with no nested event loop:
- `join_flow/driver.rs` is a `JoinDriver` driven by both the runtime and the State-A loop.
- Resolve, discovery and the five launch stages run off the loop on `DispatchDomain::Join`.
- A `JoinSaga` in core (`openvtc-core/src/join/`) records each step and its compensation. Network steps are split into I/O and apply halves. `SubjectSigner` reads the signer off the config and signs without it.
- Esc, F10 or an error cancels any stage before the submit, and the saga undoes it. A generation counter drops stale results. Keys pressed while a job runs are queued and replayed in order.
- **Submit is past the point of no return.** An exit during it waits for it to finish, so the request is recorded and the persona kept. A loop stop mid-submit keeps the persona and listener instead of forgetting them. Inbound from the community being submitted to is held until the pending record exists, then processed. The old nested loop got this by not reading inbound at all.
- **Bug fixed:** on `main`, a failed submit (other than a signer failure) forgot the persona even when it was reused, and could remove another persona's `key_info`. The saga forgets only a persona this join minted.

**#534** A `PendingReplies` table owned by the runtime replaces the three process-global reply-correlation statics in core (renewal, profile queries, elections). TTLs and caps are the same; entries are recorded on the loop before the spawn. `community_request.rs` holds the shared request/reply engine; rooms and elections run on it, and repos uses its helpers.

**#535 (part)** Every TUI save goes through `SaveScheduler`, and `settings_actions::save_config` is gone. Forced saves `flush`, which is awaited and still durable before success is reported. `flush` now leaves the config dirty while an older background save is in flight, so that save cannot have the last word. One spawn shape: a `Job` trait plus `background_dispatch::dispatch`, used by most spawners and by community-context's VTA work. **Remaining:**
- Some spawners still claim and spawn directly, because preparation with side effects precedes the claim: `DeleteDid`, VRC request, inbox, relationship, witness, mediator reconnect.
- Elections ticket and cast, the Rooms VTA call and the repos probe each need their own job type.
- The vetting jobs claim their domain elsewhere.
- Vetting's and community_context's loop handlers are not reducer + effect, and `sync_from_config` is not split per panel.

**#556** The published state is `Arc<State>` behind a `Shared<T>` view, instead of three deep copies per turn. There is no dirty tracking (R23's objection stands). The session-reconcile arm skips the broadcast only when it changed nothing; the 2 s VTA-sync tick always republishes, so time-based displays keep moving.

**#555** The post-quantum proof check is remembered per credential. did-git-sign detection runs off the loop, at startup and when a view that shows it opens; `sync_from_config` no longer reads files.

**#565** VTA retry back-off is jittered. `OPENVTC_DEBUG_LOG` rotates past 50 MiB. Relationship keys are looked up by id prefix through a sorted map. Persona labels and membership counts are maps built once per sync.

**#557 (rest)** `regenerate_persona_keys` takes `&TDK`. Personas hydrate three at a time, in a fixed order; one that fails no longer stops the rest.

**#537 (part)**
- Runtime arm tests and a join-saga test with a failure injected at every stage.
- The cancel, resolve-queue and stale-outcome tests, and the submit-stage tests.
- A new `test-ignored` CI job runs the `#[ignore]`d e2e suites on every PR (SHA-pinned, `--locked`, 60 min timeout).
- CONTRIBUTING states the policy: a test is ignored only for being slow or needing an in-process service, never for being flaky.
- Coverage floors are not set.

Also: `bip39` moves to openvtc-core's dev-dependencies (only tests use it; cargo 1.100 warned).

## Review
An independent review traced:
- every exit of `main`'s join flow against the driver: outcomes, messages and persisted effects;
- compensation;
- key queuing;
- `PendingReplies`;
- `Shared<T>`;
- the save path.

It found two medium issues. Exit during the submit forgot the persona after the request was sent, and an early community reply could be dropped. Both are fixed here with tests. It also found three low issues, all fixed: the overlapping flush, guards that left a launch locked, and slower time-based redraws.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)
- The app no longer freezes during a join. Esc, F10 or an error cancels and undoes any stage before the submit. During the submit, an exit waits for it.
- "Joining a community failed (internal error)." appears if a join job panics.
- A failed submit no longer forgets a reused persona.
- Personas after one that fails to load are still loaded. Their progress lines can interleave.
- No wire types or config formats changed.

## Testing
2,369 passed / 37 ignored on `main`, and 2,436 passed / 37 ignored on this branch (default features, and also with `--no-default-features`). `--include-ignored`: 2,473 passed, 0 failed. `-p openvtc --features dev-overrides`: 1,100 passed.

All exit 0: `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy `-D warnings` (default, `--no-default-features`, `dev-overrides`), `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`, `cargo machete`. Not tried against a live stack.

## Pre-merge checklist
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): none added
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): join I/O runs in off-loop jobs with owned inputs
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the saga records each step before its effect and compensates in reverse; the submit is not compensated once it may have gone out
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): VTA retry is bounded at 3 and now jittered; persona hydration is bounded at 3 concurrent
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): the inbound and timer arms are unchanged; held inbound is bounded (64)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): unchanged
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): none
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): unchanged
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): a join-job panic is reported; a stopped mid-submit join says the request may have been sent
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): saga compensation plus forced flushes; a flush overlapped by an older save is re-saved
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: refactor(runtime): Runtime struct, join on the main loop, unified community replies, cheaper state sync (#607)
body:
refactor(runtime): Runtime struct, join on the main loop, unified community replies, cheaper state sync (#607)

* refactor(runtime): lift main_loop's select arms into a Runtime struct (#528)

The ~2,500-line StateHandler::main_loop kept some thirty loop-local
variables and 21 select! arms in one function nothing could call from a
test. Those locals are now the fields of state_handler::runtime::Runtime,
each arm is one method on it (runtime/arms.rs, inbound_arm.rs, timers.rs),
and Runtime::run is a router over them plus the end-of-iteration work.

Pure restructuring: the arm bodies moved verbatim (each method
destructures the fields it uses, so the bodies read as they did with
locals), the setup after the State-A branch became Runtime::assemble, and
the shutdown sequence Runtime::shutdown. No behaviour change.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(runtime): a harness for the runtime loop and its arms (#537)

Assembles a real Runtime on an offline TDK, a listener-less messaging
runtime and no admin session, and drives single arms (listener and
lifecycle events, a failed save, a dispatch outcome, the VTA sync tick, a
pong, the reply-window sweep, the pending-expiry sweep) and the whole loop
until Exit or an interrupt stops it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(tui): share the published State as Arc<State> (#556)

The state channel is now watch::Sender<Arc<State>>. Publishing clones the
state once, into the Arc (PublishState::publish), and the UI's copies
share it: the main page and join flow props hold a Shared<T> projection of
the snapshot instead of cloning the main-page model and the join state on
every update, and the setup and loading props are refreshed only while
their page is on screen. A page that edits its props locally still can:
the first write copies the part, as every update used to.

Every publish still sends — no dirty tracking, so R23's stale-UI objection
does not apply. The two timer arms that can prove they changed nothing
(the VTA sync tick that starts no cycle, the session reconcile that
changes no session) skip the end-of-iteration work and its broadcast.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(core): split the join's network steps into I/O and apply halves (#529)

learn_over_http, learn_signing and submit each become an owned I/O half
that needs no Config (fetch_over_http, resolve_document, submit_prepared)
and a half that takes the Config on the caller's thread (learn_fetched,
note_signing, prepare_submit), so the TUI can run the I/O off its runtime
loop. The one-call forms remain for community join and are those halves
in sequence; no behaviour change.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(core): JoinSaga — a join launch's steps and their compensations (#529)

Records ContextRegistered -> Minted -> ListenerUp -> Submitted -> Persisted
as a launch completes them and derives, from that record alone, what undoes
the launch where it stopped: remove the listener it installed, forget the
persona it minted; nothing once the request is out. Replaces the TUI's
out-parameters and hand-placed rollbacks (wired in the next commit).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(core): jitter the VTA retry back-off (R1.4)

Equal jitter over the existing exponential step: each retry waits between
half and all of 0.5s * 2^(n-1), so clients that failed together do not
retry in lockstep. Refs #565.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(tui): rotate OPENVTC_DEBUG_LOG once it passes 50 MiB

At open, a log already over the cap is moved to <path>.1 (replacing any
earlier rotation) and a fresh file is started, so long debug sessions
keep at most two files. Refs #565.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(core): look up relationship keys by id prefix instead of scanning key_info

generate_profiles and repair_key_info_ids scanned the whole key_info map
per relationship with starts_with. Sort the ids once and range-query
them: exactly the same matches, O((keys + relationships) log keys).
Refs #565.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(tui): check each VRC for post-quantum proofs once, not on every sync

finish_credential_rows serialised every VRC to read its proofs on each
sync_from_config. Remember the answer by credential id (a VRC's id is
its proof value) across syncs; each sync keeps only the ids it shows,
so the memo is bounded by the credentials on display. Refs #555.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(tui): look up persona labels and membership counts by map in sync

finish_credential_rows scanned the personas for every self-subject row,
and the persona list counted memberships with a filter per persona.
Build both maps once per sync_from_config. Refs #565.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(tui): detect the did-git-sign install off the loop, not in every sync

sync_from_config read did-git-sign's SigningConfig and allowed_signers on
every config change. Detection now runs on a blocking thread as a
DidGitSign dispatch and is kept in SettingsState with the persona DID it
was read for: a sync for another persona hides it, and a refresh is due
on a persona switch, after a Repos signing change, or when Help / Status
or Settings is opened. The Repos tick checks for a due refresh; a check
is a few comparisons, no I/O. Refs #555.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(core): regenerate_persona_keys takes &TDK

It only reads the TDK (the secrets resolver is shared state), so a
shared borrow lets personas be hydrated concurrently. Refs #557.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(core): hydrate personas three at a time at startup

Each persona's document resolve, key fetch and profile registration ran
one persona after another. They share only read-only handles, so run
them with a bound of three and record the results in account order:
the degraded report and identities are the same whichever finishes
first, and a fault no persona can work around still fails the load.
Refs #557.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(tui): read did-git-sign's install at startup and when a view shows it (#555)

Wires the off-loop did-git-sign refresh into the runtime: once when the
loop starts, and after each action when a view that shows it has just
opened (a cheap check, no I/O). The 5-second sweep still catches anything
else.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(core): SubjectSigner — read a subject-linkage signer off the config, sign without it (#529)

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(join): drive the join from the loop that owns it, as a saga, with no nested event loop (#529)

The join flow was a nested select! loop the runtime awaited inline, parking
every other arm while the join screen was up. It is now a JoinDriver state
machine both the runtime loop and the State-A loop drive: page logic runs
on the loop, network work runs as off-loop jobs on DispatchDomain::Join
(matched by generation, aborted on Esc/F10), join keys pressed during a job
are queued and replayed, and a launch is a JoinSaga whose failures, cancels
and interrupts undo it from its compensations. A reused persona is no
longer forgotten on a failed submit. The old StateHandler::join_flow,
run_join_sequence and race_against_interrupt are removed.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(join): a launch failed at each saga stage, cancelled mid-stage, and a resolve queued behind and aborted (#529)

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(join): the join is a driven state machine, not a nested loop (#529)

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(core): PendingReplies, a runtime-owned table of replies awaited by thread

One in-memory table (thread -> community, purpose, when) for the replies
admitted only because we asked: renewals, community profiles, and election
answers from a community we hold no membership with. Each kind keeps the
window, cap, thread normalisation and community comparison of the
process-global static it replaces (#534).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor: replace the reply-correlation statics with the runtime's PendingReplies

renewal.rs PENDING, join.rs PROFILE_QUERIES and elections.rs AWAITING are
gone. The runtime loop owns one PendingReplies and passes it explicitly:
the send paths record into it on the loop thread before spawning (a
renewal's id and a profile question's id are now chosen there), and
inbound dispatch (verification_job, the community-reply gate, the renewal,
refusal and profile handlers) consumes from it. Elections records and
forgets through its Loop, its outcome and its reply path; a failed renewal
send forgets its request in CommunityOutcome::apply. Headless commands
(join, repos) hold their own table for apply_inline, and the core tests
each use a local one instead of sharing process globals (#534).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(ui): one community_request module for the panels that ask a community

Rooms and Elections now share one request/reply engine
(state_handler/community_request.rs) behind a small CommunityFeature
trait: arming the view before the send is spawned, the send job and its
outcome, taking an answer only on its thread from the community asked,
the 30 s reply window, job loss, and keeping a step whose lane is busy.
Elections' threads are recorded at, and forgotten from, the runtime's
PendingReplies by the engine (RECORDS_THREAD). Each panel keeps what is
its own: building requests, what an answer, a timeout or a failure says,
and its VTA calls.

One CommunityLoop replaces the three Loop structs (re-exported as
rooms_actions::Loop, elections_actions::Loop, repos_actions::Loop).
Repos keeps its two-slot wait (request and link poll, per-purpose
windows) but takes the shared loop, Sender/sender/sign_and_send and
answered_by from the module; did_part and capitalise exist once.
No message, timeout or correlation rule changes (#534).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(state_handler): one persistence path — every TUI save goes through SaveScheduler (#535)

Delete settings_actions::save_config. The passphrase set/remove and the
export/import log entries force-flush with SaveScheduler::flush (awaited,
so still durable before success is reported), which also clears the
pending dirty mark; clear_after_external_save has no callers left and goes.

A standalone persona mint is written in memory (MintedPersona::write_into
over the new ConfigExtension::mint_persona_in_memory) and settle_after_apply
force-flushes it through the scheduler, off the runtime. The headless join
keeps its own save. mint_persona_into (join driver, setup) still saves
itself.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(state_handler): one spawn shape — a Job trait and background_dispatch::dispatch (#535)

A job names its DispatchDomain and its I/O (Job::execute, returning the
DispatchOutcome); dispatch(job, in_flight, dispatch_tx, on_busy) claims
the domain and spawns it, or drops it unrun and hands on_busy the busy
message. Work due only once the claim succeeded is done by the caller on
true, in the same loop turn as the spawn, so no outcome can overtake it.

On it: spawn_persona_mint, spawn_community_job, spawn_capability_job,
spawn_vic_mutation, spawn_agent_name_job, spawn_vic_refresh (its
begin_vic_refresh guard folds in; the test drives spawn_vic_refresh),
spawn_persona_effect, dispatch_binding_refresh, the timer sweeps (agent
names, community contexts, device grants, VTA transports), the
did-git-sign detection, community_request's sends, the Repos send and
workspace change, and the hidden-vetting job.

Tests: dispatch claims the job's own domain and frees it when applied; a
job for a busy domain is refused unrun with the domain's busy message.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(community_context): its VTA work is a ContextJob on dispatch (#535)

The preview, delete, grant listing, grant and revoke jobs were ad-hoc
futures spawned after a claim helper that checked the session and the
domain together. They are now one ContextJob enum on the Job trait: the
session is checked first (same message), then dispatch claims and spawns,
and the panel is committed only once the claim succeeded — as before.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ci: gate PRs on the #[ignore]d e2e suites; document the policy (#537)

Also moves bip39 to openvtc-core's dev-dependencies: only the BIP32 tests use it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(changelog): the runtime restructure

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(join): the submit is past the point of no return; hold its community's replies; a flush survives an older save

From review of the runtime restructure:
- F10/Esc/an error during the submit stage wait for it instead of aborting
  it and forgetting a persona the community may now hold; a loop stop
  mid-submit keeps the persona and listener.
- Inbound messages from the community being submitted to are held until
  the pending record exists, then processed (the nested loop got this by
  not reading inbound).
- SaveScheduler::flush leaves the config dirty while an older background
  save is in flight, so that save cannot have the last word.
- Launch guards that found no persona/applicant now fail and undo instead
  of leaving the page locked.
- The 2 s VTA-sync tick republishes state again, so time-based displays
  keep moving.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: fix(vta-service): a TSP-only VTA boots (#937 follow-up)
body:
#937 let a VTA speak TSP without DIDComm: setup accepts TSP alone, and the
mediator connect supervisor opens for `services.didcomm || services.tsp`.
Two places in `server::run` were missed, so a TSP-only VTA set up that way
refused to start with "no services enabled — enable at least one of REST or
DIDComm":

- The pre-loop guard, and the restart loop's warning, counted only REST and
  DIDComm. Both now ask `any_transport_enabled`, which counts REST, DIDComm
  or TSP, each built and enabled. WebAuthn alone is still not a transport.
- `services.tsp` was migrated into the runtime state on first boot but never
  mirrored back at boot or on a soft restart, unlike REST and DIDComm, so
  `pnm services tsp {enable,disable}` did not survive a restart. It is now
  mirrored in both places, before the unbuilt-TSP check reads it.

## Testing
- New: `a_tsp_only_vta_has_a_transport`, `nothing_enabled_has_no_transport`
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 7594 passed
- workspace doctests, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `scripts/check-docs.py`: clean
- `cargo check -p vta-service --no-default-features --features rest`: clean

Found setting up a TSP-only did:webs VTA, which could not reach first boot to publish its DID.

title: ux: consistent keys, confirmations, input, status and connectivity from the repository review
body:
One pass over the UX findings from the repository review: one confirmation rule, one key table per view (drawn as the footer, listed by a new `?` overlay, checked against the handler by tests), one text-input behaviour, typed status severity, a layout that fits 80x24, honest notifications, classified connectivity failures with a retry, a wizard you can step back through, and consistent wording.

Commits are split by concern and each builds and passes the tests on its own:

1. `ux(status)` — #577
2. `ux(confirm)` — #579
3. `ux(keys)` — #580
4. `ux(input)` — #578 (+ a follow-up commit for setup paste)
5. `ux(layout)` — #576
6. `ux(notifications)` — #584
7. `ux(connectivity)` — #585
8. `ux(setup)` — #588
9. `docs(ui)` — #554
10. `docs(changelog)`

## Per issue

### #577 — typed status (rest of the issue)
- Every panel's `status_message` (communities, identity, vetting, inbox, relationships, credentials, settings, capabilities) and the device-access `message` are a typed `Status { severity, text }`. `Severity`/`Status` moved to `state_handler/main_page/status.rs` (re-exported where repos/rooms/elections had them) with one style table, `components::status::severity_style`.
- Severity is set at each producer (~250 sites reviewed; "nothing was done, and why" is `Warning`, in-flight sends are `Progress`, refusals/failures `Error`). `VettingAction::Status` and `SettingsAction::ClipboardCopied` carry a `Status`.
- The wording heuristic (`FAILURE_MARKERS` / `status_style`) is deleted; nothing decides colour from text any more. Forms' `error` fields render through `push_error` (the field is named for its severity).

### #579 — confirmations
- `ui/pages/main/confirm.rs`: `is_yes` (plain `y` only), `KEYS` ("y: confirm · any other key: cancel") and `prompt()`; every prompt uses them.
- y-only everywhere a destructive or outward-facing action was confirmed by `y` **or Enter**: community delete/leave/cancel-join, device-access revoke, Inbox dismiss/clear-all, relationship and credential remove, invitation credential delete/purge, agent-name remove, all persona confirmations, capability toggle, vetting abandon / delete-ticket / withdraw / decline (Enter on the decline note now just leaves the note), local-face delete, make-reusable, forget-contact.
- New confirmations: Inbox `r` reject (sent to the peer), Settings "Remove the unlock code", Communities `m` (issue VMC) and `R` (renew).
- Typed words stay for WIPE, RESET and context deletion.

### #580 — key map and `?`
- `ui/pages/main/keymap.rs`: a view declares its keys as `Binding`s (`k("d/Del", "delete")`); `keymap::footer` draws them in one format (`key: does · …`, wrapping rather than clipping) and advertises them for the frame. Labels use one vocabulary parsed into the `KeyCode`s they name, so a label cannot disagree with the key matched.
- `?` opens an overlay listing exactly the focused view's advertised keys plus the global table (any key closes it); the footer row and Help / Status's shortcut list are generated from the same global table.
- A key a view does not take shows "x does nothing here — ? lists this panel's keys" in the footer row. While a text field has focus, unhandled keys stay in the form (they no longer switch panels). Ctrl/Alt chords reach a view only where it lists them.
- Consistent keys: VTA invitations archive with `x` (was `r`), show-archived is `v` (was `i`), refresh is `r` (was Tab); Communities joins with `n` (was `j`) and `j`/`k` move there and in the menu. TSP Relationships gets a handler (↑/↓, Esc).
- Silent swallows removed or listed (Inbox `a`, credential `d`, VTA `u`, persona `d`, identity read-only views and pickers).
- `keymap_tests.rs` asserts, for each view, that the footer lists **exactly** the keys the handler takes (inbox list/detail, relationships list/detail/alias/new-request ×4 fields, credentials list/detail ×2, VTA ×4, communities ×4, settings ×2, Help/Status, TSP, all six identity tabs, capabilities loading/failed).

### #578 — text input
- `ui/pages/main/text_input.rs` lists every main-page string field once and edits it through `tui_input` (as setup/join do): visible cursor; ←/→, Ctrl+←/→, Home/End move inside the field; Backspace/Del; Ctrl+A/E/U/W/K edit; no chord types its letter (a chord the view lists, e.g. Ctrl+A "add owner", stays the view's).
- Paste inserts at the cursor on the main page and in setup (was append / replace). Typed confirmation words take no paste. Ballot text answers get a `BallotText` action so they edit like any field.
- Masked passphrase length counts characters, not bytes. The append-only `edit_text` and the per-panel paste code are gone.

### #576 — 80x24
- Activity log 4 rows below 32 rows; menu ≥ 23 columns and scrolls to the selection; footer row leads with `F10: quit` and `?: keys` and keeps only whole hints.
- Setup step 1 body scrolls (↑/↓, PgUp/PgDn) and the footer says so; the copy result takes the footer row.

### #584 — notifications
- Inbox badge counts inbound items only (not own outbound requests/pings); Communities (actions required) and Vetting (desk) get badges.
- Activity-log entries carry a severity (errors ✗ and warnings ! in colour; routine lines dim).
- Pong shown in the Relationships panel with latency; no pong in 30 s → a warning there and in the log, and the outbound ping task is expired.

### #585 — connectivity
- `MediatorStatus::Failed(ConnectionFailure { reason, class: ErrorClass })`; core's `ReconnectOutcome::Failed { reason, class }` (`class_of` the listener error; a listener that never connects is `Timeout`).
- Header: "✗ mediator unreachable / refused us / incompatible / not answering … · see Help". Help / Status: class, full reason, `ErrorClass::remedy()`, and `r` reconnects. Enter on the Settings mediator row reconnects. `SettingsAction::ReconnectMediator` no longer `#[allow(dead_code)]`.
- "Messaging unavailable — cannot X right now." names the class and remedy.
- Identity pane agent errors are typed (`AgentError { text, class }`); the holder-grant command is offered only for a refusal whose text names it — never for an unreachable agent (the old string-only decision).

### #588 — setup
- Esc goes back a page on every wizard page that has one (`navigation::previous_page`); back stops at the VTA once its one-time grant is spent; step 2 keeps its own back (it carries step 1's banner reason). Choice pages and the no-code warning say "[ESC] to go back".
- The setup DID is minted once per run: going back and forward keeps it, so a PNM grant still applies. (Still new on each relaunch — it is never written to disk; see leftovers.)
- One progress indicator: the header's sections. Boxes are named, not counted.

### #554 — wording
- British spelling in the American UI strings (unauthorised, recognised, Initialising, initialised, Finalised). Protocol/SDK/format text untouched.
- The profile secret is "unlock code" in Settings → Protection and the CLI prompt/`--unlock-code-file` errors (export passphrases keep their name).
- README glossary (persona, community/VTC, unlock code, Inbox, Help / Status); CONTRIBUTING wording convention. No persisted identifier or theme id renamed.

## User-visible behaviour changes

- Enter no longer confirms any destructive or outward-facing action; only `y` does, and any other key (Enter included) cancels.
- New `y` confirmations before: rejecting an Inbox request, removing the unlock code in Settings, issuing a VMC (`m`) and renewing a membership (`R`).
- Vetting: abandon / delete ticket / withdraw / decline are committed by `y`; Enter on the decline note moves off the note.
- Identity: deleting a local face, making a value reusable, and forgetting a contact are committed by `y` (were Enter).
- `?` opens a key overlay on the main page (outside text fields).
- A key that does nothing shows a one-line hint in the footer row.
- Footers everywhere use "key: does · key: does" and the same key names (`Enter`, not `⏎`).
- VTA panel: archive is `x` (was `r`), show archived is `v` (was `i`), refresh is `r` (was Tab).
- Communities: join is `n` (was `j`); `j`/`k` move the selection; same in the menu.
- TSP Relationships: ↑/↓ move the cursor, Esc returns to the menu.
- Text fields show a cursor; ←/→/Home/End move within them; Ctrl+A/E/U/W/K edit; Ctrl chords never type letters; Tab/←/→ in a field no longer switch panels.
- Paste inserts at the cursor (main page and setup).
- 80x24: activity log shrinks to 4 rows; the menu is wider and scrolls; the footer row starts with `F10: quit · ?: keys`.
- Setup step 1 scrolls; its copy result shows in the footer row.
- Inbox badge counts only inbound items; Communities and Vetting show badges.
- Activity log shows errors/warnings in colour with ✗ / !.
- Pings report their pong (or no reply after 30 s) in the Relationships panel; unanswered ping tasks expire.
- Header shows the class of a messaging failure and "see Help"; Help / Status shows the cause, the remedy and `r` to reconnect; Enter on Settings' mediator row reconnects.
- "Messaging unavailable" messages name the class and remedy.
- Setup: Esc goes back instead of clearing; boxes no longer show "Step x/y".
- Settings/CLI say "unlock code" for the profile secret.
- Status lines are coloured by severity (warnings orange, successes green, errors red/bold) — no longer by wording.

## Tests added

- Status: colour follows severity not wording; every severity distinct.
- Confirmation: table test — for 16 armed confirmations Enter never commits and `y` does; Inbox reject arms; remove-unlock-code arms.
- Key map: per-view exactness (footer ⇔ handler) for the views listed under #580; `?` lists the focused view's keys and the global ones and any key closes it; an unused key gives feedback; label parsing; footer wrapping.
- Input: insert at cursor, arrows, deletes, chords never insert, non-ASCII, cursor drawing; ← then type; paste at Home; Ctrl+U clears / Ctrl+T doesn't type.
- Layout: 80x24 render shows every menu item incl. Quit and `F10: quit`/`?: keys`; short terminal scrolls to Quit; setup step 1 at 80x24 scrolls to the F4 command and shows the copy result in the footer.
- Notifications: Inbox badge counts inbound only; activity log keeps severity.
- Connectivity: header per class (unreachable / rejected / incompatible); Help / Status shows cause + remedy and `r` reconnects; Settings mediator row reconnects.
- Setup: Esc walks back from step 1 to the start keeping the input.

Verified locally (rustc 1.100): `cargo fmt --all --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and with `--no-default-features`; `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --workspace --locked` and with `--no-default-features`; `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`; `cargo machete`.

## Not done here (follow-ups)

- #580: exactness tests do not yet cover the vetting forms/desk, repos, rooms, elections and the overlays; their footers are converted to the key table but vetting forms take Tab/arrows uniformly. Repos' "this machine" keys (`c e E s S u w f F R`) are still taken where they do not apply (the handler answers with a status saying why) and only the applicable ones are listed. `j`/`k` are movement in lists that do not use them as verbs; identity (`k` who it knows you as) and the vetting desk (`k` get tokens) keep theirs. Repos archive stays `A` (it archives the forge repository, `x` is revoke there).
- #578: identity forms keep their in-state `tui_input` (cursor movement works) but still draw the caret at the end of the field.
- #588: the setup DID is not persisted across a relaunch — writing an admin-capable private key to disk needs its own security review.
- #554: "community" vs "VTC" in UI prose is not swept beyond the glossary.

Closes #576
Closes #577
Closes #579
Closes #584
Closes #585
Closes #588
Part of #578
Part of #580
Part of #554

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no new clients; the ping reply window is a finite 30 s
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — confirmations only gate sends; ping-task expiry is local bookkeeping after the window
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — reconnect is operator-triggered, one at a time (existing in-flight domain)
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — unchanged
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — unchanged
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — no wire types changed
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — unchanged
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — R6.4: header, Help / Status, "Messaging unavailable" and the identity pane now name the failure class
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — ping expiry marks the config dirty after removal; nothing else persisted changed
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none

title: ux: consistent keys, confirmations, input, status and connectivity from the repository review (#606)
body:
ux: consistent keys, confirmations, input, status and connectivity from the repository review (#606)

* ux(status): typed status severity on every panel, drop the wording heuristic (#577)

Every main-page panel's status_message (communities, identity, vetting,
inbox, relationships, credentials, settings, capabilities) and the device
access view's message are now a typed Status { severity, text }. The
producer that knows whether its operation worked sets the severity; the
renderer colours by severity only. The string-prefix/marker heuristic in
components/status.rs is deleted.

Severity and Status move from main_page/repos.rs to main_page/status.rs
(re-exported where they were) so rooms, elections and repos share one
type and one style table (severity_style). Actions that carried a status
string (VettingAction::Status, SettingsAction::ClipboardCopied) carry a
Status.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ux(confirm): one confirmation rule — y confirms, any other key cancels (#579)

Destructive and outward-facing actions are armed by their key and
committed by y alone; Enter, the key that opened the view, now cancels
like any other key. Shared in ui/pages/main/confirm.rs (is_yes, KEYS,
prompt) and used by every prompt, which now reads
'y: confirm · any other key: cancel'.

Changed to y-only: community delete/leave/withdraw, device-grant revoke,
inbox dismiss/clear-all, relationship and credential remove, invitation
credential delete/purge, agent-name remove, persona confirmations,
capability toggle, vetting abandon/delete-ticket/withdraw/decline.

Now confirmed (previously sent on one key): Inbox reject (sent to the
peer), Settings remove passphrase, Communities m (issue VMC) and R
(renew). Typed-word confirmation stays for WIPE and RESET.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ux(keys): one key table per view drives the footer, a ? overlay and feedback (#580)

Every main-page view now builds its keys as a list of Bindings
(ui/pages/main/keymap.rs) and draws them with keymap::footer, which also
advertises them for the frame. The ? overlay lists exactly the advertised
keys of the focused view plus the global ones; the footer row and the
Help / Status shortcut list are generated from the same global table.

- one label vocabulary (Enter, Esc, Tab, Shift+Tab, arrows, Space, Del,
  Ctrl+X) parsed into the key codes it names, so a label cannot name a
  key it does not match; one format 'key: does · key: does'
- a key a view does not take shows 'x does nothing here — ? lists this
  panel's keys' in the footer row instead of vanishing; a text field keeps
  ←/→/Tab rather than switching panels; Ctrl/Alt chords reach a view only
  where it lists them
- consistent keys: archive is x (VTA invitations too), show archived is v
  (was i on the VTA panel), refresh is r (was Tab on the VTA panel);
  Communities joins with n, and j/k move there as in rooms, elections and
  the menu
- TSP Relationships gets a key handler (↑/↓, Esc)
- silent swallows removed (inbox a, credential d, VTA u, persona d,
  identity read-only overlays and pickers); local-face delete, make
  reusable and forget-contact now confirm with y only
- keymap_tests checks, per view, that the footer lists exactly the keys
  the handler takes (inbox, relationships, credentials, VTA, communities,
  settings, help, TSP, identity tabs, capabilities)

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ux(input): one text-input behaviour for the main page's forms (#578)

Every string field on the main page (relationship request, alias and
witness; credential reason; settings name, export/import path and the
typed WIPE/RESET words; vetting text fields; the device-grant form; the
context-delete word; the repos forms; ballot text answers) is listed
once in ui/pages/main/text_input.rs and edited there through tui_input,
the editor the setup and join screens use:

- a visible cursor; ←/→, Ctrl+←/→, Home/End move within the field instead
  of switching panels; Backspace/Del delete either side; Ctrl+A/E/U/W/K
  edit; no Ctrl or Alt chord types its letter (a chord the view lists as
  its own, such as Ctrl+A 'add owner', stays the view's)
- a paste is inserted at the cursor in every field that takes one (it was
  appended on the main page); the typed confirmation words take no paste
- the masked passphrase length counts characters, not bytes
- ballot text answers get a BallotText action so they edit like any field
- the append-only edit_text helper and the per-panel paste code go

Tests: editor semantics (insert at cursor, arrows, deletes, chords,
non-ASCII), cursor drawing, ← then type, paste at Home, Ctrl+U/Ctrl+T.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ux(layout): nothing essential is clipped at 80x24 (#576)

- the activity log takes 4 rows instead of 8 below 32 rows, so all twelve
  menu items fit at 24 rows; the menu also scrolls to keep the selection
  on screen on anything shorter
- the menu is at least 23 columns wide (its longest item and a badge), so
  'My Relationships', 'TSP Relationships', 'My Credentials' and
  'Help / Status' are no longer cut at 80 columns
- the footer row is built from the global key table with F10 quit and ?
  first, and keeps only whole hints that fit
- setup step 1 (Run the PNM command): the actions-and-commands body scrolls
  with ↑/↓ and PgUp/PgDn, the footer says so when it can, and the copy
  result takes the footer row instead of the end of the body
- tests: 80x24 TestBackend renders of the main page (every menu item and
  'F10: quit' visible) and setup step 1 (scrolls to the F4 command; copy
  result in the footer row)

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ux(notifications): inbound-only Inbox badge, badges for arrivals, ping results (#584)

- the Inbox badge counts what was sent to the user (requests, issued
  credentials, information, vetting), not their own outbound requests or
  pings; Communities shows its actions-required count and Vetting the
  requests on the desk, as badges of their own
- activity-log entries carry a severity: errors (log_error) and warnings
  are drawn in their colour with a glyph (✗ / !), routine lines stay dim
- a pong is reported in the Relationships panel ('Pong from X (N ms) —
  they are reachable.'), not only in the log; a ping with no pong in 30 s
  says so there ('No reply to the ping after 30 s …'), is logged as a
  warning, and its outbound task is expired so it does not sit in the
  Inbox
- tests: badge counts inbound only; log keeps each entry's severity

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ux(connectivity): classify the header's failure and offer a retry (#585)

- MediatorStatus::Failed carries a ConnectionFailure { reason, class }
  with the typed openvtc_core::errors::ErrorClass; ReconnectOutcome::Failed
  carries the class too (class_of the listener error; a listener that never
  connects is a Timeout)
- the header shows the class ('✗ mediator unreachable', 'mediator refused
  us', 'mediator incompatible', 'mediator not answering', …) and 'see
  Help' instead of 17 characters of error text; Help / Status shows the
  class, the full reason and the class's remedy, and r there reconnects
- SettingsAction::ReconnectMediator is live: Enter on the Settings mediator
  row ('[Enter to reconnect]') and r on Help / Status; its
  #[allow(dead_code)] is gone
- 'Messaging unavailable — cannot X right now.' now names the class and
  the remedy, and points at the retry
- the identity pane's agent errors are typed (AgentError { text, class }):
  the holder-grant hint is offered only for a refusal (AuthRejected /
  Refused) whose text names the holder credential, never for an
  unreachable agent; other failures show their class's remedy
- tests: header per class, Help / Status cause + r, mediator row Enter

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ux(setup): Esc goes back on every wizard page, one progress indicator (#588)

- Esc goes back a page on every setup page that has one
  (setup_flow::navigation::previous_page), instead of clearing the field:
  ConfigImport and VTA DID go back to the start, step 1 (PNM command) to
  the VTA DID, the context-occupied warning to step 1, the unlock-code
  pages to the unlock-code choice, the token pages to the page before.
  Back stops at the VTA once its one-time grant is spent. Step 2 keeps its
  own back (it carries the reason for step 1's banner). Choice pages and
  the no-code warning say '[ESC] to go back'; the input pages' '[ESC] to
  clear input' now reads '[ESC] to go back'.
- going back keeps what was typed and the setup DID: the ephemeral setup
  key is minted once per run, so a PNM grant already made for it still
  applies after going back and forward (it is still new each relaunch:
  it is never written to disk)
- one progress indicator: the header's 'Section n/4'; the boxes are named
  ('Run the PNM command', 'Connect to the VTA', 'Enter unlock code', …)
  instead of carrying their own 'Step x/y' counters that disagreed with it
- test: Esc walks back from step 1 to the start keeping the context id

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(ui): British spelling and one name per concept in UI strings (#554)

- British spelling in the user-visible strings that were American:
  unauthorised (unlock-code page), recognised (token scan),
  'Initialising:' (header, Inbox, Help / Status), 'not initialised',
  'Finalised'. Protocol and SDK text keeps its own spelling (the VTA's
  'is not authorized on' is matched verbatim; theme 'color' keys and
  'organization' JSON are formats).
- the profile's secret is the 'unlock code' everywhere: Settings →
  Protection ('Set an unlock code', 'Remove the unlock code (keyring
  only)', 'Unlock code:'), its log lines, and the CLI unlock prompt and
  --unlock-code-file errors. An export file's 'passphrase' is a different
  secret and keeps its name.
- README gains a Glossary (persona, community/VTC, unlock code, Inbox,
  Help / Status); CONTRIBUTING states the wording convention (British
  spelling, one name per concept, one key vocabulary via keymap::Binding).
- Persisted identifiers and theme ids are unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(changelog): the UX consistency changes (#576 #577 #578 #579 #580 #584 #585 #588 #554)

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ux(input): a paste in setup is inserted at the cursor too (#578)

Setup's text fields replaced their whole content with a paste while the
main page appended it; both now insert at the cursor.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

### Build & CI

- **deps**: Affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.47, TDK 0.45, trust-tasks 0.39 and mediator 0.52, with delivery receipts and mediator wake ([#2741](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2741))

* build(deps)!: move to affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.47, affinidi-tdk 0.45 and trust-tasks 0.39

  affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.47.2 (-core 0.1.12, -delivery 0.2.0), affinidi-tdk
  0.45 with what it carries (affinidi-crypto 0.3, data-integrity 0.8.7,
  did-common 0.4.7, vc 0.3, sd-jwt 0.2, sd-jwt-vc 0.3, mdoc 0.6,
  oid4vc-core 0.1.11), trust-tasks-* 0.39 (the SDK's own copy, so one
  trust-tasks-rs across the boundary) and mediator 0.52 (test-mediator,
  -admin, -tui).

  affinidi-sd-jwt 0.2 builds the kb-jwt verifier from the credential's own
  cnf.jwk and requires aud, nonce and a fresh iat: the VTC's OpenID4VP
  verifier now checks the kb-jwt iat (600 s, RFC 9901 §7.3), which it did
  not before.

  SchemaValidator, so the private jsonschema 0.46 copy
  (jsonschema-trust-tasks) is gone. CompiledSchema is removed and
  SchemaError is trust_tasks_rs::validate::ValidationError.

  cargo deny: the fancy-regex skip goes; jsonschema and jsonwebtoken stay
  duplicated upstream (trust-tasks-rs 0.39 on jsonschema 0.49,
  trust-tasks-https 0.39 on jsonwebtoken 10).
