title: refactor(state_handler): split vetting_actions and persona_actions along their seams
body:
Mechanical split of the two largest `state_handler` modules into directory modules along the seams listed in #532.

**No behaviour change.** Code is moved, not rewritten. The only edits are the ones the move forces:
- `mod` declarations and `use` paths
- `pub(super)` on items a sibling module now uses (plus the fields of `SendJob`, `Presenting` and `CardJob`, which `send`/`faces` build)
- `pub(crate) use` re-exports in each `mod.rs`, so every outside path (`state_handler::vetting_actions::X`, `state_handler::persona_actions::X`) still resolves. No caller outside the two modules was edited.
- intra-doc links to items now in a sibling module get an explicit target, so `cargo doc` with `-D warnings` stays clean
- the `include_str!` fixture path in a vetting test gets one more `../`, because the file is one directory deeper
- each `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` moved beside the code it tests; fixtures shared across test modules live in a `#[cfg(test)] test_support.rs`

Test count for the `openvtc` bin: **1049 before, 1049 after** (`cargo test -p openvtc --bin openvtc -- --list`). Every test is kept; only their module paths changed.

Two commits: the first is a pure `git mv` of each file to `<name>/mod.rs`, so history follows. The second moves code out of `mod.rs`. `git diff --color-moved` and `git blame -C -C` show the moved blocks.

## Layout

### `state_handler/vetting_actions/` (was 8,733 lines)

| File | Lines | Contents |
|---|---:|---|
| `mod.rs` | 37 | module docs, `mod` declarations, re-exports |
| `words.rs` | 1,087 | display wording: grants, hidden-vetting standing, tokens, next steps, requirements (`outlook_words`, `get_tokens_words`, `community_display`, `progress_line`, …), plus their tests |
| `view_sync.rs` | 741 | `sync` and `sync_journey`, which rebuild the view model from the book, plus tests |
| `dispatch.rs` | 812 | `dispatch`, form navigation (`input`, `back`, `move_field`, `cycle`), `submit`, plus the `page`/`status`/`persist` helpers and a test |
| `send.rs` | 108 | `begin`, `abandon`, `persona_did`, `resolver`, `sign_and_send`, `spawn_send` |
| `applicant.rs` | 663 | applicant side: start/abandon an application, switch path, request a vetter, vetter directory, plus a test |
| `faces.rs` | 788 | faces at the VTA: new-face form, list/wear faces, `send_card`, `preview_refusal`, plus tests |
| `vetter.rs` | 366 | the vetter's directory profile, event-mode and resend requests, plus a test |
| `tickets.rs` | 636 | `ticket_check`, issue/mint/delete tickets, `settle_pending_tickets`, plus tests |
| `desk.rs` | 653 | vetter desk: `open_session`, `attest`, `decline`, `withdraw`, `refresh_vetter_side`, `refresh_stale_modes`, `desk_open` |
| `hidden.rs` | 396 | hidden vetting: `hidden_vetting_tick`, `ensure_hidden_vetter`, `attest_hidden`, `ask_for_challenge` |
| `pcs.rs` | 699 | PCS work at the VTA: `pcs_work_due`, `start_pcs_work`, `apply_pcs_outcome`, recovery and inbound handling |
| `jobs.rs` | 534 | `Sent`, `SendJob`, `FaceJob`, `CardJob` |
| `outcome.rs` | 831 | `VettingOutcome` and its `apply`, `sent_result`, plus tests |
| `answers.rs` | 687 | community answers, directory rows, `expire_queries`, grant checks, journey focus, plus tests |

title: chore: manifests, dependency hygiene and CI hardening from the repository review
body:
One PR for four review issues. Each claim was checked against current `main` (aa9fed6), not against the commit the issues were written on.

## #544: manifest comments

- In the root `Cargo.toml`, `openvtc/Cargo.toml`, `openvtc-core/Cargo.toml` and `deny.toml`, each dependency's comment is now at most about 5 lines stating the current invariant: what it follows, what must move in lockstep, and the `cargo tree` check that proves it. The version-by-version history is gone; git history and `CHANGELOG.md` already hold it.
- Fixed the contradictions the issue lists: `dtg-credentials` ("0.11 / patch block"), `dirs` ("held at 6"), the `vta-sdk` header ("the 0.38 line"), `trust-tasks-rs` ("0.20 → 0.21"), `did-git-sign` ("floor 0.4.10 / 0.4.14"), the core dev-dep's "vta-sdk 0.56", and the conflicting histories in `deny.toml`.
- Other stale claims I found and corrected:
  - The `argon2` 0.5 duplicate comes from `pgp`, not from the mediator crates.
  - The keyring-store comments still described a per-binary store. Stores are now registered by `vta_sdk::keyring_init::install_default_store`, and keyutils is only the migration path.
- Every "one node" claim was checked with `cargo tree -i <crate> -e normal,build,dev`: dtg-credentials, trust-tasks-rs, trust-tasks-capability-client, vta-sdk, didwebvh-rs, affinidi-messaging-sdk, affinidi-tdk, dirs, vti-common, agent-names and the net-guard crates each have exactly one node.
- No dependency version or feature changed under this item.

## #538: dependency hygiene

1. **`deprecated = "allow"` removed** from `[workspace.lints.rust]`. Clippy under the default, `--no-default-features`, `dev-overrides` and `arbitrary` feature sets gives zero deprecation warnings: since #512 nothing uses the prebuilt spec modules. So no `#[allow(deprecated)]` was needed anywhere.
2. **Unused dependencies removed**, confirmed by `cargo machete`, a clean build, and cargo 1.100's own `unused_dependencies` manifest lint:
   - `openvtc`: aes-gcm, byteorder, card-backend-pcsc, hex, multibase, regex, serde_json_canonicalizer, sha2, sysinfo.
   - `openvtc`: apple-native, dbus-secret-service and windows-native keyring stores. No code references them; `vta-sdk`'s `keyring` feature pulls the same crates with the same features (`keychain` included, checked with `cargo tree -e features`). `linux-keyutils-keyring-store` stays because it is used directly.
   - `openvtc-core`: x25519-dalek.
   - **Now optional under `openpgp-card`**, because a `--no-default-features` build never uses them: `pgp` in both crates, `byteorder` in `openvtc-core`, `x25519-dalek` in `openvtc`.
   - Dropped the unused `description` / `readme` from `[workspace.package]` (cargo warned about them; both crates set their own). The workspace `version` is untouched.
3. **`sysinfo`** is now `default-features = false, features = ["system"]` (0.40.1, per `Cargo.lock`). `process_lock` refreshes only the one PID the lock file names, through `refresh_processes_specifics(ProcessesToUpdate::Some(&[pid]), …)` in a small `pid_is_alive` helper with a unit test. Before, it built a `System` over the whole process table.
4. **tokio features declared**:
   - Workspace: `macros`, `rt-multi-thread`, `signal`, `sync`, `time`.
   - Dev-dependencies add only what tests use: `net` and `io-util` for the loopback listeners, `test-util` for the paused clock.
5. **`did-git-sign` / `vgi-core` moved into `[workspace.dependencies]`**. Both crates were pinning them separately.
6. **Duplicates (dalek 2/3, rand 0.8/0.9/0.10, etc.)**: note only, as scoped. `pgp` 0.21.1 and `openpgp-card-rpgp` 0.9.1 are now published but still require `rand ^0.8` and `x25519-dalek ^2`. So a coordinated `pgp` move is possible, but it doesn't resolve the dalek/rand duplicates. This is recorded in `dependabot.yml`.
7. **`unsafe_code = "deny"`** at workspace level, with one `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` on the `libc::poll` in `openvtc/src/theme/terminal.rs`. `openvtc-core` keeps its `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`, and its test-only `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` for `env::set_var` is unchanged.

## #539: CI

- `concurrency` group `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}`, with `cancel-in-progress` only for `pull_request`. Pushes to main and release branches are never cancelled, because `nightly.yml` reads those runs.
- `timeout-minutes` on every `ci.yml` job:
  - fmt / machete: 10
  - audit / deny: 15
  - doc: 45
  - clippy, test-no-default-features, test-dev-overrides, bench, msrv: 60
  - test (3-OS): 90
  - coverage: 120
  - `verify-trust.yml` also gets 15. The other workflows already had timeouts.
- `--locked` on every cargo build/test/clippy/check/doc/bench/llvm-cov call in `ci.yml`. `publish-crates.py` already passes `--locked` to `cargo package` and `cargo publish`.
- New clippy step with `--no-default-features`, added to the existing **Clippy** job so the job name, and any required check on it, stays the same.
- The MSRV job now runs `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked`.
- New `machete` job running `cargo-machete@0.9.2` through the already-pinned `taiki-e/install-action`.
- The "Add swap" step, pasted nine times, is now a local composite action, `.github/actions/add-swap`. Every third-party action is still SHA-pinned; no new ones were added.
- `actionlint` is clean.

## #572: supply chain

1. **Advisory lists reconciled.** `deny.toml` and `.cargo/audit.toml` now carry the same IDs with the same reasons, and each file says to keep them in step. Each is dated 2026-11-15.
   - **Kept:** RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (rsa, via pgp), 2026-0173 (proc-macro-error2, dev graph only), 2026-0387 (crypto-bigint 0.5, via pgp).
   - **Pruned, because they no longer match `Cargo.lock`:** 2026-0097 (rand 0.8.8 is patched), 2024-0370, 2025-0134, 2026-0194/0195 (quick-xml is 0.41), and 2024-0436 (paste is gone; cargo-deny was warning `advisory-not-detected`).
   - **The one documented difference:** RUSTSEC-2026-0330/0331 (libcrux-kem) stay in `audit.toml` only. libcrux-kem is in `Cargo.lock` as an optional dependency of `hpke-rs-libcrux` that no enabled feature builds. cargo-audit scans the lockfile and flags it; cargo-deny checks the built graph and never sees it.
   - The stale "aes-gcm 0.10" comment is gone.
2. **verify-trust.** The action SHA is confirmed to be the `v0.29.0` tag. `version: v0.16.0` is a real but older binary release. The comment claiming they come from the same release is replaced with an accurate one: before enabling, move `version:` to the action's release in the same change, and check that the registry grants use the `github.com/...` resource form. The action and `version:` are both unchanged.
3. **Silent skip.** Commented in place: the job is not a required check yet, and once dogfooded it should fail when unconfigured. Left that way on purpose.
4. **Dependabot ignores.** Added a dated re-check note (2026-11-15) covering the three held crates, their link to the pgp-borne advisories, and the newly published `pgp` 0.21.1 / `openpgp-card-rpgp` 0.9.1.
5. **Backport token scope.** This can't be verified from the repository. Please confirm `RELEASE_TOKEN` is a fine-grained token scoped to contents + pull requests on this repo only.

## Left out

- **Coverage floor (#539):** not added. It needs a threshold agreed first.
- **The duplicates item (#538.6):** note only, as above.
- **`cargo semver-checks`:** has no `--locked` added.

## Checks run (Rust 1.100.0, macOS aarch64)

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked --no-default-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --locked --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings`
- `cargo clippy -p openvtc-core --all-targets --locked --no-default-features --features arbitrary -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace --locked`, the same with `--no-default-features`, and `cargo test -p openvtc --locked --features dev-overrides`
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --locked`
- `cargo +1.95.0 check --workspace --all-targets --locked` (MSRV)
- `cargo deny check`: advisories, bans, licenses and sources all ok. The remaining warnings are `multiple-versions` duplicates and two existing `license-not-encountered`.
- `cargo audit`: clean, no warnings.
- `cargo machete`: clean.
- `actionlint`: clean.

The Linux and Windows builds were not run locally; CI covers them.

Closes #544
Closes #538
Closes #539
Closes #572

title: fix(net): network and identity safety from the repository review
body:
PR 2 of the remediation plan on #589: network and identity safety.

Closes #571, closes #558, closes #573, closes #562, closes #561, closes #560, closes #559. Part of #557.

## Changes

**Agent names (#571)**
- A claim, park, resume or remove no longer caches `format!("{host}/@{name}")` as a verified name. It calls the new `Config::forget_cached_agent_name`, so the background sweep re-verifies with the full round-trip. Opening the overlay (no change) leaves a verified name alone. The now-unused `host` field on the job/outcome is removed.
- A name pulled from VTA state sync is stored unchanged, so it projects to the same record and is not pushed back. Its DID is also added to a new local-only set, `ProtectedConfig::agent_names_unverified` (serde default, skipped when empty). `cached_agent_name` returns `None` for those DIDs, the refresh targets include them, and `set_cached_agent_name` clears the mark. Marking the synced entry stale instead would have made devices push it back and forth.

**Peer-advertised answers (#558)**
- New crate-private `foreign_http::read_text_capped`: a `Content-Length` pre-check, then vta-sdk's `read_body_capped`, at `DEFAULT_MAX_FOREIGN_BODY` (2 MiB). It is used for the join-manifest fetch and the ballot-box answer. An oversize answer maps to `Unreadable`, not `Unreachable`; for a cast, resending would not change it. Tests cover declared, chunked and in-cap bodies.

**#573**
- `post_cast` uses `EndpointPolicy::public_only()`. `process_default()` honoured `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS` in release builds.
- New `display::webvh_path_tail`, built on `WebVHURL::parse_did_url` (a `did:scid` is read through `webvh_did`). `health`'s `short_tail` uses it. A path-less `did:webvh` now shows `host[:port]`, not `host%3Aport`, and a `did:key` is shown whole.
- `rebuild_apply` builds the sub-context id with `build_sub_context_id`, so it is validated and slugified. **Behaviour change:** a rebuilt `did:scid` community's placeholder id is `top/qmv` (lowercase) rather than `top/QmV`, and a path-less `did:webvh` gets its SCID token rather than its host.

**#562** `agent_name::resolve_identifier` is bounded at `IDENTIFIER_RESOLVE_TIMEOUT` (15 s) and returns `Unreachable` on timeout. That covers the relationships form, the join entry and the witness job. The join screen shows "Resolving …". The relationships form gets the bound but no live status, because its dispatch has no state sender.

**#561** `send_message_via` clones the ATM and DID out, then packs after the read guard drops, as `pickup_stored` does.

**#560**
- The four TSP discovery helpers in `config/mod.rs` share one local-mode `DIDCacheClient` (`tokio::sync::OnceCell`), so the document cache is actually used.
- The status-list client (`shared_status_client`) and the manifest client (one per `ProbePolicy`) are built once.

**#557 (part)**
- A persona's VTA-held keys are fetched concurrently (`try_join_all`). vta-sdk 0.80's DIDComm session demuxes replies by `thid` (`didcomm_session.rs`, the F5 fix), so the comment that kept these sequential is stale and has been removed. Nothing is inserted unless every key loads.
- The relationship-key fan-out is capped at 8 at once.
- Not done: loading several personas in parallel. `load_step2` threads `&mut TDK` through each persona, so that needs restructuring.

**#559** `health` resolves and probes up to 4 parties at once (`buffered`), and a party's endpoints are probed together. Progress is buffered per party and replayed in order, so the output still reads one party at a time.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)
- A newly claimed agent name is displayed once the background sweep (≤ 5 min) has verified it. It no longer shows immediately.
- A name synced from another device is not shown until this device has verified it.
- Peer-advertised answers over 2 MiB are refused.
- No wire types or config formats changed. The new `ProtectedConfig` field is optional and omitted when empty.

## Testing
New tests: `foreign_http` (3), `display::webvh_path_tail` (2), `rebuild_apply` sub-context naming (2), `health_cmd` short-tail cases, `vta_sync::a_synced_agent_name_is_not_shown_until_verified_here`, and agent-name overlay tests (a change forgets the name; a plain listing keeps it).

Local, all exit 0: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (with and without `--no-default-features`), `cargo test --workspace` (with and without `--no-default-features`), `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`. Not tried against a live stack.

## Pre-merge checklist
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): the shared clients keep their existing timeouts; identifier resolution gains one
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): #561 fixed
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the cache changes are local
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): fan-outs bounded (8 keys, 4 health parties); no retries added
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): unchanged
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): unchanged
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): none; the synced agent-name record is unchanged
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): ballot box pinned to public hosts; unverified names are not shown
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): #571
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): a forgotten name is re-verified by the next sweep
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: docs: refresh user and contributor docs from the repository review
body:
Documentation refresh from the repository review. No code changes; two `Cargo.toml` metadata edits and a LICENSE copy in each crate. No `version` field is touched.

## What changed

**#540 — command reference**
- `docs/openvtc-tool-commands.md` rewritten from `cli.rs` and the `*_cmd.rs` files: `setup` (wizard and headless `--vta-did` / `--unlock-code-file` / `--context` / `--wait`), `health` (`--vtc`, `--json`, `--recoverable`, `--allow-private-probes`), `theme {list,set,import,new,export}`, `community join`, `repo {list,clone,sign}`.
- Global options now include `--unlock-code-file`, `--monochrome` and `--invitation`; `-u/--unlock-code` is marked deprecated. `--profile` is documented as accepted before or after the subcommand (made global in #597).
- Environment variables listed in one table (none appear in `--help`); notes there are no shell completions.
- "Planned commands" removed here and in the README; the TUI section names the real main menu.

**#541 — onboarding and user guides**
- README getting-started now describes the VTA flow: setup connects to a VTA and authorises via PNM; the persona DID is created through the VTA on the first community join; headless `setup --vta-did …` and `community join` shown; `openvtc health` for checking. Self-hosted `did.jsonl`, "default mediator" and the domain prerequisite removed.
- `cargo install openvtc` added (README and `openvtc/README.md`); Windows config path corrected to `%APPDATA%\openvtc` (`dirs::config_dir()`); `dev-overrides` added to the feature table.
- `docs/multiple-didweb-same-domain.md` deleted.
- `docs/backup-restore.md` rewritten around Settings → Export Config, setup → Recover from backup, and recovery from the VTA Trust Context (`health --recoverable`, the [R] recover path and its known gaps).
- `docs/relationships-vrcs.md`: CLI snippets replaced with My Relationships / Inbox / My Credentials panel and key instructions; dead anchors removed; behaviour the code no longer has (validity prompts, alias on accept) removed.

**#542 — `did-git-sign` is not in this workspace**
- Crate rows and the old "DID Git Signing" section removed from the README; replaced with: set up from the Repos view or `openvtc repo sign`, `cargo install did-git-sign`, link to verifiable-git-infrastructure.
- CLAUDE.md project overview, CONTRIBUTING architecture, SECURITY scope and the core README corrected. The stale `cli2` comment on the `did-git-sign` dependency in `openvtc/Cargo.toml` rewritten.

**#543 — SECURITY.md (remainder)**
- Scope: workspace crates are `openvtc-core` and `openvtc`; TSP named alongside DIDComm; signer and VTI service reports pointed at their repos.
- Security design: VTA key backend (credential bundle stored locally, keys managed by the VTA), legacy BIP32, the `OPENVTC_SECURE_STORE=file` store, plaintext protection only after a warning, and the activity log being in the plaintext tier.
- `docs/secured-configuration-management.md` and `docs/secure-key-management.md` lead with the VTA backend, call the BIP32 seed legacy, and describe the unlock-code KDF (Argon2id).

**#545** — `docs/releasing.md` deleted; its one unique fact (`openvtc-vetting-pcs` published up to 0.6.0, no longer in the workspace) moved into `RELEASES.md`. No other file linked to it.

**#546** — `docs/openvtc-config-data-structure.md` replaced with a short layer overview (public / protected / secured; Account → personas → communities; key backends; how the protected config is encrypted) that links to docs.rs for field detail.

**#550 — `tasks/` and `docs/design/`**
- `tasks/follow-ups.md`: ticked the join-submit size guard, `include_sensitive`, and VTC reply-proof verification (each confirmed in code); D4 stub-VP statements updated to `build_join_vp` with "needs re-scoping" (also in `tasks/d4-scoping.md`); drifted file pointers fixed.
- `tasks/vtc-client-migration-scoping.md`: note that it was verified against vta-sdk 0.42.1 / vtc-client 0.6.7, not re-checked against 0.80.
- Broken relative links fixed in `tasks/archive/{plan,todo}.md`, `t1-active-identity-api.md`, `multi-community-support.md`.
- `docs/design/README.md` indexes all documents with their own status; T1 and multi-community set to IMPLEMENTED; references to files no longer in this repo corrected or annotated.
- `docs/README.md` now indexes every guide in `docs/`.

**#551 — MSRV, CLA, duplication**
- MSRV set to 1.95.0 (README badge and prerequisites, core README badge); CONTRIBUTING points at `rust-version` in `Cargo.toml`.
- CLA references removed (CONTRIBUTING, README); the DCO requirement is stated once in CONTRIBUTING.
- README "Workspace Layout / Building / Testing / PR Guidelines" removed; README links to CONTRIBUTING, which gained the one unique line ("TBD — help wanted").

**#552 — crates.io metadata**
- Both crates: real `description`, `homepage`, `documentation`, `keywords`, `categories`.
- `LICENSE` copied into each crate directory so the published packages carry it.
- `openvtc-core/README.md` rewritten: module table and the "maintainer list exchange" claim replaced with a docs.rs pointer and a short usage snippet; absolute URLs; env-var table formatting fixed.
- `openvtc/README.md`: `cargo install openvtc`, absolute GitHub URLs for docs links, overview lists the current panels.

**#553 — CHANGELOG convention**
- `## [0.7.0] - 2026-11-05 (cut to release/0.7)` → `## [0.7.0] - 2026-11-05`. Both `release_lib.py` (`^## (\[v\]|v)( |$)`) and `release-tag.yml` (prefix match on `## [v]`) still match it.
- Released sections: non-standard `###` headings renamed to Keep a Changelog names, keeping the old name as a `####` sub-heading (e.g. `### Breaking` → `### Changed` / `#### Breaking`); "Major changes" summaries fold into the release intro. Headings only; no entry text changed or moved. `[Unreleased]` is untouched.
- CONTRIBUTING states the convention going forward: fixed section names, two to three lines per entry, PR number.

## Not done
- `openvtc-core/examples/encrypt_decrypt.rs` still uses `derive_passphrase_key`. Switching it to `derive_passphrase_key_v2` is a code change that should be compiled; left for a follow-up. (The v1 KDF is still the one the unlock code uses; v2 is used for exports.)
- `authors` in `Cargo.toml` left as is.
- No drift test for the command reference, no `clap_complete`, no `.env()` annotations, no `check-release-guards.py` checks (all suggested in the issues; they are code changes).

title: fix(tui): user-facing bugs from the repository review
body:
PR 1 of the remediation plan on #589: the user-facing bugs, kept small enough to backport to `release/0.7`.

Closes #574, closes #563, closes #575, closes #577, closes #581, closes #583, closes #586, closes #587.

## Changes

**Unlock code length (#574) and key derivation off the render task (#563)**
- The setup wizard and backup import check the minimum length (`validate_passphrase`) before accepting a new unlock code. Every unlock path already required 8, so a shorter code locked the profile for good.
- Unlocking now uses the new `UnlockCode::for_existing`, which derives without the length check. A short code set by an earlier release therefore still opens its profile, and the user is told to set a longer one. A short code that does *not* open the profile still gets the "too short" message from #590.
- Setup sends the code to the handler (`Action::SetUnlockCode`), which derives it with `derive_passphrase_key_blocking` and then creates the account. The unused `SetProtection` action and `NavResult::SendActionThenCompleteSetup` are removed. Import runs inside `block_in_place`, so the render task keeps drawing while Argon2 runs.
- Import refuses a backup protected by an unlock code when no valid new code is given. Before, it derived a key from an empty string.

**Token Factory Reset (#575)**
- Enter on Factory Reset opens a confirmation that names the card (identifier and manufacturer) and warns when that card protects this profile. `RESET` must be typed to proceed. With no card, or more than one, nothing is offered. The card is looked up again at confirm time, and nothing is erased if it changed.

**Status colour (#577)**
- `status_style` matches failure wording anywhere in the message, case-insensitively ("couldn't", "unavailable", "not available", …). Anything else uses the plain text colour instead of success green. Moving all ~200 `status_message` sites to a typed `Status` is UX-consistency work and is left to PR 8 of the plan.

**Passphrase forms (#586)**
- Export Config has a Confirm field. Export and Change Protection report an empty, short or mismatched passphrase in the form rather than ignoring Enter, and the length-only "may not match" hint is gone. Enter on the first passphrase field moves to Confirm. The Import footer now says "import". Not done: the suggested verify-by-decrypt step after export.

**Diagnostics (#581)**
- `openvtc --setup` → `openvtc setup`. "Settings -> Import / Restore Backup" → `openvtc setup` then Restore Backup (the profile cannot load in that state), or "Settings -> Import Config" on the loading screen. "Config Protection" → "Protection".
- `--profile` is `global(true)`, so `openvtc health --profile X` (as the diagnostics print it) works.
- A new test extracts every `` `openvtc …` `` command the diagnostics emit, for each error class, and parses it with `cli()`.

**Stdout and non-terminal use (#583)**
- The `OPENVTC_CONFIG_PROFILE` notices go to stderr.
- With stdin or stdout not a terminal, the interactive path stops before the unlock prompt and lists the headless commands.

**Signals and terminal restore (#587)**
- SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP all go through the terminator (`Interrupted::OsSignal(name)` replaces `OsSigInt`). That gives them the graceful shutdown: final save, lock release, terminal restore.
- The panic hook and normal exit share `reset_terminal`, which also turns off bracketed paste and shows the cursor.
- F10 is no longer swallowed on the join DID page while it is processing. It takes effect when the in-flight resolve ends. Cancelling the resolve itself needs the join flow on the main loop (#529, PR 9).
- A user quit prints nothing. Signal and error exits explain themselves on stderr.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)
- Status messages that are not failures are drawn in the plain text colour, not green.
- `openvtc` with stdin or stdout redirected now exits with an error instead of drawing the TUI.
- Exit messages moved to stderr, and a normal quit prints none.
- No wire types or config formats changed. `openvtc-core` gains `UnlockCode::for_existing` and `openpgp_card::card_identity` (additive).

## Testing

New tests: `cli::tests::every_command_the_diagnostics_suggest_parses`, `profile_is_accepted_before_or_after_a_subcommand`, `status::tests::failures_without_an_error_prefix_are_red`, `secured_config::tests::a_short_existing_code_still_unlocks`, an updated navigation test for `SetUnlockCode`, and updated export/import form tests (export tabs through 3 fields).

Local, all exit 0: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (with and without `--no-default-features`), `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`, `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`.

Not run interactively: the token reset confirmation (no card to hand), the signal paths, and the setup and import screens. They are covered only by the unit tests above and by reading the code.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no network code touched
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): local only
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries added
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): unchanged
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): unchanged
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): none
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): a failed key derivation in setup stops before account creation rather than falling back to plaintext; token reset refuses on any doubt about the card
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): failures no longer render as success (#577); forms say why they did not submit
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): SIGTERM/SIGHUP now take the graceful path that flushes the save
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: vti-trust-task-server-v0.11.0
body:
### Build & CI

- **deps**: Enforce cargo-deny bans/sources, drop unused deps, hoist shared deps, forbid unsafe ([#2708](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2708))

* build(deps): enforce cargo-deny bans/sources, drop unused deps, hoist shared deps, forbid unsafe

  pgp, openssl only via webauthn-rs 0.5, no wildcards, and
  multiple-versions = "deny" with a skip list of today's duplicates grouped by
  cause. The two advisory ignores cargo-deny reports as not detected
  (RUSTSEC-2026-0381, RUSTSEC-2024-0436) are removed, the stale [graph]
  comment rewritten, and the yanked crypto-bigint 0.7.6 moved to 0.7.11.

  ring leaves the VTA and VTC graphs; it stays only under attest-verify.

  removed from 19 crates; deliberate ones are listed under
  [package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored. A tier-0 "manifest hygiene" CI job
  runs cargo-machete and the lint check.

  once in [workspace.dependencies]; vta-tee inherits aws-lc-rs. The five
  crypto crates carry real minimum-patch floors, enforced by
  check-workspace-version-reqs.py.

  (check-workspace-lints.py); unsafe_code = "forbid" workspace-wide, with
  the four crates that need unsafe restating the table at "deny" and
  rewritten safely. The two missing publish = false comments are added.



### Changed

- **vta**: Decouple vta-cli-common, split key/room modules, extract vta-test-support, share reject helpers and service plumbing ([#2730](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2730))

* refactor(vta): put vta-cli-common and dialoguer behind cli-synthesis ([#2566](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2566))

  Only the `vta` binary's offline CLI modules and setup wizard use them,
  and the binary already requires `cli-synthesis`. The library — and so
  vta-enclave — no longer compiles vtc-client, ratatui, qrcode, dialoguer
  or crossterm: `cargo tree -p vta-enclave -e normal` drops from 981 to
  ~935 unique lines.

  The vti-rooms comment claimed `default-features = false` kept the host
  half out of the build; feature unification through vti-rooms-dtg (which
  verifies through `vti_rooms::authz`) turns `host` back on. Say so,
  and why it costs nothing new.

- **rooms**: Share the rooms/* handlers between hosts and run every host receive path on Spine ([#2731](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2731))

* refactor(room-host): receive every document through vti_trust_task_server::Spine

  room-host re-implemented the receive pipeline inline: size, freshness,
  validate_basic and the accepted-id claim/settle, with no spec-policy step
  and the proof verified lazily inside each handler. It now runs the shared
  Spine the VTC runs ([#2576](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2576)): the size gate holds each task to its declared
  maxDocumentBytes, the spec policy comes from
  vti_specs::schema_index::spec_policy_for, the proof is verified once over
  the document as received and bound to its issuer, DIDComm and TSP frames
  carry their authenticated sender so the spine binds it (VTI-OPS-021/093),
  and the duplicate-id record is StoreAcceptedIds (VTI-OPS-025..029).

  A host without a DID still refuses an expired document: the spine skips
  the recipient binding then, so before_proof applies the expiry check.
  A proof made by someone other than the issuer is now proofInvalid, as at
  the VTC, rather than permissionDenied.



### Performance

- **vta**: Cache compiled schemas and policies, verify once, bound sweeps and list pages ([#2713](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2713))

* perf(vta-sdk,vta-service): compile each Trust Task payload schema once ([#2622](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2622))

  trust-tasks-rs 0.37's against_schema / validate_value parse and compile the
  schema on every call. vta_sdk::schema_cache keeps the compiled validator by
  the &'static schema text's address (the same technique as trust-tasks-rs
  0.38's SchemaValidator), with the jsonschema release trust-tasks-rs 0.37 uses
  so the check and its error text are unchanged. The dispatch spine, the SDK's
  send-side check, room act, notifications, rooms, task consent, vetting and
  the VTA's per-handler payload checks use it.

  trust-tasks-rs 0.38 moves in lockstep with affinidi-tdk and the messaging
  SDK, so the bump is left to that train; this module then wraps
  SchemaValidator.

body:
### Build & CI

- Harden CI and the build: pinned toolchain, image digests, release-token checks, advisories, fuzzing, tooling lint ([#2709](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2709))

* build: pin the Rust toolchain to 1.95.0 and pass clippy 1.95 ([#2658](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2658))

  rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.95.0, the workspace rust-version and the Dockerfiles' Rust image. CI jobs install it with scripts/install-rust-toolchain.sh instead of a floating stable, so a new Rust release's lints can no longer turn main red with no code change; Dependabot proposes the next one as a PR. scripts/check-toolchain-pins.sh keeps the pin at or above the MSRV and the Dockerfiles in line.

  Clippy 1.95 is stricter than the stable CI ran in nonminimal_bool and collapsible_match: De Morgan rewrites at eleven call sites (behaviour unchanged), Option::take().map in vta-persona, and one allow on vti_voting::audit::check_order, where a match guard would fall through to later arms.

### Performance

- **rooms**: Indexed record reads, per-room locks, commits outside the host lock, per-election ballot boxes ([#2712](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2712))

* perf(vti-common): per-bundle chunk lock and a progress bitmap apart from the plan

  A chunked transfer's lock is striped by bundle id, so one bundle's finalize
  (a whole-file hash) no longer stalls every other transfer ([#2596](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2596)). Progress

  a chunk no longer re-reads and rewrites a plan of up to 4,096 digests ([#2597](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2597)).
  A bundle opened before the bitmap row existed keeps the progress its plan
  recorded; get_plan still returns the plan with its progress.

### Changed

- **rooms**: Share the rooms/* handlers between hosts and run every host receive path on Spine ([#2731](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2731))

* refactor(room-host): receive every document through vti_trust_task_server::Spine

  room-host re-implemented the receive pipeline inline: size, freshness,
  validate_basic and the accepted-id claim/settle, with no spec-policy step
  and the proof verified lazily inside each handler. It now runs the shared
  Spine the VTC runs ([#2576](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2576)): the size gate holds each task to its declared
  maxDocumentBytes, the spec policy comes from
  vti_specs::schema_index::spec_policy_for, the proof is verified once over
  the document as received and bound to its issuer, DIDComm and TSP frames
  carry their authenticated sender so the spine binds it (VTI-OPS-021/093),
  and the duplicate-id record is StoreAcceptedIds (VTI-OPS-025..029).

  the recipient binding then, so before_proof applies the expiry check.
  A proof made by someone other than the issuer is now proofInvalid, as at
  the VTC, rather than permissionDenied.

- **rooms**: Indexed record reads, per-room locks, commits outside the host lock, per-election ballot boxes ([#2712](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2712))

* perf(vti-common): per-bundle chunk lock and a progress bitmap apart from the plan

  A chunked transfer's lock is striped by bundle id, so one bundle's finalize
  (a whole-file hash) no longer stalls every other transfer ([#2596](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2596)). Progress
  is a bitmap row beside the immutable plan, read from a per-process cache, so
  a chunk no longer re-reads and rewrites a plan of up to 4,096 digests ([#2597](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2597)).

  recorded; get_plan still returns the plan with its progress.

  the invitation (which create 0.2 says withdraws the authority it confers) or
  letting it lapse left an unexpiring community administrator nobody claimed.

  The entry is now written to expire with the invitation and recorded beside it
  (install::InviteGrant, keyed by jti). vtc/install/claim/finish/0.3 makes it
  permanent once the DID has proved itself with the token and claim code;
  vtc/admin/invites/revoke/0.1, and the void after five wrong claim codes,

  same provisional entry.

  create 0.2 item 3 and claim/finish 0.3 item 7, so the entry is still written
  at mint.

(check-workspace-lints.py); unsafe_code = "forbid" workspace-wide, with the four crates that need unsafe restating the table at "deny" and rewritten safely. The two missing publish = false comments are added. ### Changed - **vtc**: One typed routing table for every Trust Task family; routes/ is the HTTP surface only ([#2732](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2732)) * refactor(vtc): route every Trust Task family through one typed AsyncDispatcher #2728 split trust_tasks/mod.rs into handler files but left three routing styles: about sixty direct arms in `dispatch_typed`, thirty-three family modules each keeping a `URIS` list beside a `match` that re-matched it (one `FAMILIES` table arm), and typed `AsyncDispatcher` registration for rooms and git-ns. A hand-kept `DISPATCHED_URIS` (540 lines) had to agree with all of it, and already did not: `auth/step-up/requests/show/0.1` was routed but not listed, so discovery never advertised it. - `trust_tasks::routing`: one `AsyncDispatcher` every family registers on, keyed on the generated payload type (`on!(routes, P => handler)`). The URI a handler answers is `P::TYPE_URI`; the served set is the table itself (`routing::served_uris`), and `dispatched_uris()` (that plus discovery) replaces `DISPATCHED_URIS` for the unsupported-version hint, discovery, the size gate and the censuses. - Each family exposes `register(Routes) -> Routes`; every `URIS` constant, every family `dispatch` and the `FAMILIES` table are gone, and the direct arms moved into their handler files' `register`. Families whose verbs share an authority check before the payload is read (backup, website, the administrator's passkeys) route through a small `Op` enum, not a URI match. - Handlers are registered on `Received

`: routed and policed as `P`, but handed the JSON as received, so every handler still reads it against the schema before parsing it and still resolves the signer's authority before reading the payload (a typed downcast in the router would reverse that order and change which refusal a stranger gets). - Censuses: no URI is registered twice (the dispatcher would silently keep the later one), and none is also a rooms or git-ns task. - The URI constants nothing but the removed lists named are deleted; the ones only tests name stay behind `#[cfg(test)]`. Behaviour is unchanged except that discovery and the version hint now list `auth/step-up/requests/show/0.1`, which was always served. - **vta**: Decouple vta-cli-common, split key/room modules, extract vta-test-support, share reject helpers and service plumbing ([#2730](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2730)) * refactor(vta): put vta-cli-common and dialoguer behind cli-synthesis ([#2566](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2566)) Only the `vta` binary's offline CLI modules and setup wizard use them, and the binary already requires `cli-synthesis`. The library — and so vta-enclave — no longer compiles vtc-client, ratatui, qrcode, dialoguer or crossterm: `cargo tree -p vta-enclave -e normal` drops from 981 to ~935 unique lines. The vti-rooms comment claimed `default-features = false` kept the host half out of the build; feature unification through vti-rooms-dtg (which verifies through `vti_rooms::authz`) turns `host` back on. Say so, and why it costs nothing new. - **vtc**: Vtc-audit leaf crate, one regorus engine, typed error codes, trust_tasks split, AdminActor ([#2728](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2728)) * refactor(vti-common)!: move the VTC's audit-event vocabulary to a new vtc-audit leaf crate ### Documentation - Operator guides, CLI remediation strings and the crate map match the tree, checked in CI ([#2706](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2706)) * fix(cli): operator-facing remediation strings name commands that parse Every error, hint and --help string that tells an operator what to run now names a command the current pnm / vta / cnm accepts ([#2631](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2631)): the retired `pnm webvh …` / `vta webvh …` surface becomes `did-mgmt servers|dids …`, `pnm auth login` (pnm has none) becomes `pnm setup`, `pnm acl delete` takes the DID positionally, `list-domains` sits under `dids`, the backup descriptor hints no longer name `pnm backup save|restore`, and stale doc comments (`pnm passkey-enroll-token`, `vta export-mnemonic`, `cnm community info`) are corrected. A pnm and a vta test parse each remediation command through Cli::try_parse_from. title: style: rustfmt for Rust 1.100
body:
Rust 1.100 (2026-11-09) ships a rustfmt that indents the closing line of `/*! … */` block comments. CI installs the latest stable, so the Format job has failed on `main` since cd7551e and on every PR (e.g. #597).

Formatting only: `cargo fmt --all` on 1.100.0. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean on 1.100.0, with and without `--no-default-features`.

Needs backporting so `release/0.7` PRs (including the #597 backport) pass Format.

title: chore(deps): Bump jsonschema from 0.60.2 to 0.61.1
body:
Bumps [jsonschema](https://github.com/Stranger6667/jsonschema) from 0.60.2 to 0.61.1.
Release notes

Sourced from jsonschema's releases.

[Python] Release 0.61.1

Fixed

  • dereference following $ref in keywords that hold data, such as const and examples. #1858
  • pattern over one character class under a large bounded count, such as ^.{0,404600}$, failing with a regex engine error on the empty string when the size limit was raised to compile it.

Performance

  • pattern and patternProperties with a large bounded count over one character class, such as ^.{0,262144}$ or [^\p{C}]{1,2048}, build without unrolling the count and fit the default size limit.
  • pattern and patternProperties match anchored character-class patterns such as ^[a-z0-9-]+$ without a regex engine.

[Ruby] Release 0.61.1

Fixed

  • dereference following $ref in keywords that hold data, such as const and examples. #1858
  • pattern over one character class under a large bounded count, such as ^.{0,404600}$, failing with a regex engine error on the empty string when the size limit was raised to compile it.

Performance

  • pattern and patternProperties with a large bounded count over one character class, such as ^.{0,262144}$ or [^\p{C}]{1,2048}, build without unrolling the count and fit the default size limit.
  • pattern and patternProperties match anchored character-class patterns such as ^[a-z0-9-]+$ without a regex engine.

[Rust] Release 0.61.1

Added

  • PatternCache and ValidationOptions::with_pattern_cache to compile each regex once across validator builds.

Fixed

  • dereference following $ref in keywords that hold data, such as const and examples. #1858
  • pattern over one character class under a large bounded count, such as ^.{0,404600}$, failing with a regex engine error on the empty string when the size limit was raised to compile it.

Performance

  • pattern and patternProperties with a large bounded count over one character class, such as ^.{0,262144}$ or [^\p{C}]{1,2048}, build without unrolling the count and fit the default size limit.
  • pattern and patternProperties match anchored character-class patterns such as ^[a-z0-9-]+$ without a regex engine.

[Python] Release 0.61.0

Fixed

  • . in pattern and patternProperties matched \r, U+2028 and U+2029 (it should reject every line terminator).
  • evaluate() reported a missing single required name beside additionalProperties: false at /additionalProperties (it should be /required).
  • Numeric keywords misjudging whole floats past 2^53. #1825
  • Building a validator with an explicit draft retrieving the schema's $schema URI.
  • format: "date-time", "date" and "time" accepting +, ,, -, . or / where RFC 3339 requires a digit. #1829
  • Numeric keywords misjudging instances against whole floats past 2^53 in the schema. #1825
  • $ref pointers through a numeric object key (#/responses/200) skipping the references under their target.
  • oneOf / anyOf rejecting valid instances when a $ref inside a branch sits under an $id.
  • unevaluatedItems treated every element as evaluated beside a non-schema items value (it should evaluate none).

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from jsonschema's changelog.

[0.61.1] - 2026-11-10

Added

  • PatternCache and ValidationOptions::with_pattern_cache to compile each regex once across validator builds.

Fixed

  • dereference following $ref in keywords that hold data, such as const and examples. #1858
  • pattern over one character class under a large bounded count, such as ^.{0,404600}$, failing with a regex engine error on the empty string when the size limit was raised to compile it.

Performance

  • pattern and patternProperties with a large bounded count over one character class, such as ^.{0,262144}$ or [^\p{C}]{1,2048}, build without unrolling the count and fit the default size limit.
  • pattern and patternProperties match anchored character-class patterns such as ^[a-z0-9-]+$ without a regex engine.

[0.61.0] - 2026-11-08

Added

Sourced from serde-saphyr's releases.

2.1.1 Optimization and maintenance release

Fixed

  • Fixed 2.1.0 regression empty documents producing errors (#265). Empty document is a valid YAML document. Fix of this regression is the reason of making this release so early.

Performance improvements

  • Significantly reduced allocations when deserializing (#262), thanks @​mat-gas

2.1.0 Minor feature extension, maintenance and performance release

Added

  • Added opt-in Options::reject_tagged_field_names to catch misplaced tags on struct field names, with Error::TaggedStructFieldName diagnostics. Struct field names can only be strings; !!str is still accepted. As other tags can only be ignored, tag on a structure field name is almost for sure placed wrongly. This setting will be default in next major release.
  • Added Options::leading_zero_numbers_as_strings and Options::underscored_numbers_as_strings to preserve numeric spellings such as 0755 and 1_000 as strings in untyped values, including untagged enums and flattened fields (#225).   • Added Error::render_to to append diagnostics to any std::fmt::Write using RenderOptions, without collecting the complete output in an intermediate string (#221).
  • Added DuplicateKeyPolicy::PassThrough to delegate repeated explicit mapping entries to Serde visitors, matching serde_yaml's handling for structs, standard maps, and custom multimap visitors (#226). title: chore(vtc-admin-ui): move lucide-react and lucide-static to 1.70.0 together
body:
Supersedes #2734 (lucide-static 0.469.0 → 1.70.0) and #2736 (lucide-react 0.469.0 → 1.70.0), which each failed alone.

## Why the two must move together

The badge picture builder (`admin-ui/src/components/badge-icons.ts`) joins lucide-react's `icons` to lucide-static's `tags.json` by name, so search can find an icon by what it means ("insect" finds the bug). That only works if both packages come from the same release: 0.469.0 has 1,544 icons and 1.70.0 has 2,029, so bumping either one alone fails `BadgeBuilder.test.tsx` ("expected 1544 to be 2029").

## What changed

- **`chore(vtc-admin-ui)`**: `lucide-react` and `lucide-static` both go to **1.70.0** and are pinned exactly. `lucide-react` used to be `^0.469.0`, and a caret let it move ahead of its tag file on any `npm install`. With 1.70.0, the 2,029 icons and 2,029 tag entries name the same icons, with nothing missing on either side. The builder test now compares the two catalogues' key sets rather than only their sizes. `docs/03-vtc/badges.md` now says "about 2,000" icons instead of 1,500, and the comment in `badge-icons.ts` gives the coupling rule.
- **`ci(dependabot)`**: adds a `lucide` group (`lucide-*`) to the `/vtc-service/admin-ui` npm entry, listed before `minor-and-patch`. lucide bumps of every kind, majors included, now arrive as one PR.

## lucide 1.x and stored badges

lucide 1.0 removed the brand icons and renamed some others. `tsc -b` shows the console imports none of the removed ones. **Stored badges are not affected:** nothing persists an icon name. The builder draws the chosen icon onto a canvas and uploads only the resulting PNG through `vtc/badges/images/upload`, where the community re-encodes it (VTI-BDG-050). Badges hold an image digest, and no lucide name appears in any record, wire type or Rust code. A renamed or removed icon only changes what can be chosen next. No alias map is needed.

## Checks run

- admin-ui (after `npm ci`): `npm run lint` (`wire:check` + typecheck), `npx vitest run` (131 files, 1614 tests), `npm run build`, `npm run build:members`
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3754 passed, 1 skipped

body:
Updates the requirements on [rand_chacha](https://github.com/rust-random/rand) to permit the latest version.
Release notes

Sourced from rand_chacha's releases.

0.9.0

Upgrade guide

See https://rust-random.github.io/book/update-0.9.html

Changelog

Security and unsafe

  • Policy: "rand is not a crypto library" (#1514)
  • Remove fork-protection from ReseedingRng and ThreadRng. Instead, it is recommended to call ThreadRng::reseed on fork. (#1379)
  • Use zerocopy to replace some unsafe code (#1349, #1393, #1446, #1502)

Dependencies

  • Bump the MSRV to 1.63.0 (#1207, #1246, #1269, #1341, #1416, #1536); note that 1.60.0 may work for dependents when using --ignore-rust-version
  • Update to rand_core v0.9.0 (#1558)

Features

  • Support std feature without getrandom or rand_chacha (#1354)
  • Enable feature small_rng by default (#1455)
  • Remove implicit feature rand_chacha; use std_rng instead. (#1473)
  • Rename feature serde1 to serde (#1477)
  • Rename feature getrandom to os_rng (#1537)
  • Add feature thread_rng (#1547)

API changes: rand_core traits

  • Add fn RngCore::read_adapter implementing std::io::Read (#1267)
  • Add trait CryptoBlockRng: BlockRngCore; make trait CryptoRng: RngCore (#1273)
  • Add traits TryRngCore, TryCryptoRng (#1424, #1499)
  • Rename fn SeedableRng::from_rng -> try_from_rng and add infallible variant fn from_rng (#1424)
  • Rename fn SeedableRng::from_entropy -> from_os_rng and add fallible variant fn try_from_os_rng (#1424)
  • Add bounds Clone and AsRef to associated type SeedableRng::Seed (#1491)

API changes: Rng trait and top-level fns

  • Rename fn rand::thread_rng() to rand::rng() and remove from the prelude (#1506)
  • Remove fn rand::random() from the prelude (#1506)
  • Add top-level fns random_iter, random_range, random_bool, random_ratio, fill (#1488)
  • Re-introduce fn Rng::gen_iter as random_iter (#1305, #1500)
  • Rename fn Rng::gen to random to avoid conflict with the new gen keyword in Rust 2024 (#1438)
  • Rename fns Rng::gen_range to random_range, gen_bool to random_bool, gen_ratio to random_ratio (#1505)
  • Annotate panicking methods with #[track_caller] (#1442, #1447)

API changes: RNGs

  • Fix <SmallRng as SeedableRng>::Seed size to 256 bits (#1455)
  • Remove first parameter (rng) of ReseedingRng::new (#1533)

API changes: Sequences

  • Split trait SliceRandom into IndexedRandom, IndexedMutRandom, SliceRandom (#1382)
  • Add IndexedRandom::choose_multiple_array, index::sample_array (#1453, #1469)

API changes: Distributions: renames

  • Rename distribution Standard to StandardUniform (#1526)

feat(go-specs): release the generated specification packages as their own module (#1315)

Step 3 of #1112. Core v0.13.0, the first without specs/, is on the proxy, so
trust-tasks-go/specs now requires it and builds. The module is released on its
own trust-tasks-go/specs/vX.Y.Z tags, starting at v0.1.0. Importers of a
prebuilt package add it beside the core; import paths do not change.

- specs/go.mod requires core v0.13.0 (TODO removed); go mod tidy adds go.sum.
- Release wiring as for proof: specs/version.go (const Version = "0.1.0"), an
  empty CHANGELOG.md, a verify-go/publish-go matrix leg, a GO_MODULES entry, and
  a release-bump-go.sh arm watching trust-tasks-go/specs, specs/ and
  scripts/build-go-bindings.mjs (scopes go-specs, go-bindings). go-specs is
  added to commit-lint's `!` scopes. The core watch keeps excluding the module
  and keeps watching specs/ for its extends index.
- go.yml gets a `specs` job (build, vet, gofmt, test -race on 1.22 and stable,
  with the changed-paths early exit). specs leaves NOT_BUILT_YET.
- The smoke test moves to specs/smoke/smoke_test.go and runs in the module
  against the published core. The core's smoke driver now copies it from there
  and still runs it against the checkout's runtime.
- build-go-bindings keeps version.go, CHANGELOG.md and smoke/ as well as
  go.mod/go.sum, and refuses to generate a package onto any of them.
- dependabot watches the module; README, docs/packages/go.md (interim section
  replaced), RELEASING.md and the website library summary are updated.

Closes #1112.

title: ci(dependabot): hold webauthn-rs 0.6 in /fuzz and TypeScript majors in the admin UI
body:
Dependabot opened three PRs that can never pass:

- #2721 / #2722 bump webauthn-rs / webauthn-rs-proto to 0.6 in `/fuzz` only. The harness builds from the root `Cargo.lock`, where 0.6 is deliberately held (it refuses Ed25519 passkeys — see the root cargo entry), so `lockfile resolves`, `cargo-deny` and both Docker builds fail. The `/fuzz` entry now carries the same `webauthn-rs*` `>= 0.6` ignore.
- #2719 bumps TypeScript 5.9 → 7.0 in the admin UI. `npm ci` fails ERESOLVE: openapi-typescript 7.13 declares a TypeScript 5 peer. Semver-major TypeScript updates are now ignored; move it deliberately together with openapi-typescript.

Those three PRs are closed with a pointer here.

body:
The first weekly Dependabot PRs from #1182 (#1184 npm, #1185 pub, #1186 cargo) all failed. Each group had one or two updates that break something, and they made the whole group fail. This PR changes `.github/dependabot.yml` so that grouped minor and patch updates normally pass, and so that anything needing a deliberate change arrives on its own or not at all.

## What broke, by update

I read the failing job logs and then reproduced each cause locally on the PR heads, holding back the update I suspected and rerunning the check.

| PR | Update | Kind | Failing checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| #1186 | `schemars` 0.8 → 1.2 (+ `typify` 0.6 → 0.8, which requires it) | major, API break | build, codegen drift, consumer generation, gen-ts equivalence, gen ≡ build-go-bindings, rs API compatibility, cargo test (cli), example application. Each fails at `cannot find type RootSchema in schemars::schema` (`trust-tasks-build/src/generate.rs:163`) |
| #1186 | the other 31 updates (syn 3, prettyplease 0.3, sha2 0.11, serde-saphyr 2, jsonwebtoken 11, affinidi-*, …) | — | none. With schemars/typify held back: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features` and `cargo test --workspace` pass, `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen` + `cargo fmt` leaves no diff, `npm run build-bundles` + `check-bundles` pass |
| #1184 | `json-schema-to-typescript` 15 → 16 | major, changes generated output | build-ts-bindings drift and trust-tasks-gen-ts equivalence: both generators reject the output (`counter-suffixed duplicates: DecryptionTarget1, EncryptedCast1, …`) |
| #1184 | `prettier` 3.8.3 → 3.9.10 (direct in trust-tasks-ts-gen, transitive in the root lockfile) | minor, changes generated output | with json-schema-to-typescript held at 15, prettier 3.9 alone reflows union types in 8 generated modules (drift) and the equivalence check reports 8 files that are not byte-identical. Pinning 3.8.3 back gives no drift |
| #1184 | `typescript` 5.9/6.0 → 7.0 | major, API break | trust-tasks-ts-proof, -tsp, -capability-client: `Cannot find name 'TextEncoder'` / `'crypto'`. Their tsconfigs set `lib: ["ES2022"]` and no `types`, and TS 7 no longer loads `@types/node` by default. TS 5.9 with @types/node 26 compiles cleanly |
| #1184 | `@openvtc/vti-tsp-js` 0.2 → 0.4 | 0.x "minor", API break | trust-tasks-ts-tsp: `'senderEncryptionKey' does not exist in type 'UnpackKeys'/'PackKeys'`. With vti-tsp-js at 0.2.0, those errors go away |
| #1185 | `lints` 4/5 → 6.1 | major, new lint | trust-tasks-dart-tsp (3.8, stable): `dart analyze --fatal-infos` reports 4 `use_null_aware_elements` infos in `test/support/fixtures.dart` |

The other two expected kinds of cause did not appear. No Dart SDK floor changed: Dependabot widened the `lints` range and left every `sdk:` constraint as it was. No failure was infrastructure flakiness: every failure is deterministic and reproduced locally.

## Changes

- **Every group (`github-actions`, `cargo`, `npm`, `gomod`, `pub`) takes only `update-types: ["minor", "patch"]`.** Majors come as their own PRs. TypeScript 7 (needs `"types": ["node"]` in three tsconfigs) and lints 6 (four lines in one test fixture) are deliberately **not** ignored. Each will arrive as its own PR and needs a small fix-up commit.
- **`ignore`, each with a comment giving the reason**, only where the logs show a deliberate migration is needed:
  - `schemars` majors and `typify` minors+majors. They move together, and `trust-tasks-build`/`trust-tasks-codegen` build on `schemars::schema::RootSchema`.
  - `json-schema-to-typescript` majors. 16 makes both TS generators emit duplicate names.
  - `@openvtc/vti-tsp-js` minors+majors. It is 0.x, and 0.4 removes `senderEncryptionKey`.

  Dependabot classes a 0.x step (0.2 → 0.4) as "minor", so grouping by `update-types` cannot keep a breaking 0.x update out of the group. That is why the two 0.x entries also ignore minors.
- **A new `ts-generator` npm group** (`json-schema-to-typescript`, `prettier`) sits ahead of `npm`, so generator updates no longer share a PR with the rest.

## Generator updates still need a regeneration commit

The ts-generator group handles a patch or minor bump of a generator dependency that changes the generated output, as prettier 3.9 does. It does not ignore it. A PR from that group will fail `build-ts-bindings drift` / `trust-tasks-gen-ts equivalence` until someone:

1. moves the root lockfile's `prettier` (a transitive dependency of json-schema-to-typescript) to the version `trust-tasks-ts-gen` pins. The equivalence check compares output from the two generators, so they must format identically.
2. runs `npm run build-ts-bindings` and commits `trust-tasks-ts/src` and `trust-tasks-ts/component-names.lock.json`.

The same applies on the Rust side if a minor/patch of typify's or prettyplease's dependencies ever changes output: run `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all` and commit the result. None of the current cargo updates do that.

No version or CHANGELOG changes. Validated with `check-jsonschema --builtin-schema vendor.dependabot` and `actionlint`.

title: ci: weekly dependency updates for every ecosystem, and a scheduled advisory check
body:
Adds dependency updates for every ecosystem in the repository and a weekly advisory check, and clears advisory ignores in `deny.toml` that no longer match anything.

## Dependabot

`.github/dependabot.yml` (added in #1160 for `github-actions`) is extended. There is one grouped PR per ecosystem per week:

| Ecosystem | Directories | Title |
|---|---|---|
| github-actions | `/` | `ci:` (unchanged) |
| cargo | `/` (the workspace) | `chore(deps):` |
| npm | `/`, `trust-tasks-ts`, `-proof`, `-tsp`, `-capability-client`, `-gen`, `examples/consumer-app-ts` | `chore(deps):` |
| gomod | `trust-tasks-go` and its `proof`, `didcomm`, `capabilityclient`, `tsp` modules, `examples/consumer-app-go` | `chore(deps):` |
| pub | the six `trust-tasks-dart*` packages, `examples/consumer-app-dart` | `chore(deps):` |

`chore(deps)` passes commit-lint, and `cliff.toml` keeps it out of the changelogs. A note in the file covers two cases. An update inside a package directory still gives that package a patch release. An update that raises a Go module's `go` floor fails CI on purpose.

## Advisories workflow

`.github/workflows/advisories.yml` runs weekly (Monday 04:23 UTC) and on dispatch. It has read-only permissions and does not persist credentials.

- **cargo**: `cargo deny check advisories --all-features`, through the `EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action` pin rust.yml already uses. This adds a schedule to the per-PR `cargo deny` job. No new action.
- **npm**: `npm audit`, which reads the lockfile and installs nothing, run in each of the seven lockfile directories. For the five published packages, `npm audit --omit=dev` fails on any advisory in what consumers install. In every directory, `npm audit --audit-level=high` fails on high or critical anywhere in the tree.

Go and Dart get no advisory scan here. `govulncheck` is not used in this repository yet, and adding it is a separate decision. For now they are covered by the Dependabot updates above.

## deny.toml

All eight advisory ignores were stale. `cargo deny check advisories` (cargo-deny 0.19.8) reported each one as `advisory-not-detected`. None of the crates they covered is in `Cargo.lock`: `proc-macro-error`, `rustls-pemfile`, `smallstr`, `clear_on_drop`, `bitmaps`, `im` and `sized-chunks` are absent, and `h2` is only at 0.4.16. The list is now `ignore = []`, and the new `unused-ignored-advisory = "deny"` setting fails the check when a future ignore stops matching. Without that setting, a stale ignore would stay green if its crate came back. The header comment no longer describes a `notice` downgrade the file does not make.

## Behaviour changes

- New weekly Dependabot PRs for cargo, npm, gomod and pub.
- `cargo deny` now fails on an ignore entry that matches nothing.
- The new `Advisories` workflow is scheduled, not a PR check. Its first run will report what `npm audit` reports today:
  - root tooling: `fast-uri` (high, via the build tooling), which fails the run;
  - `trust-tasks-ts` dev tree: `minimatch` (moderate, via `@microsoft/api-extractor`), which is below the high threshold and only logged.

  The published packages' runtime trees are clean.

## Checks

- `cargo deny check advisories` on `main` before the change: `advisories ok`, with eight `advisory-not-detected` warnings. After: `advisories ok`. Full `cargo deny check`: `advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`, exit 0.
- `unused-ignored-advisory = "deny"` tested by putting one stale ignore back: `error[advisory-not-detected]`, `advisories FAILED`, exit 1.
- `npm audit` run locally in all seven directories, with the results above.
- `actionlint` 1.7.12 on `advisories.yml`: clean. `dependabot.yml` parses.

## Checklist (development guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no client code; both jobs have `timeout-minutes`
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — n/a
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — no wire types
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — an empty ignore list plus `unused-ignored-advisory = "deny"`
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — the scheduled job fails rather than warns on an advisory that blocks
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — no mutations; the workflow is read-only
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none

title: fix(messaging/mux/ack): notPermitted only for a member whose mail the connection reads (0.1)
body:
Follow-up to #1174 and #1176. `messaging/mux/ack` 0.1 (draft) no longer lets a principal confirm mail it was never shown.

**The problem:** after #1176, rule 3 answers `notPermitted` for any message held for a member the connection carries without `delete`. A member may be carried with only `send` (or another scope that never shows its mail). An id is a hash of the message, so a principal that knows one (it sent the message, say) could ask for it and learn from `notPermitted` vs `notFound` whether that member still holds it.

**Change:**
- **Rule 3:** `notPermitted` only for a member carried with `receive` or `pickup`, whose mail the connection already sees. A member carried with neither is answered `notFound`, the same as a DID the connection does not carry.
- **Security & Privacy → Data carried:** names the sent-message case.
- **`AckRefusal.reason` description** updated to match. Same enum, no schema change beyond the description.

Bindings regenerated (doc comments only). `npm run validate`, `check-bindings` and `check-published-schemas` pass. The reference mediator implements this in a follow-up to affinidi/affinidi-messaging-mediator#231.

title: feat(messaging/mux/ack): acknowledge frames on the mux connection they were delivered on (0.1)
body:
Adds **`messaging/mux/ack` 0.1 (draft)**: a principal acknowledges frames delivered on its mux connection, on that connection, and the mediator deletes each one the principal, or the member it was for, may delete.

**Why:** a raw-TSP `tsp-mux` socket is delete-to-ack, and until now a client acked out of band (a REST delete). Only the connection knows which members it carries and with what scope, so on a clustered mediator a delete landing on an instance that doesn't hold the connection was refused for every member's frame, and those frames were redelivered for ever. Acking on the socket gets the same answer on every instance.

**The task:**
- **Request:** `messageIds`, 1–100 lowercase hex SHA-256 ids (the stored message's hash, as `tsp-ack` and message-pickup deletes already name it).
- **Authority:** a frame the principal owns is deleted as its owner. A member's frame is deleted only while that member is on this connection with the `delete` scope.
- **Response:** `acked`, plus `refused` entries `{ messageId, reason }` with reason `notFound` or `notPermitted`. A refused message is left as it was.
- **Error:** `messaging/mux:notMuxConnection`.
- Declared `mutating`, not `destructive`: only the mediator's copy of frames the principal has already taken goes, and acking again changes nothing.
- Because acking is idempotent, the mediator **MAY** answer on the connection without storing the response, so acks of acks don't pile up.

**`messaging/mux/event` 0.1 (draft):** "Raw-TSP sockets" rule 5 now says a client acknowledges on the socket with `messaging/mux/ack`. `ack` is added to `related`. No schema change.

Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart). `npm run validate`, `npm run build`, `check-published-schemas` (nothing released changed) and `check-bindings` pass.

The reference mediator (affinidi/affinidi-messaging-mediator) and the Rust SDK client (affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs) will implement it next.
